definition_zh: 源头；来源；出处；（消息）来源；货源；v. 从某处取得
definition_en: the place or thing from which something begins, comes, or is obtained; also to obtain something from a particular place
core_image: 泉眼：水从地底向上涌出的那一点，下游的一切都从它开始
scene: 地理课上，老师把手指按在地图上一整条大河最上游的泉眼。She said that the spring was the source of the whole river, and that every branch below it started from this high ground.
sceneCN: 这里 source 是「源头」（第 1 个义项：河流发源的泉眼）；句意：她说那处泉眼就是整条河的源头，下游每一条支流都从这片高地出发。图中可辨识物件：地图、泉眼、高地上游、河流。

pos.zh: 源头；来源；出处；（消息）人士；货源
从某处取得、采购；（报道）注明出处

derivatives.zh: 足智多谋的；善用资源的

senses.title: Springhead: where a river begins
senses.definition: the point where a river or stream begins, especially a spring rising from the ground
senses.definitionCN: 河流或溪流的起点，尤指从地下涌出的泉眼
senses.example: For centuries the source of the Nile was a geographical mystery.
senses.exampleCN: 几个世纪以来，尼罗河的源头一直是地理之谜。
senses.why: Source comes from Old French sourse 'spring, fountainhead', from sourdre 'to rise, spring forth'. The first image is water coming up out of the ground at one identifiable point.
senses.whyCN: source 来自古法语 sourse“泉、泉源”，再来自 sourdre“涌出、涌起”。最初的画面是水从地下在某个可指认的点涌出。

senses.title: Origin: the cause a thing grows from
senses.titleCN: 根源：事物由此生长出来的起因
senses.definition: the cause, beginning, or origin of something abstract, such as a problem or a feeling
senses.definitionCN: 抽象事物的起因、开端或根源，如问题、情绪等
senses.example: The source of the dispute was a disputed stretch of border.
senses.exampleCN: 争端的根源是一段有争议的边界。
senses.why: The spring is no longer water but a cause: whatever comes later flows from that first point. The image is unchanged — one point upstream, everything else downstream.
senses.whyCN: 泉眼不再是水，而是一个原因：后来的一切都从那第一个点流出。意象没有变——上游一个点，其余全在下游。

senses.title: Informant: the person information comes from
senses.titleCN: 消息来源：信息由谁提供
senses.definition: a person, organization, or document that provides information, especially to a journalist
senses.definitionCN: 提供信息的人、机构或文件，尤指给记者的消息来源
senses.example: The reporter refused to name her source.
senses.exampleCN: 记者拒绝透露她的消息来源姓名。
senses.why: Information is treated as water: it rises from a person and flows into the report. A source is the point of emergence, which is why it can be protected or anonymous.
senses.whyCN: 信息被当作水：从某个人那里涌出，流进报道里。source 就是涌出的那个点，因此它可以被保护，也可以匿名。

senses.title: Documentary origin: the material a claim rests on
senses.titleCN: 文献出处：一个说法所依据的原始材料
senses.definition: an original text, record, or authority that a statement or study is based on
senses.definitionCN: 某个说法或研究所依据的原始文本、记录或权威依据
senses.example: Good history is built on primary sources, not on later summaries.
senses.exampleCN: 好的历史研究建立在第一手资料上，而不是后人的概述。
senses.why: A document is a fixed spring: whoever cites it can point back to the same point of emergence. Primary source keeps the 'original' force, secondary source is water that has already travelled.
senses.whyCN: 文献是一口固定的泉：引用者都能指回同一个涌出点。primary source 保留“最初”的力度，secondary source 则是已经流了一段的水。

senses.title: Supply origin: where goods or materials come from
senses.titleCN: 货源产地：商品或原料的来处
senses.definition: the place, country, or supplier that goods, materials, or workers come from
senses.definitionCN: 商品、原料或人员所来自的地方、国家或供应商
senses.example: The country is a major source of coffee for European roasters.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家是欧洲烘焙商的主要咖啡货源。
senses.why: Goods also 'rise' from a place of origin. The spring becomes a farm, a mine, or a factory, and source names the upstream end of a supply chain.
senses.whyCN: 货物同样从产地“涌出”。泉眼变成了农场、矿山或工厂，source 指供应链的上游端点。

senses.title: Energy source: where power is drawn from
senses.titleCN: 能源：能量被取用的来处
senses.definition: a natural resource such as wind, sun, or coal from which energy is obtained
senses.definitionCN: 风、太阳、煤等可从中获取能量的自然资源
senses.example: Wind and sunlight are renewable sources of power.
senses.exampleCN: 风与阳光是可再生的能源。
senses.why: This is the supply sense narrowed to energy: the sun, wind, or coal seam is the upstream point, and electricity is what flows downstream into use.
senses.whyCN: 这是“货源”义收窄到能量：太阳、风或煤层是上游点，电流则是流向下游、进入使用的那部分。

senses.title: Computing: the file a program is built from
senses.titleCN: 计算机：程序由之构建的源文件
senses.definition: the original code or data from which a program or document is generated
senses.definitionCN: 用来生成程序或文档的原始代码或数据
senses.example: The source code is open, so anyone can study it.
senses.exampleCN: 源代码是公开的，因此任何人都可以研读。
senses.why: A program is compiled downstream from source code, just as a river runs downstream from its spring. What you edit is the origin; what runs is the result.
senses.whyCN: 程序是从源代码向下游编译出来的，就像河流从泉眼向下游流去。你编辑的是源头，运行的是结果。

senses.title: Verb: obtain goods from a particular place
senses.titleCN: 动词：从特定地点采购、取得
senses.definition: to obtain parts, materials, or products from a specified place or supplier
senses.definitionCN: 从指定的地方或供应商处取得零件、原料或产品
senses.example: The company sources its parts from three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司从三个国家采购零件。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an action: you trace a thing back to its spring and bring it from there. The object is always obtained at a named upstream point.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：你把某物追溯到它的泉眼，再从那里取来。宾语总是在一个被点名的上游点被取得。

senses.title: Verb: attribute a statement to its origin
senses.titleCN: 动词：把说法归到它的出处
senses.definition: to state where a piece of information or a quotation came from
senses.definitionCN: 说明某条信息或引语来自何处
senses.example: Every claim in the article is sourced to a named expert.
senses.exampleCN: 文章中的每个说法都注明了具名专家的出处。
senses.why: Attribution is the same tracing motion performed on words: the statement is followed back to the mouth it rose from, and the source is written down.
senses.whyCN: 溯源就是对语言做同一个追溯动作：把一个说法跟回到它涌出的那张嘴，并把出处写下来。

intro.en: Source is a water word before it is an information word. It reached English through Old French from Latin surgere 'to rise', and the oldest image is a spring rising out of the ground.
intro.cn: source 先是水之词，后才是信息之词。它经古法语进入英语，源头是拉丁语 surgere“上升”；最古老的意象是从地下涌出的泉。

items.en: First recorded in English as a noun meaning 'a spring, fountainhead' and, very soon after, 'origin, cause'. The supply and information senses are much later extensions.
items.cn: 最早于 14 世纪晚期作为名词记录，意为“泉、泉源”，紧接着出现“起源、原因”义；货源与消息来源义都是后来的延伸。

items.en: From Old French sourse 'spring, fountainhead', a feminine noun from sourdre 'to rise, spring forth'. Modern French keeps the form source.
items.cn: 来自古法语 sourse“泉、泉源”，是 sourdre“涌出、涌起”派生的阴性名词；现代法语保留 source 这一形式。

items.en: Old French sourdre goes back to Latin surgere 'to rise, spring up', analysed as sub- 'from below' + regere 'to lead straight, guide'. The same verb underlies surge, insurgent, resource and resurrect.
items.cn: 古法语 sourdre 上溯拉丁语 surgere“上升、涌起”，可分析为 sub-“从下”+ regere“引导、使直”。同一个动词也是 surge、insurgent、resource、resurrect 的来源。

items.en: The root behind regere is PIE *reg- 'to move in a straight line, rule', the source of rule, right, region and direct. The link is generally accepted but reconstructed, not directly attested.
items.cn: regere 背后的词根是原始印欧语 *reg-“沿直线移动、统治”，也是 rule、right、region、direct 的来源。这一联系属一般认为，属重构而非直接实证。

items.en: The noun extends from water to causes, people, documents, goods, energy and code; the verb 'to obtain from a source' is a 20th-century business usage. The core 'point of emergence' never disappears.
items.cn: 名词从水延伸到原因、人、文献、货物、能源与代码；“从某处取得”的动词用法是 20 世纪商业用语。核心的“涌出点”始终没有消失。

note.en: The first group checks spelling, sound and root; the second separates words that also name a beginning, a cause, or a documented origin.
note.cn: 第一组看拼写、读音与词根；第二组区分同样表示“开端、原因、有据来源”的词。

entries.definition: something available to be used; literally a 'rising again', from re- + source. It is a stock you draw on, not the point where a thing begins.
entries.definitionCN: 可动用的东西；字面义“再次涌起”，由 re- + source 构成。它是可供取用的储备，而不是事物开始的点。

entries.definition: a sudden strong upward or forward movement. It comes from the same Latin surgere 'to rise' but has no 'origin' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的向上或向前涌动。它同样来自拉丁语 surgere“上升”，但没有“源头”义。

entries.definition: a liquid served with food. In British English it sounds the same as source, but it comes from Latin salsa 'salted things', not surgere.
entries.definitionCN: 佐餐的酱汁。英式英语中与 source 同音，但它来自拉丁语 salsa“盐腌之物”，与 surgere 无关。

entries.definition: the point at which something begins. It is more abstract and neutral than source and carries no supply or information sense.
entries.definitionCN: 事物开始的那一点。它比 source 更抽象、更中性，也没有货源或消息来源义。

entries.definition: the hidden cause that supports everything else. It is more forceful and figurative than source, as in the root of the problem.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑一切的隐藏原因。它比 source 更有力度、更偏比喻，如 the root of the problem。

entries.definition: the original source of something. It is literary and keeps the water image openly, unlike everyday source.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物最初的源头。它是文学用语，公开保留水的意象，不像日常的 source 那样中性。

entries.definition: the documented history of where an object came from. It is used for art, antiques and specimens, not for people or claims.
entries.definitionCN: 一件物品来源的可查历史。它用于艺术品、古董与标本，不用于人或说法。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: the Latin verb 'to rise', real water images, and real compounds such as resource and source code.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：拉丁语“上升”动词、真实的水之意象，以及 resource、source code 等真实组合。

normal.en: Old French sourse was simply 'a spring'. The English word still carries water rising out of the ground at one point.
normal.cn: 古法语 sourse 就是“泉”。英语这个词至今仍带着“水从地下某一点涌出”的画面。

normal.en: surgere = sub- 'from below' + regere 'guide straight': water guiding itself upward. Surge, insurgent and resource are the same verb.
normal.cn: surgere = sub-“从下”+ regere“引直”：水自己向上引。surge、insurgent、resource 都出自同一个动词。

normal.en: A news source is a person who lets information rise to the surface; protecting a source is protecting the spring.
normal.cn: 消息来源就是让信息浮出水面的人；保护 source 就是保护那口泉。

normal.en: Source code is the file a program rises from; the compiled program is downstream.
normal.cn: 源代码是程序由之涌出的文件；编译后的程序在下游。

normal.en: To source parts is to trace each part back to the place it rises from and buy it there.
normal.cn: 采购零件（source parts）就是把每个零件追溯到它涌出的地方，并在那里买下。

abstract.en: A spring is a point, not a store: all the water downstream is the same water, but only the first point is the source.
abstract.cn: 泉是一个“点”，不是一座“库”：下游所有的水都是同一股水，但只有最初那一点才叫 source。

abstract.en: Any process can be followed upstream to a single dot; source is that dot, whether it is a lake, a person or a line of code.
abstract.cn: 任何过程都能逆流追到一个点；source 就是那个点，无论它是湖泊、一个人，还是一行代码。

abstract.en: A claim with no source is water with no spring: it may look clean, but no one can check where it came from.
abstract.cn: 没有出处的说法就像没有泉的水：看起来也许清澈，却没人能查它从哪来。

examples.en: The source of the river is a small lake high in the mountains.
examples.cn: 这条河的源头是高山上的一个小湖。

examples.en: The article gives no source for its central claim.
examples.cn: 这篇文章没有为它的核心说法注明出处。

examples.en: The firm sources its coffee beans from small farms in Ethiopia.
examples.cn: 这家公司从埃塞俄比亚的小农场采购咖啡豆。

dict_mnemonic.text: “索思”——索思顺着河一路往上索，思到水源那一点 → source 源头、来源

root: 古法语 sourse“泉源”，来自 sourdre“涌出”，再上溯拉丁语 surgere“上升”（sub-“自下”+ regere“引导、使直”），核心是“从底下涌出的那一点”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of source, all one point of emergence: a spring, a cause, a speaker, a document, a supplier, an energy, a code file, and the act of tracing any of them back.
sensesIntro.cn: source 的九个义项都是同一个“涌出点”：泉眼、起因、发言人、文献、供应商、能源、代码文件，以及把其中任何一个追溯回去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water rises from one identifiable point, and everything else flows downstream from it.
core.cn: 核心意象：水从一个可指认的点涌出，其余一切都由它流向下游。

branches.en: WATER: the literal springhead, still the shape of every other sense.
branches.cn: 水：字面的泉源，仍是其余所有义项的形状。

branches.en: CAUSE: a spring becomes the reason later events flow from.
branches.cn: 原因：泉变成后来事件所流出的理由。

branches.en: INFORMATION: a person or a document is the point where a claim rises.
branches.cn: 信息：人或文献就是一个说法涌出的那一点。

branches.en: SUPPLY: farms, mines and power stations are springs of goods and energy.
branches.cn: 供给：农场、矿山与电站是货物与能量的泉。

branches.en: TECHNICAL AND VERBAL: code is a source file, and to source is to buy at the spring or to write the spring down.
branches.cn: 技术与动词：代码是源文件；to source 是在泉眼处采购，或把泉眼写下来。

intro.en: Source has no live English prefix. Its Latin parts are frozen inside surgere; English adds only ordinary suffixes such as -ing and compounds such as sourcebook.
intro.cn: source 没有活的英语前缀，它的拉丁成分凝固在 surgere 里；英语只添加 -ing 这类普通后缀，或构成 sourcebook 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on surgere 'to rise': surge, insurgent, resource and resurrect all describe something rising, again or against something.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族围绕 surgere“上升”：surge、insurgent、resource、resurrect 都描述某物涌起、再起或反抗而起。

items.meaning: a supply that can be drawn on; literally 'a rising again'
items.meaningCN: 可供取用的资源；字面义“再次涌起”
items.example: The region's water resources are under pressure.
items.exampleCN: 该地区的水资源正承受压力。

items.meaning: good at finding ways to deal with problems
items.meaningCN: 足智多谋的；善于想办法的
items.example: A resourceful teacher turns a broken projector into a lesson.
items.exampleCN: 一位足智多谋的老师能把坏掉的投影仪变成一堂课。

items.meaning: the activity of obtaining goods or materials from suppliers
items.meaningCN: 采购；货源组织（-ing 构成行为名词）
items.example: Ethical sourcing means checking how goods are produced.
items.exampleCN: 道德采购意味着核查商品是如何生产的。

items.meaning: a collection of original documents for study or reference
items.example: The course uses a sourcebook of medieval letters.
items.exampleCN: 这门课使用一本中世纪书信的资料集。

items.example: The verb is the spring behind source and surge.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 source 与 surge 背后的“涌起”。

items.example: The stem appears in surge, insurgent and resurrect.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 surge、insurgent 与 resurrect。

items.structure: Old French verb from Latin surgere
items.example: Old French sourse came from this verb.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 sourse 就来自这个动词。

items.meaning: to obtain work from an outside supplier
items.example: The firm outsourced its payroll last year.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司去年把工资发放外包了。

items.meaning: with source code free to use and modify
items.example: She teaches with open-source tools.
items.exampleCN: 她用开源工具教学。

latinEntries.meaning: a sudden upward or forward movement
latinEntries.meaningCN: 激增；涌动（突然向上或向前）

latinEntries.meaning: one who rises up against an established authority
latinEntries.meaningCN: 起义者；叛乱者（起来反抗当权者的人）

latinEntries.meaning: means available for use; literally a rising again
latinEntries.meaningCN: 资源；字面义“再次涌起”

latinEntries.structure: re- (again) + surrectus, past participle of surgere
latinEntries.meaning: to bring back to life or bring into use again
latinEntries.meaningCN: 使复活；使重新启用

definition_zh: 具体的；特定的；特有的；明确的；（specifics）细节；特效药
definition_en: clearly identified and not general; belonging to one particular kind or thing; also the details of a matter, or a remedy for one disease
core_image: 从一整块材料里切出带标签的一小块：只此一块，不是整类
scene: 质检员在零件堆里举起一个带编号的样品。The inspector held up the numbered sample and asked the supplier to deliver this specific size, not something roughly like it.
sceneCN: 这里 specific 是「特定的、具体的」（第 2 个义项：某一个而非任意一个）；句意：质检员举起带编号的样品，要求供应商按这个特定尺寸交货，不接受笼统的“差不多”。图中可辨识物件：带编号样品、卡尺、零件堆、检验台。

pos.zh: 具体的；特定的；特有的；明确的
（specifics）具体细节；（a specific）特效药

senses.title: Concrete rather than general
senses.definition: described by an actual instance or detail rather than by a broad category
senses.definitionCN: 用实际事例或细节来描述，而不是用宽泛的类别
senses.example: Can you give a specific example of what went wrong?
senses.exampleCN: 你能举一个出问题的具体例子吗？
senses.why: Latin specificus meant 'making a particular kind', from species 'kind' + facere 'to make'. The first move is to cut one member out of a general class and show it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 specificus 意为“使成某一种类”，来自 species“种类”+ facere“做”。第一个动作就是从大类中切出一个成员并把它拿出来看。

senses.title: A particular one, not just any
senses.titleCN: 特定的某一个，而非任意一个
senses.definition: fixed or named as one particular person, thing, time, or place
senses.definitionCN: 被固定或点名为某一个特定的人、物、时间或地点
senses.example: The drug targets a specific enzyme in the liver.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药作用于肝脏里的一种特定酶。
senses.why: Once a kind has been cut out, it can be pointed at: this one, not any one. The adjective now separates one item from all others of its kind.
senses.whyCN: 一旦切出一个种类，它就可以被指认：是这一个，而不是任意一个。此时形容词把一个项目从同类中分离出来。

senses.title: Explicit and detailed
senses.definition: stated clearly and in detail, so that there is little room for misunderstanding
senses.definitionCN: 清楚而详细地说明，几乎没有误解空间
senses.example: The manual gives specific instructions for each step.
senses.exampleCN: 手册为每一步给出了明确具体的指示。
senses.why: A detail that is 'made into a kind' is pinned down. Precision is the natural result of pointing at one item instead of waving at a class.
senses.whyCN: 被“做成一个种类”的细节是被钉住的。精确性正是指向一个项目、而不是朝一整类挥手的自然结果。

senses.title: Peculiar to one kind
senses.definition: existing only in, or characteristic of, one particular group, species, or thing
senses.definitionCN: 只存在于某一群体、物种或事物中，或为其特征
senses.example: This nesting behaviour is specific to the island's finches.
senses.exampleCN: 这种筑巢行为是该岛雀类所特有的。
senses.why: Species is the root, so the adjective can say that a trait belongs to one species and no other. The 'kind' is now a boundary rather than a sample.
senses.whyCN: species 就是词根，因此这个形容词可以表示某特征只属于一个物种而不属于其他。这里的“种类”成了边界，而不是样本。

senses.title: Technical: measured per unit or against a standard
senses.titleCN: 专业用法：按单位量或按标准物计量
senses.definition: in physics, relating a quantity to a unit amount of a particular substance, as in specific heat and specific gravity
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中，把某个量联系到特定物质的单位量，如比热与比重
senses.example: Water has a specific heat of about 4.18 kilojoules per kilogram per degree.
senses.exampleCN: 水的比热约为每千克每摄氏度 4.18 千焦。
senses.why: The 'particular kind' sense narrows to a particular substance: the quantity is stated for one material rather than for matter in general.
senses.whyCN: “特定种类”义收窄到特定物质：这个量是说某一种材料的，而不是笼统说物质的。

senses.title: Noun: the specifics of a matter
senses.definition: the exact details of a plan, arrangement, or proposal, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 计划、安排或提案的确切细节，通常用复数
senses.example: The two sides agreed in principle but are still arguing over the specifics.
senses.exampleCN: 双方原则上同意，但仍在具体细节上争执。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for the cut-out items themselves. Once a plan is divided into particulars, those particulars are the specifics.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化为名词，指被切出来的那些条目本身。一旦计划被分成若干细项，这些细项就是 specifics。

senses.title: Noun: a remedy for one disease
senses.titleCN: 名词：针对一种病的特效药
senses.definition: a medicine or remedy that is effective against one particular disease
senses.definitionCN: 对某一种特定疾病有效的药物或疗法
senses.example: Quinine was long regarded as a specific for malaria.
senses.exampleCN: 奎宁曾长期被视为疟疾的特效药。
senses.why: A remedy that works on one disease and not on others is literally 'specific' — cut to a single kind. The noun is old medical usage and now sounds dated.
senses.whyCN: 只对一种病有效、对别的病无效的药，字面上就是“特定的”——被切到单一一种。这个名词是较旧的医学用法，如今显得过时。

senses.title: Usage boundary: specific versus special
senses.definition: specific means identifiable or precise; special means exceptional or set apart, and the two are not interchangeable
senses.definitionCN: specific 指可指认的、精确的；special 指特别的、被单独对待的，二者不能互换
senses.example: A specific price is a precise figure; a special price is a discount for you.
senses.exampleCN: a specific price 是一个精确数字；a special price 是给你的优惠价。
senses.why: Special comes from specialis 'belonging to a kind' and stops there. Specific adds the facere 'make' element, so it says 'made into this kind', which is why only specific means precise or particular.
senses.whyCN: special 来自 specialis“属于某一种类的”，到此为止。specific 多出 facere“做”的成分，表示“被做成这一种类”，因此只有 specific 能表示“精确的、特定的”。

intro.en: Specific is a 'kind-making' word: species supplies the kind and facere supplies the making. Its cousin special shares species but lacks the making, which is the root of the modern difference.
intro.cn: specific 是一个“造种类”的词：species 提供“种类”，facere 提供“做”。它的表亲 special 也共享 species，却没有“做”的成分，这正是现代区别的词源根源。

items.en: First recorded in English as an adjective meaning 'pertaining to a species or kind'. The senses 'distinctive, particular' and 'precise, definite' develop later in the 16c.
items.cn: 16 世纪 10 年代最早作为形容词记录，意为“属于某一种类的”；“独特的、特定的”与“精确的、明确的”义在 16 世纪稍后发展出来。

items.en: From Late Latin specificus 'making a particular kind, constituting a species', built as species + -ficus 'making', from facere 'to make, do'.
items.cn: 来自晚期拉丁语 specificus“使成某一种类、构成一个物种”，由 species + -ficus“造成”构成，后者来自 facere“做、为”。

items.en: Latin species meant 'a look, appearance, form, kind', from specere 'to look at, observe'. It is the same word that gives biological species and the plural species.
items.cn: 拉丁语 species 意为“外观、样子、形式、种类”，来自 specere“看、观察”。生物学 species 与单复数同形的 species 都出自这个词。

items.en: Specere is traced to PIE *spek- 'to observe', also behind spectrum, specimen, inspect and spy. The reconstruction is generally accepted, though the intermediate forms are not directly attested.
items.cn: specere 被追溯到原始印欧语 *spek-“观察”，也是 spectrum、specimen、inspect、spy 的词根。该重构属一般认为，中间形式并无直接实证。

items.en: Special comes from Latin specialis 'belonging to a kind', also from species, but it has no -ficus element. Special therefore means 'set apart, exceptional', while specific means 'made into this kind', hence 'particular, precise'. They are cousins, not synonyms.
items.cn: special 来自拉丁语 specialis“属于某一种类的”，同样出自 species，但没有 -ficus 成分。因此 special 表示“被单独对待的、特别的”，specific 表示“被做成这一种类的”，故有“特定的、精确的”义。二者是表亲，不是同义词。

items.en: The phrase specific to dates from the 19c. Physics fixed specific heat and specific gravity, medicine used the noun for a one-disease remedy, and business English turned specifics into 'the details'.
items.cn: 短语 specific to 见于 19 世纪。物理学固定了 specific heat 与 specific gravity；医学用该名词指针对单一疾病的药；商业英语把 specifics 变成“具体细节”。

note.en: The first group shares the species root or the -spec- shape; the second separates precision, particularity, tangibility and certainty.
note.cn: 第一组共享 species 词根或 -spec- 词形；第二组区分精确、特定、具体可感与确定。

entries.definition: exceptional, or intended for one purpose. From specialis 'belonging to a kind' without the 'making' element, so it never means 'precise'.
entries.definitionCN: 特别的，或专为某一用途的。来自 specialis“属于某一种类”，没有“做”的成分，因此从不表示“精确的”。

entries.definition: the verb: to name or state something exactly. It is the action that specific describes.
entries.definitionCN: 动词：确切点名或说明某事。它就是 specific 所描述的那个动作。

entries.definition: a biological kind. Latin species 'appearance, kind' is the noun on which specific was built.
entries.definitionCN: 生物物种。拉丁语 species“外观、种类”正是构成 specific 的那个名词。

entries.definition: a single item singled out from others. It stresses selection, while specific stresses that the item is identifiable and non-general.
entries.definitionCN: 从其他项目中单挑出来的一个。它强调“挑选”，而 specific 强调该项目可指认、不笼统。

entries.definition: exact in every detail. It focuses on accuracy of measurement or wording; specific focuses on being definite rather than general.
entries.definitionCN: 每个细节都精确。它侧重测量或措辞的准确，specific 则侧重“明确而非笼统”。

entries.definition: real and tangible, opposed to abstract. Specific is opposed to general, so a concrete example and a specific example are close but not identical.
entries.definitionCN: 真实可感的，与抽象相对。specific 与笼统相对，因此 a concrete example 与 a specific example 接近但不相同。

entries.definition: clear and certain, with no ambiguity. It stresses that a decision or answer is fixed, not that it is detailed.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚确定的，没有歧义。它强调决定或答案已经定下，而不是强调详细。

normalIntro.en: Real word parts: species 'kind' + facere 'make'. The word literally 'makes a kind', which separates it from its cousin special.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：species“种类”+ facere“做”。这个词字面上就是“造出一个种类”，这也把它和表亲 special 分开。

normal.en: species + -fic (make) = 'make a kind': specific carves one member out of a genus and puts a label on it.
normal.cn: species + -fic（做）=“造一个种类”：specific 从一个大类里切出一个成员，并贴上标签。

normal.en: special is the cousin without facere: it only says 'of a kind', not 'made into this kind', so a special offer is not a specific offer.
normal.cn: special 是没有 facere 的表亲：它只说“属于某类”，不说“被做成这一类”，所以 special offer 不是 specific offer。

normal.en: The everyday phrase 'specific to' marks a trait that belongs to one species and no other.
normal.cn: 日常短语 specific to 标记一个只属于某物种、不属于其他的特征。

normal.en: Specific heat asks how much heat one particular substance needs, which is why the word appears in physics.
normal.cn: specific heat 问的是某一种特定物质需要多少热量，这正是这个词出现在物理里的原因。

normal.en: The specifics of a contract are its numbered details: a general deal cut into separate kinds.
normal.cn: 合同的 specifics 就是它逐条编号的细节：一笔笼统的交易被切成一个个具体的种类。

abstract.en: A wide spotlight beam is general; narrow it until one object alone is lit and the circle is specific.
abstract.cn: 宽泛的聚光灯是笼统的；把它收窄到只照亮一个物体，那个圆就是 specific。

abstract.en: A stencil with one shape cut out lets only that shape through. Specific is the stencil: it makes one kind and excludes the rest.
abstract.cn: 一块只镂出一个形状的模板，只让那个形状通过。specific 就是这块模板：造出一个种类，排除其余。

abstract.en: A barcode unique to one product: scan it and the whole class collapses into a single identifiable item.
abstract.cn: 一个只属于某件商品的条形码：一扫，整个类别就收缩成一个可指认的单项。

examples.en: The report makes a specific claim about the cause of the fire.
examples.cn: 这份报告对火灾原因提出了一个具体说法。

examples.en: Some diseases are specific to particular regions.
examples.cn: 有些疾病是某些地区特有的。

examples.en: Before signing, read the specifics of the agreement.
examples.cn: 签字之前，先读一读协议的具体条款。

dict_mnemonic.text: “斯佩西菲克”——斯佩西菲克把长长的清单缩到只剩一行，只指那一个 → specific 具体的、特定的

root: 晚期拉丁语 specificus“使成某一种类”= species“外观、种类”+ -ficus（facere“做”），核心是“从大类中造出、标出某一个”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of specific, all one act of cutting a kind out of a class: a concrete instance, a named item, a precise order, a peculiar trait, a per-unit quantity, the details themselves, a single-disease remedy, and the boundary with special.
sensesIntro.cn: specific 的八个义项都是同一个“从大类中切出种类”的动作：具体实例、被点名的一项、精确指令、特有特征、按单位计的量、细节本身、单病特效药，以及与 special 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one member is cut out of a whole class and labelled 'this one'.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一个整类中切出一个成员，贴上“就是这一个”的标签。

branches.en: INSTANCE: the cut-out member shown as a concrete example.
branches.cn: 实例：被切出的成员作为具体例子展示。

branches.en: IDENTIFICATION: the label is used to point at one particular item.
branches.cn: 指认：标签被用来指向某一个特定项目。

branches.en: PRECISION: pointing at one item produces explicit, detailed instructions.
branches.cn: 精确：指向单项，自然产生明确而详细的指示。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: the kind becomes a species boundary, then a single substance measured per unit.
branches.cn: 边界：种类变成物种边界，再变成按单位量计的单一物质。

branches.en: NOUNS AND LIMITS: the cut-out items are specifics, a one-disease drug is a specific, and special marks the cousin without facere.
branches.cn: 名词与边界：切出的条目是 specifics，单病药物是 a specific，而 special 是没有 facere 的表亲。

intro.en: Specific is a Latin adjective ending in -fic, from facere 'make'. English adds -ally, -ity and the negative prefix non- to the finished word; the root itself is not a live English prefix.
intro.cn: specific 是以 -fic 结尾的拉丁形容词，来自 facere“做”。英语在成品词上加 -ally、-ity 和否定前缀 non-；词根本身不是活的英语前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on specere 'to look': species is a visible kind, a specimen is something shown, and a spectrum is an image seen.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族围绕 specere“看”：species 是看得见的种类，specimen 是被展示之物，spectrum 是被看见的像。

items.meaning: in a precise or particular way; for a particular purpose
items.meaningCN: 具体地；明确地；特意地（-ally 构成副词）
items.example: The course is designed specifically for beginners.
items.exampleCN: 这门课是专为初学者设计的。

items.meaning: the quality of being specific, precise, or limited to one kind
items.meaningCN: 特异性；明确性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: Antibody specificity determines which invader is recognised.
items.exampleCN: 抗体的特异性决定它能识别哪种入侵者。

items.meaning: not clearly tied to one cause, kind, or disease
items.meaningCN: 非特异性的；不明确的（non- 表示否定）
items.example: Fever is a nonspecific sign that can have many causes.
items.exampleCN: 发烧是一个非特异性体征，可能有很多原因。

items.meaning: found only in, or acting only on, one species
items.meaningCN: 物种特有的；仅作用于某一物种的
items.example: The virus is species-specific and does not infect humans.
items.exampleCN: 这种病毒具有物种特异性，不会感染人类。

items.example: The noun gives specific its idea of a kind.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词给 specific 提供“种类”的概念。

items.example: Seeing is the oldest layer of the spec- family.
items.exampleCN: “看”是这个词族最古老的一层。

items.example: The stem appears in species, specimen and spectrum.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 species、specimen 与 spectrum。

items.example: It marks specific as making a kind.
items.exampleCN: 它把 specific 标为“造成某一种类”。

items.example: Please specify the size you need.
items.exampleCN: 请明确说明你需要的尺寸。

latinEntries.meaning: a kind or class; in biology, a group that can interbreed
latinEntries.meaningCN: 种类；生物学中的物种

latinEntries.meaning: to look at, observe
latinEntries.meaningCN: 看；观察

latinEntries.meaning: a sample shown for study or testing
latinEntries.meaningCN: 标本；样本

latinEntries.meaning: a range of light or values; literally something seen
latinEntries.meaningCN: 光谱；范围（字面义“被看见之物”）

definition_zh: 明确说明；具体指出；指定；规定
definition_en: to state something exactly and in detail, to name a particular item, or to lay something down as a requirement
core_image: 在清单上逐行写下名称、数量与条件，一行都不留空
scene: 工程评审会上，客户在需求表上逐项落笔。The client used the form to specify every size, material and delivery date, down to the tolerance.
sceneCN: 这里 specify 是「逐项规定、明确说明」（第 1 个义项：把细节说清楚）；句意：客户用那张表逐项规定尺寸、材料和交付日期，连公差都写清楚。图中可辨识物件：需求表、尺寸标注、材料样品、交付日历。

pos.zh: 明确说明；具体指出；指定；规定

derivatives.zh: 规格；规格说明；具体规定
可明确说明的；可指定的
说明者；指定者；（语言学）限定语

senses.title: State exactly: leave nothing vague
senses.definition: to say or write something exactly, with enough detail that it cannot be misunderstood
senses.definitionCN: 把某事说得或写得十分确切，细节足以避免误解
senses.example: Please specify how many copies you need.
senses.exampleCN: 请明确说明你需要多少份。
senses.why: Specify comes from specificare 'to mention particularly', built on specificus 'making a kind'. To specify is to perform that making: a vague need is turned into a named, countable thing.
senses.whyCN: specify 来自 specificare“特别指出”，后者建立在 specificus“使成某一种类”之上。specify 就是执行这个“造种类”的动作：把模糊的需求变成一个被命名、可计数的东西。

senses.title: Name item by item
senses.definition: to list or name each item, member, or element separately rather than as a group
senses.definitionCN: 把每个项目、成员或要素分别列出或点名，而不是笼统归为一组
senses.example: The schedule specifies every stop along the route.
senses.exampleCN: 日程表逐项列出了路线上的每一站。
senses.why: The -fic element is 'make', so the verb does not merely mention a group; it produces separate named entries. This is the 'item by item' force that separates specify from special.
senses.whyCN: -fic 的成分是“做”，因此这个动词不只是提到一个整体，而是造出一个个有名字的条目。这正是把 specify 与 special 区分开的“逐项”力度。

senses.title: Designate: pick the exact one
senses.titleCN: 指定：挑出确切的那一个
senses.definition: to name a particular person, place, time, or thing for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某一目的点名特定的人、地点、时间或事物
senses.example: The notice specifies 9 a.m. as the starting time.
senses.exampleCN: 通知指定上午九点为开始时间。
senses.why: Once each item has a name, one of them can be chosen. The verb moves from describing a list to selecting the entry that will be used.
senses.whyCN: 一旦每一项都有了名字，就可以从中选出一个。动词从“描述清单”转到“选出将被使用的那一条”。

senses.title: Stipulate: write it into an agreement
senses.definition: to state a condition or requirement formally, especially in a contract or rule
senses.definitionCN: 正式规定某项条件或要求，尤指在合同或规则中
senses.example: The contract specifies a penalty for late delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 合同规定了延迟交货的罚金。
senses.why: A specified item is one that has been made into a fixed entry. Writing it into a contract gives that entry legal force, so 'state exactly' becomes 'stipulate'.
senses.whyCN: 被 specify 的条目是被做成固定条目之物。把它写进合同，就赋予该条目法律效力，于是“精确说明”变成“规定”。

senses.title: Technical: set out specs and parameters
senses.definition: to state the required dimensions, materials, performance, or settings of a product or system
senses.definitionCN: 说明产品或系统所要求的尺寸、材料、性能或设置
senses.example: The brief specifies a battery life of at least twelve hours.
senses.exampleCN: 需求书规定电池续航至少十二小时。
senses.why: Engineering carries the contract sense into design: each parameter is a named entry that the finished object must match. The noun specification is simply the list produced.
senses.whyCN: 工程把合同义带进设计：每个参数都是一个被点名的条目，成品必须与之相符。名词 specification 就是这份被造出来的清单。

senses.title: Rules and conditions: define who or what qualifies
senses.titleCN: 规则与条件：界定谁符合、什么成立
senses.definition: to fix the conditions under which something applies, is allowed, or must happen
senses.definitionCN: 确定某事物在何种条件下适用、被允许或必须发生
senses.example: The rules specify who may vote in the election.
senses.exampleCN: 规则界定了谁可以在选举中投票。
senses.why: A condition is a boundary drawn around a class. Specifying it is cutting the class down to those entries that meet the named test.
senses.whyCN: 条件就是围绕一个类别画出的边界。specify 一个条件，就是把该类收窄到符合这条具名检验的那些条目。

senses.title: Formula: 'unless otherwise specified'
senses.titleCN: 固定说法：除非另有规定
senses.definition: in the phrase unless otherwise specified, used to set a default that applies until another entry is named
senses.definitionCN: 用于 unless otherwise specified，表示设定一个默认值，直到另有条目被点名
senses.example: All prices include tax unless otherwise specified.
senses.exampleCN: 除非另有说明，所有价格均含税。
senses.why: The past participle specified points back to a list already made. The formula says: the default holds until someone specifies a different entry.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词 specified 指向一份已经造好的清单。这个固定说法意为：默认值一直有效，直到有人 specify 了另一个条目。

senses.title: Usage boundary: specify versus mention or suggest
senses.definition: specify requires exact identification; mention only refers to something, and suggest only offers it as a possibility
senses.definitionCN: specify 要求确切指认；mention 只是提到某事物，suggest 只是把它作为可能性提出
senses.example: She mentioned a hotel, but she did not specify which one.
senses.exampleCN: 她提到了一家酒店，但没有说明是哪一家。
senses.why: Mention and suggest leave the item unnamed, so the 'making a kind' work has not been done. Specify is the verb that completes it, which is why the pair contrasts so sharply.
senses.whyCN: mention 与 suggest 都让项目停留在未命名状态，也就是“造种类”的工作还没完成。specify 正是完成它的动词，因此对比格外鲜明。

intro.en: Specify is the verb form of the specific family: French spécifier and Medieval Latin specificare 'to mention particularly', both built on specificus. Its special cousin shares species but never gained the 'making' element.
intro.cn: specify 是 specific 词族的动词形式：法语 spécifier 与中世纪拉丁语 specificare“特别指出”，都建立在 specificus 上。它的表亲 special 共享 species，却从未获得“制造”的成分。

items.en: First recorded in English, meaning 'to mention or name a particular thing'. The modern sense 'to state exactly' is well established by the 16c.
items.cn: 最早于 14 世纪中期记录于英语，意为“提到或点名称某事物”；现代“精确说明”义在 16 世纪已确立。

items.en: From Old French specifier (Modern French spécifier) 'to specify, detail', the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: 来自古法语 specifier（现代法语 spécifier）“具体说明、逐项列出”，是英语动词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French goes back to Medieval Latin specificare 'to mention particularly, designate', a verb formed on specificus 'making a kind'.
items.cn: 古法语上溯中世纪拉丁语 specificare“特别指出、指定”，这是由 specificus“使成某一种类”构成的动词。

items.en: Specificus = species 'appearance, kind' + -ficus, from facere 'to make'. So specify literally means 'to make a kind': each item is named until the class is replaced by separate made entries.
items.cn: specificus = species“外观、种类”+ -ficus，后者来自 facere“做”。因此 specify 字面上是“造一个种类”：逐一点名，直到整类被一条条造出的条目取代。

items.en: Special, from specialis 'belonging to a kind', has no facere element, so it cannot mean 'name item by item'. Specify keeps the making, which is why it always implies exact, enumerated detail.
items.cn: special 来自 specialis“属于某一种类”，没有 facere 成分，因此不能表示“逐项点名”。specify 保留“做”的成分，因此总含“精确、逐条”的意思。

items.en: The noun specification 'detailed statement' appears in the 17c. and becomes the everyday word for technical requirements. The passive as specified and the formula unless otherwise specified are modern contract and manual usage.
items.cn: 名词 specification“详细说明”见于 17 世纪，后来成为技术要求的日常词。被动式 as specified 与固定说法 unless otherwise specified 属现代合同与手册用语。

note.en: The first group shares the species/spec- root or the -ify shape; the second separates saying, stipulating, designating and defining.
note.cn: 第一组共享 species／spec- 词根或 -ify 词形；第二组区分“说出、规定、指定、界定”。

entries.definition: the adjective: exact, particular, or peculiar to one kind. Specify is the act; specific is the result.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：精确的、特定的、某一类特有的。specify 是动作，specific 是结果。

entries.definition: exceptional or set apart. It shares species but lacks the 'making' element, so it does not mean 'state exactly'.
entries.definitionCN: 特别的、被单独对待的。它共享 species，却缺少“做”的成分，因此不表示“精确说明”。

entries.definition: to make speeches, often in a tiresome way. It has the same -ify ending but comes from speech, not species.
entries.definitionCN: 发表演说，常含贬义。它有同样的 -ify 结尾，但来自 speech，而非 species。

entries.definition: to say or write something formally and clearly. It does not require the item-by-item detail that specify does.
entries.definitionCN: 正式而清楚地说出或写出。它不要求 specify 那样的逐项细节。

entries.definition: to make a condition a formal part of an agreement. It is narrower and more legal than specify.
entries.definitionCN: 把某项条件正式写入协议。它比 specify 更窄，也更法律化。

entries.definition: to officially name or assign someone or something. It focuses on the appointment, not on the details that specify provides.
entries.definitionCN: 正式命名或指派某人某物。它侧重“任命”，而不是 specify 所提供的细节。

entries.definition: to state the exact meaning or limits of something. It draws the boundary, while specify fills the boundary with named items.
entries.definitionCN: 说明某事物的确切含义或界限。它画出边界，而 specify 用一个个具名条目填满边界。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: specific + -ify, where -ify goes back to facere 'make'. Specify is literally 'make specific', and its cousin special never had that making.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：specific + -ify，而 -ify 上溯 facere“做”。specify 字面上就是“使具体化”，它的表亲 special 从来没有这个“做”。

normal.en: specificare is the verb built on specificus 'making a kind': to specify is to do that making, naming each item until it exists as a separate entry.
normal.cn: specificare 是由 specificus“使成某一种类”构成的动词：specify 就是执行这个“造”，逐项命名，直到它作为独立条目存在。

normal.en: -ify is from facere 'make', so specify = make specific. A vague wish becomes a made thing once you specify it.
normal.cn: -ify 来自 facere“做”，所以 specify = 使具体。模糊的愿望一旦被你 specify，就成了被造出来的东西。

normal.en: In a contract, 'as specified' points to the schedule: the schedule is the kind that has been made.
normal.cn: 合同里的 as specified 指向附件清单：那份清单就是被“造”出来的种类。

normal.en: 'Unless otherwise specified' means the default holds until someone names a different entry.
normal.cn: unless otherwise specified 意为：默认值一直有效，直到有人点名另一个条目。

normal.en: special has no facere, so you can specify details but you cannot 'special' them.
normal.cn: special 没有 facere，所以你可以 specify 细节，却不能“special”它们。

abstract.en: A form full of blank lines: specify is filling every blank with a value so that nothing is left open.
abstract.cn: 一张满是空行的表格：specify 就是把每个空都填上值，不留下任何未定项。

abstract.en: A stencil cuts one shape out of a sheet. Specifying is cutting the class down until only one named shape can pass.
abstract.cn: 模板从一张纸上镂出一个形状。specifying 就是把整个类别切到只剩一个具名形状能通过。

abstract.en: A spoken agreement becomes a signed schedule of numbered clauses: specify is the act that pins each word to an item.
abstract.cn: 口头协议变成一份签字的分条清单：specify 就是把每个词钉到一个条目上的那个动作。

examples.en: The form asks you to specify your arrival date and flight number.
examples.cn: 表格要求你明确填写到达日期和航班号。

examples.en: The law specifies how much notice an employer must give.
examples.cn: 法律规定了雇主必须提前多久通知。

examples.en: Unless the order specifies otherwise, we ship by standard mail.
examples.cn: 除非订单另有规定，我们用普通邮件发货。

dict_mnemonic.text: “斯佩西法伊”——斯佩西法伊拿着表格逐项点名，一项不漏 → specify 明确规定、具体说明

root: 古法语 spécifier，晚期拉丁语 specificare“特别指出”，同出 specificus（species“种类”+ facere“做”），核心是“逐项点名，把笼统变成可指认的条目”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of specify, all one act of naming items until nothing is vague: exact speech, item-by-item listing, designation, contract stipulation, technical specs, rule conditions, the 'as specified' formula, and the boundary with mere mention.
sensesIntro.cn: specify 的八个义项都是同一个“逐项命名直到不再模糊”的动作：精确说明、逐条列出、指定、合同规定、技术规格、规则条件、as specified 固定说法，以及与“仅仅提到”的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand writes one named entry per line until the blank list is full and nothing is left vague.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在每一行写下一个具名条目，直到空白清单被填满，不再有模糊之处。

branches.en: NAMING: exact speech and item-by-item listing perform the original 'making a kind'.
branches.cn: 命名：精确说明与逐条列出，执行的正是最初的“造一个种类”。

branches.en: SELECTION: from the named entries, one exact item is chosen.
branches.cn: 选择：从具名条目中挑出确切的那一个。

branches.en: REQUIREMENT: the named entries become contract clauses and technical parameters.
branches.cn: 要求：具名条目变成合同条款与技术参数。

branches.en: RULES AND FORMULAS: conditions are drawn around a class, and 'as specified' points back to the written list.
branches.cn: 规则与固定说法：条件围绕类别画出边界，as specified 则指回那份写好的清单。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: mention and suggest leave the item unnamed, which is exactly what specify refuses to do.
branches.cn: 边界：mention 与 suggest 让条目保持未命名，而这正是 specify 拒绝做的事。

intro.en: English -ify comes through French from Latin -ificare, a fusion of facere 'make'. Specify is specific + -ify, so the suffix is a real 'make' element, not decorative.
intro.cn: 英语 -ify 经法语来自拉丁语 -ificare，是 facere“做”的融合形式。specify = specific + -ify，因此这个后缀是真的“使…做”成分，不是装饰。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around specify is the same one around specific: specificare 'mention particularly', specificus 'making a kind', species 'kind' and specere 'to look'.
latinIntro.cn: specify 周围的拉丁词族与 specific 相同：specificare“特别指出”、specificus“使成某一种类”、species“种类”、specere“看”。

items.meaning: a detailed description of requirements, or the act of stating them
items.meaningCN: 规格说明；明确规定（-cation 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The bridge was built to the engineer's specification.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥是按工程师的规格建造的。

items.meaning: named or laid down in advance
items.meaningCN: 规定的；指定的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: Use only the specified tools on this machine.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器上只能使用规定的工具。

items.meaningCN: 可明确说明的；可指定的
items.example: The goal must be specifiable in measurable terms.
items.exampleCN: 目标必须能用可测量的说法明确表述。

items.meaning: one who specifies; in linguistics, a word that limits a phrase
items.meaningCN: 说明者；指定者；（语言学）限定语
items.example: In 'this book', 'this' is a specifier.
items.exampleCN: 在 this book 中，this 是限定语。

items.example: The seeing verb lies under specify and species.
items.exampleCN: “看”的动词在 specify 与 species 之下。

items.example: The noun supplies the kind that specify makes explicit.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供 specify 所要明确的“种类”。

items.meaning: to make specific, to name in detail
items.example: The medieval verb is the direct parent of specify.
items.exampleCN: 这个中世纪拉丁动词是 specify 的直接母体。

items.example: It joins the kind to the act of making it clear.
items.exampleCN: 它把“种类”与“使其清楚”的动作连起来。

items.example: It forms specification, the act of stating in detail.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 specification，即详细说明。

latinEntries.meaning: to name or point out a particular thing
latinEntries.meaningCN: 特别指出；点名称出某事物

latinEntries.meaning: making or constituting a particular kind
latinEntries.meaningCN: 使成某一种类的；构成一个种类的

latinEntries.meaning: a kind or class; a biological species
latinEntries.meaningCN: 种类；物种

latinEntries.meaning: to look at, observe
latinEntries.meaningCN: 看；观察

definition_zh: 球体；球面；天球；范围；领域；势力范围；社会圈子
definition_en: a round solid or its surface; the sky imagined as a shell; a bounded area of activity, influence, or society
core_image: 从中心向各个方向等距撑开的球壳：中心到任何一点都一样远
scene: 天文馆里，讲解员把地球仪放进一个巨大的透明球壳。She explained that the old astronomers imagined the stars as fixed on one sphere that wrapped around the earth.
sceneCN: 这里 sphere 是「天球」（第 4 个义项：天文学中包裹地球的假想球面）；句意：她解释说，古代天文学家把星星想象成固定在一个包裹地球的球壳上。图中可辨识物件：地球仪、透明球壳、星点、天文馆投影。

pos.zh: 球体；球面；天球；范围；领域；势力范围；社会圈子

collocations.zh: 在某人能力／职责范围之内
半径为 r 的球面

senses.title: Geometry: a round solid
senses.definition: a perfectly round three-dimensional solid whose every point is the same distance from its centre
senses.definitionCN: 完全圆的三维实体，其表面每一点到中心的距离都相等
senses.example: The planet is not a perfect sphere; it bulges at the equator.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗行星不是完美的球体，它在赤道处隆起。
senses.why: Greek sphaira meant 'ball, sphere'. The defining image is a centre plus equal distance in every direction, which produces a closed round body.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 sphaira 意为“球、球体”。定义性的意象是一个中心，加上向各个方向相等的距离，由此生成一个闭合的圆形实体。

senses.title: Geometry: the surface alone
senses.definition: the two-dimensional surface of a ball, considered without its interior
senses.definitionCN: 球的二维表面，不计其内部
senses.example: The shortest path between two points on a sphere is an arc of a great circle.
senses.exampleCN: 球面上两点之间的最短路径是大圆的一段弧。
senses.why: Mathematics can separate the shell from the solid. The same word names the boundary itself, because a sphere is defined by its equal-distance surface.
senses.whyCN: 数学可以把壳与实体分开。同一个词也指边界本身，因为球正是由“等距表面”定义的。

senses.title: A ball-shaped object
senses.definition: a round object or container shaped like a ball, such as a glass globe or a lamp shade
senses.definitionCN: 形状像球的圆形物体或容器，如玻璃球、灯罩
senses.example: A glass sphere hung above the entrance, catching the light.
senses.exampleCN: 入口上方悬着一个玻璃球，接住了光。
senses.why: The abstract solid becomes a thing you can hold. Any manufactured ball — a lamp, a lens, a globe — is named by the same shape.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的几何体变成了可以拿在手里的东西。任何造出来的球——灯、透镜、地球仪——都用同一个形状命名。

senses.title: Astronomy: the celestial sphere
senses.definition: the sky imagined as a huge sphere surrounding the earth, on which the stars appear to be fixed
senses.definitionCN: 把天空想象成包围地球的巨大球面，星星看起来固定在其上
senses.example: Ancient astronomers mapped the stars onto a single celestial sphere.
senses.exampleCN: 古代天文学家把星星标绘在同一个天球上。
senses.why: Because the sky looks like a dome, Greek astronomy modelled it as a sphere. The shell sense is used for something with no real surface, purely to locate points.
senses.whyCN: 因为天空看起来像一个穹顶，希腊天文学把它模型化为球。球壳义被用于一个并没有真实表面的东西，纯粹为了定位各点。

senses.title: Range: a bounded area of knowledge or activity
senses.titleCN: 范围：有边界的一个知识或活动领域
senses.definition: a particular area of knowledge, activity, or interest, considered as having limits
senses.definitionCN: 知识、活动或兴趣的某个特定领域，被视为有界限的
senses.example: Tax policy lies outside the sphere of this committee.
senses.exampleCN: 税收政策不在这个委员会的职权范围之内。
senses.why: A sphere is closed and bounded. Abstract territory inherits that shape: an area with an inside and an outside, where the boundary matters more than the content.
senses.whyCN: 球是闭合而有界的。抽象领域继承了这一形状：一个有内、有外的区域，边界比内容更重要。

senses.title: Politics: sphere of influence
senses.definition: a region or domain in which a country or organization can exert dominant influence
senses.definitionCN: 某个国家或组织能施加主导影响的区域或领域
senses.example: The two empires divided the region into separate spheres of influence.
senses.exampleCN: 两个帝国把该地区划分成各自的势力范围。
senses.why: The bounded ball becomes a territory whose radius is reach. Inside the sphere your power is felt; outside it is another's.
senses.whyCN: 有界的球变成了一个以“影响力半径”衡量的领土。球内能感到你的力量，球外则属于别人。

senses.title: Society: one's circle or rank
senses.titleCN: 社会：某人的圈子或阶层
senses.definition: the social class, circle, or walk of life to which a person belongs
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所属的社会阶层、圈子或生活圈
senses.example: She moved easily among the spheres of art and finance.
senses.exampleCN: 她在艺术圈与金融圈之间游走自如。
senses.why: Social life is also divided into bounded regions. The sphere is the circle whose edge you do not casually cross, so the word names rank as well as company.
senses.whyCN: 社会生活同样被分成有界的区域。sphere 就是你不会随意越界的那个圈子，因此它既指“同伴”，也指“阶层”。

senses.title: Function: the area one is responsible for
senses.titleCN: 职能：一个人负责的范围
senses.definition: the field of duties, powers, or competence assigned to a person or body
senses.definitionCN: 分配给一个人或机构的职责、权力或权限范围
senses.example: Budget decisions are within the sphere of the finance office.
senses.exampleCN: 预算决定属于财务办公室的职责范围。
senses.why: This narrows the 'area of activity' sense to official duties. The boundary is now an assignment: what is inside is yours to decide.
senses.whyCN: 这是“活动领域”义收窄到正式职责。边界此时是一种分配：里面的部分由你决定。

senses.title: Usage boundary: sphere versus field or area
senses.definition: sphere suggests a closed, bounded domain; field and area are looser and do not imply a clear boundary
senses.definitionCN: sphere 暗示一个闭合、有边界的领域；field 与 area 更宽松，不暗示清晰的边界
senses.example: The field of biology is broad; the sphere of this lab is narrower.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学这个领域很广，而这个实验室的范围更窄。
senses.why: Field is open ground you work in; area is a neutral extent. Sphere keeps the closed shell, so it suits influence, responsibility and social rank, where edges are meant to be felt.
senses.whyCN: field 是你耕作的开阔地面；area 是中性的面积。sphere 保留了闭合球壳，因此适合影响力、职责与社会阶层这些“边界要被感觉到”的场合。

intro.en: Sphere is a Greek word for a ball that became a Latin and French word for the sky, then an English word for any bounded region. The deeper Greek origin is not securely known.
intro.cn: sphere 是希腊语中表示“球”的词，先变成拉丁语和法语中表示“天空”的词，再变成英语中表示任何有界区域的词。希腊语更深一层的来源并不确知。

items.en: Greek sphaira meant 'ball, sphere, globe', and was already used by astronomers for the celestial sphere. Its deeper origin is uncertain; handbooks suggest it may be a Pre-Greek word rather than a securely Indo-European one.
items.cn: 希腊语 sphaira 意为“球、球体、天体球”，天文学家已用它指天球。其更深来源不确定；工具书认为它可能是前希腊语词，而非可确证的印欧语词。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as sphaera 'sphere, globe, celestial sphere'. The Latin spelling with ph marks the Greek origin and is the reason English keeps ph today.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 sphaera“球、球体、天球”。带 ph 的拉丁拼写标记了希腊来源，也是英语今天保留 ph 的原因。

items.en: Old French espere (Modern French sphère) carried the word into English. The initial e- was dropped, giving Middle English spere and modern sphere.
items.cn: 古法语 espere（现代法语 sphère）把词带入英语。词首的 e- 脱落，形成中古英语 spere 与现代 sphere。

items.en: First recorded in English with the astronomical and geometrical senses. Medieval cosmology pictured nested spheres carrying the planets, and the 'music of the spheres' came from that model.
items.cn: 14 世纪最早记录于英语，兼有天文与几何义。中世纪宇宙论想象一层层球壳承载行星，“天球音乐”之说就来自这个模型。

items.en: The bounded-ball image extends to society and politics: 'sphere of activity' is 17c., 'sphere of influence' becomes a standard term in 19c. diplomacy.
items.cn: 有界球的意象延伸到社会与政治：sphere of activity 见于 17 世纪，sphere of influence 在 19 世纪外交中成为标准术语。

items.en: No Proto-Indo-European root is given here. The Greek word's prehistory is marked uncertain in standard references, so any deeper reconstruction would be guesswork.
items.cn: 此处不给出原始印欧语词根。通行资料把希腊语词的更早历史标为不确定，再做更深的重构只能算猜测。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Greek ball; the second separates a model globe, a poetic orb, an open field, and a domain that is owned.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个希腊语“球”上；第二组区分模型地球仪、诗性球体、开阔领域与归属性的域。

entries.definition: shaped like a sphere. It is the adjective; note the first vowel is not the same as the noun sphere.
entries.definitionCN: 球形的。它是形容词；注意首个元音与名词 sphere 并不相同。

entries.definition: a shape that is almost a sphere, such as the earth or a rugby ball. The -oid suffix means 'like'.
entries.definitionCN: 接近球形的形状，如地球或橄榄球。-oid 后缀意为“像”。

entries.definition: half of a sphere, especially half of the earth. hemi- 'half' + sphere.
entries.definitionCN: 半球，尤指地球的一半。hemi-“半”+ sphere。

entries.definition: a spherical model of the earth, or the earth itself. It is concrete, while sphere is often abstract.
entries.definitionCN: 地球的球状模型，或地球本身。它偏具体，而 sphere 常用于抽象义。

entries.definition: a sphere, especially a heavenly body or an eye. It is poetic and much narrower than sphere.
entries.definitionCN: 球体，尤指天体或眼睛。它属诗语，适用范围比 sphere 窄得多。

entries.definition: an area of study or activity. It is open and unbounded, unlike sphere, which keeps a closed edge.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或活动的领域。它是开放、无界的，不像 sphere 保留闭合的边缘。

entries.definition: an area of knowledge or control belonging to someone. It stresses ownership, while sphere stresses the boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某人的知识或控制领域。它强调归属，而 sphere 强调边界。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: Greek sphaira 'ball' passed through Latin sphaera into English, and the combining form still builds hemisphere and biosphere.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：希腊语 sphaira“球”经拉丁语 sphaera 进入英语，这个组合成分至今仍能构成 hemisphere 与 biosphere。

normal.en: Sphaira has meant 'ball' for more than two thousand years; every sense still has that round, closed shape.
normal.cn: sphaira 表示“球”已有两千多年；每个义项都还带着那个圆而闭合的形状。

normal.en: The ph in sphere marks its Greek origin (sphaira), just as ph does in philosophy and physics.
normal.cn: sphere 里的 ph 标记了它的希腊来源（sphaira），就像 philosophy 与 physics 中的 ph 一样。

normal.en: The celestial sphere is the sky treated as one shell with stars pinned to it: a useful fiction for locating points.
normal.cn: 天球就是把天空当作一层壳，把星星钉在上面：一个用来定位各点的有用虚构。

normal.en: Sphere of influence is a ball whose radius is reach: the further from the centre, the weaker the pull.
normal.cn: sphere of influence 是一个以“影响力”为半径的球：离中心越远，拉力越弱。

normal.en: Hemisphere and biosphere keep the bounded-ball image: half a ball, and the thin shell of life around the earth.
normal.cn: hemisphere 与 biosphere 保留有界球的意象：半个球，以及地球周围那层薄薄的生物壳。

abstract.en: Put a dot on paper and expand it equally in every direction. The surface you get is the sphere: its centre is power, its radius is reach.
abstract.cn: 在纸上点一个点，让它向四面八方等距扩张。得到的那层表面就是 sphere：中心是力量，半径是触及范围。

abstract.en: Every area has an edge. Sphere makes that edge a surface: inside is yours, outside is not, and the wall itself is the meaning.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都有边缘。sphere 把边缘变成一层表面：里面是你的，外面不是，而那面墙本身就是词义。

abstract.en: The celestial sphere is a thought-bubble drawn around the earth, an imaginary shell that lets people place what has no fixed place.
abstract.cn: 天球是围绕地球画出的一个思想气泡，一层假想的壳，让人能安放那些本来没有固定位置的东西。

examples.en: A sphere has the same distance from its centre to every point on its surface.
examples.cn: 球体从中心到表面每一点的距离都相等。

examples.en: Education policy belongs to the public sphere, not to one ministry alone.
examples.cn: 教育政策属于公共领域，不归某一个部委独有。

examples.en: The two countries agreed to respect each other's spheres of influence.
examples.cn: 两国同意尊重彼此的势力范围。

dict_mnemonic.text: “斯菲尔”——斯菲尔把一颗球吹圆，气从中心向四面八方等距撑开 → sphere 球体、范围

root: 希腊语 sphaira“球、球体、天体球”，经拉丁语 sphaera 与古法语进入英语；更深来源不确定（可能为前希腊语），核心是“从中心等距撑开的球壳”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of sphere, all one closed shell around a centre: a solid, a surface, a ball-like object, the sky, an area of knowledge, a zone of influence, a social circle, a duty, and the boundary with looser words.
sensesIntro.cn: sphere 的九个义项都是围绕一个中心的同一层闭合球壳：实体、表面、球状物、天空、知识领域、势力范围、社会圈子、职责，以及它与更宽松词语的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a centre expands equally in every direction and closes into a shell; whatever is inside is bounded.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个中心向各方向等距扩张，闭合成一层壳；壳内的一切都是有界的。

branches.en: GEOMETRY: the solid and its surface are the literal shell.
branches.cn: 几何：实体与表面就是字面的球壳。

branches.en: OBJECTS AND SKY: a manufactured ball, then the imagined shell of the stars.
branches.cn: 实物与天空：造出来的球，再到想象出的星空之壳。

branches.en: TERRITORY: knowledge and political reach both become bounded regions.
branches.cn: 领地：知识领域与政治影响力都变成有界区域。

branches.en: SOCIETY AND DUTY: social circles and official responsibilities are spheres with edges you do not cross.
branches.cn: 社会与职责：社会圈子与官方职责都是带边界的 sphere，边界不可随意越过。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: field and area are open; sphere is closed, which is the whole difference.
branches.cn: 边界：field 与 area 是开放的；sphere 是闭合的，这就是全部区别。

intro.en: Sphere is a free root that also works as a combining form. English builds compounds with hemi- and bio-, and adjectives with -ical and -oid; it does not add a native prefix to sphere itself.
intro.cn: sphere 是自由词根，也可作组合成分。英语用 hemi-、bio- 构成复合词，用 -ical、-oid 构成形容词；它本身不加本土前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin took Greek sphaira as sphaera, and the derived family stays close to 'ball': sphaericus 'spherical', sphaeroides 'sphere-like', sphaerula 'small sphere'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语 sphaira 借为 sphaera，其派生词族始终围绕“球”：sphaericus“球形的”、sphaeroides“球状的”、sphaerula“小球”。

items.meaningCN: 球形的；球面的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: The lens is spherical, so the image curves at the edges.
items.exampleCN: 这片透镜是球面的，所以图像边缘会弯曲。

items.meaning: a body that is nearly but not exactly spherical
items.meaningCN: 类球体；椭球体（-oid 表示“像、形状”）
items.example: The earth is an oblate spheroid, flattened at the poles.
items.exampleCN: 地球是一个扁椭球体，两极略扁。

items.meaning: half of a sphere, especially half of the earth
items.meaningCN: 半球；地球的一半（hemi- 表示“半”）
items.example: Most of the world's population lives in the northern hemisphere.
items.exampleCN: 世界大多数人口住在北半球。

items.meaning: the zone of the earth where life exists
items.meaningCN: 生物圈；地球上生命存在的区域（bio- 表示“生命”）
items.example: Pollution is altering the chemistry of the biosphere.
items.exampleCN: 污染正在改变生物圈的化学组成。

items.example: The Latin noun is the direct source of sphere.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是 sphere 的直接来源。

items.example: Greek sphaira named the ball before Latin borrowed it.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 sphaira 先命名了球，再由拉丁语借入。

items.example: It forms spherical, shaped like a ball.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 spherical，即球形的。

items.example: It forms hemisphere, half of a sphere.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 hemisphere，即半球。

items.example: It forms spheroid, a ball-like solid.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 spheroid，即类球体。

latinEntries.meaning: a sphere, globe, or celestial sphere
latinEntries.meaningCN: 球；球体；天球

latinEntries.meaning: spherical, round
latinEntries.meaningCN: 球形的；圆的

latinEntries.meaning: sphere-shaped, nearly spherical
latinEntries.meaningCN: 球状的；近球形的

latinEntries.meaning: a small sphere or ball
latinEntries.meaningCN: 小球；小球体

definition_zh: 稳定的；稳固的；可靠的；n. 马厩；赛马房
definition_en: firmly balanced and unlikely to move, change, or fail; a building where horses are kept
core_image: 一根柱子稳稳扎在地里，四面来风都推不动它
scene: 老木匠把梯子第四条腿垫平，双手摇了摇。The ladder did not move at all, and only after it was stable did he let the apprentice climb.
sceneCN: 这里 stable 是「稳固的」（第 1 个义项：结构不易倾倒）；句意：梯子一点不动，只有确认它稳固了，他才让学徒爬上去。图中可辨识物件：木梯、垫木、木匠的手、地面。

pos.zh: 稳定的；稳固的；可靠的；（病情）稳定的
马厩；赛马房；（同一马主的）一群赛马

senses.title: Structurally firm: it will not fall
senses.definition: built or placed so that it does not move, tip, or collapse easily
senses.definitionCN: 建造或放置得不易移动、倾覆或倒塌
senses.example: The ladder is stable enough to carry two workers.
senses.exampleCN: 这架梯子足够稳固，可以站两个工人。
senses.why: Stable comes from Latin stabilis 'firm', built on stare 'to stand' + -bilis 'able to'. The first image is a thing able to stand: its base holds and its weight is over it.
senses.whyCN: stable 来自拉丁语 stabilis“稳固”，由 stare“站立”+ -bilis“能…的”构成。最初的画面是一个“站得住”的东西：底座撑住，重量落在其上。

senses.title: Steady state: it does not change much
senses.definition: remaining at a similar level or condition over time, without sudden rises or falls
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内保持相近的水平或状态，没有突然的起落
senses.example: The patient's blood pressure has been stable for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 病人的血压已经稳定了三天。
senses.why: A standing object does not shift. Applied to a level or condition, 'able to stand' becomes 'does not move much' — the same balance, now in time rather than space.
senses.whyCN: 站住的东西不会移位。用在水平或状态上，“站得住”就变成“变化不大”——同一种平衡，只是从空间移到了时间上。

senses.title: Personal reliability: steady in character
senses.definition: reasonable, calm, and not likely to change mood or behaviour suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 讲理、冷静，情绪或行为不易突然变化
senses.example: He is a stable person who stays calm under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个稳重的人，在压力下仍能保持冷静。
senses.why: A person who is stable keeps their balance like a standing body. The physical 'does not tip' becomes emotional 'does not swing', and reliability follows.
senses.whyCN: stable 的人像站立的物体一样保持平衡。物理上的“不倾倒”变成情绪上的“不摇摆”，可靠感随之而来。

senses.title: Chemistry and physics: not decaying or breaking down
senses.titleCN: 化学与物理：不衰变、不分解
senses.definition: describing an atom, compound, or system that does not spontaneously decay or break apart
senses.definitionCN: 描述不自发衰变或分解的原子、化合物或系统
senses.example: Carbon-12 is a stable isotope of carbon.
senses.exampleCN: 碳-12 是碳的一种稳定同位素。
senses.why: The technical sense is literal staying power: an atom that 'stands' instead of falling apart. Stability here is measured by whether the structure holds over time.
senses.whyCN: 这个专业义就是字面的“站得住”：一个“站住”而不散架的原子。这里的稳定性用结构能否随时间保持来衡量。

senses.title: Medicine: a condition that is not worsening
senses.definition: in a serious but unchanging condition that is not getting better or worse
senses.definitionCN: 处于严重但未变化的状态，既未好转也未恶化
senses.example: After surgery she was listed as stable.
senses.exampleCN: 手术后她的情况被列为稳定。
senses.why: Medical stable is a narrow, cautious use: the patient is not improving, but the level is holding. The word reports balance, not health.
senses.whyCN: 医学上的 stable 是一个狭窄而谨慎的用法：病人并未好转，但水平维持住了。这个词报告的是平衡，不是健康。

senses.title: Noun: a building for horses
senses.definition: a building in which horses are kept and fed
senses.definitionCN: 饲养马匹的建筑
senses.example: The groom led the mare back to the stable.
senses.exampleCN: 马夫把母马牵回马厩。
senses.why: The noun comes from Latin stabulum 'standing place', from stare 'to stand'. A stable is literally where animals stand — the same stand-root, a different part of speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自拉丁语 stabulum“站立之处”，再来自 stare“站立”。马厩字面上就是动物站立的地方——同一个 stand 词根，不同的词性。

senses.title: Noun: the horses of one owner
senses.titleCN: 名词：同一马主的一群赛马
senses.definition: a group of racing horses owned or trained by one person or yard
senses.definitionCN: 由同一人或同一马房拥有或训练的一群赛马
senses.example: The trainer has a stable of twenty horses.
senses.exampleCN: 这位练马师有一个二十匹马的赛马房。
senses.why: The building stands for the group inside it. Metonymy turns 'the barn' into 'the horses kept in the barn', a standard racing usage.
senses.whyCN: 建筑代替了里面的一群。转喻把“马厩”变成“养在马厩里的马”，这是赛马界的标准用法。

senses.title: Figurative: a stable of talent
senses.definition: a group of writers, players, or performers kept available by one organization
senses.definitionCN: 由一个机构储备、可供调用的作家、球员或表演者群体
senses.example: The magazine has a stable of young writers.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志拥有一批年轻作家。
senses.why: The horse stable is applied to people: talent is kept, trained and sent out, like racehorses. The metaphor is slightly ironic but well established in journalism and sport.
senses.whyCN: 马厩被用到人身上：人才像赛马一样被养着、训练、派出去。这个比喻略带反讽，但在新闻与体育界已很固定。

senses.title: Usage boundary: stable versus steady
senses.definition: steady means continuing at a regular rate; stable means not likely to move, change, or collapse
senses.definitionCN: steady 指以规律的速度持续；stable 指不易移动、改变或崩溃
senses.example: Steady growth can still be unstable if it depends on debt.
senses.exampleCN: 稳定的增长如果是靠债务支撑，也可能是不稳定的。
senses.why: Steady describes a rate: it keeps going. Stable describes a state: it keeps standing. A steady heartbeat can be dangerously high; a stable patient is not necessarily improving.
senses.whyCN: steady 描述速率：一直进行；stable 描述状态：一直站住。心跳 steady 可能快到危险；病人 stable 也未必在好转。

intro.en: Stable is a standing word. Latin stare 'to stand' gives both the adjective stabilis 'able to stand' and the noun stabulum 'standing place', which is why a horse stable and a stable economy share a root.
intro.cn: stable 是一个“站立”词。拉丁语 stare“站立”既给出形容词 stabilis“站得住的”，也给出名词 stabulum“站立之处”，因此马厩与稳定的经济共享同一个词根。

items.en: First recorded in English as an adjective meaning 'firmly fixed, steadfast', and as a noun for a horse house. The figurative senses develop later.
items.cn: 13 世纪最早记录于英语：形容词义“牢牢固定、坚定”，名词义“马厩”。比喻义在此后发展。

items.en: From Latin stabilis 'firm, steadfast', analysed as stare 'to stand' + -bilis 'able to be'. The noun stabulum 'standing place, stall' comes from the same stare.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 stabilis“稳固、坚定”，可分析为 stare“站立”+ -bilis“能够被…的”。名词 stabulum“站立之处、厩”也来自同一个 stare。

items.en: Old French estable supplied both the adjective 'firm' and the noun 'stall, stable', which is why English stable has two parts of speech from one spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 estable 同时提供了形容词“稳固的”和名词“厩、马房”，因此英语 stable 一个拼写兼有两个词性。

items.en: Stare is traced to PIE *sta- 'to stand', also behind stand, state, status, statue, constant and insist. The root is generally accepted, though the reconstruction is not directly attested.
items.cn: stare 被追溯到原始印欧语 *sta-“站立”，也是 stand、state、status、statue、constant、insist 的词根。该词根属一般认为，重构并无直接实证。

items.en: Status also comes from stare, but it means 'the position where one stands'; statistic reached English through German Statistik from status. Stable is 'able to stand', status is 'the place stood in' — same root, different meanings.
items.cn: status 同样来自 stare，但意为“所站的位置”；statistic 则经德语 Statistik 上溯 status。stable 是“站得住”，status 是“所站之处”——同源而不同义。

items.en: The 'unchanging level' sense is standard by the 17c.; the psychological and medical uses are modern. The 'stable of talent' metaphor belongs to 20c. journalism and sport.
items.cn: “水平不变”义在 17 世纪已成标准；心理与医学用法属现代。a stable of talent 的比喻属 20 世纪新闻与体育用语。

note.en: The first group shares the stare root or the -stable shape; the second separates regularity, physical firmness, safety, and absolute sameness.
note.cn: 第一组共享 stare 词根或 -stable 词形；第二组区分规律性、物理坚固、安全与绝对的同一不变。

entries.definition: the noun: the quality of being stable. Note the stress moves to the second syllable.
entries.definitionCN: 名词：稳定的性质。注意重音移到第二音节。

entries.definition: the verb: to make or become stable. It adds -ize to the adjective stem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词：使稳定、变得稳定。它在形容词词干后加 -ize。

entries.definition: a basic food, or a fastener. It looks and sounds close to stable but comes from Middle Low German stapel 'pile, market', not stare.
entries.definitionCN: 主食；订书钉。它形音都接近 stable，但来自中古低地德语 stapel“堆、市场”，与 stare 无关。

entries.definition: continuing at a regular pace or level. It describes movement, while stable describes the ability to stay put.
entries.definitionCN: 以规律的速度或水平持续。它描述运动，而 stable 描述“站得住”的能力。

entries.definition: solid and not yielding to pressure. It is about physical hardness or resolve, not about balance over time.
entries.definitionCN: 坚实、受压不变形。它讲物理硬度或决心，不讲随时间的平衡。

entries.definition: protected from danger or loss. It concerns safety, while stable concerns balance and the absence of change.
entries.definitionCN: 免受危险或损失。它关心安全，而 stable 关心平衡与不变化。

entries.definition: staying exactly the same. It is more absolute than stable, which allows small fluctuations around a level.
entries.definitionCN: 完全保持不变。它比 stable 更绝对；stable 允许在一个水平附近有小幅波动。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: stare 'stand' + -bilis 'able to'. The same stare gives stabulum 'standing place', which is the horse stable, and also status, which is where you stand.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：stare“站立”+ -bilis“能够…的”。同一个 stare 还给出 stabulum“站立之处”，即马厩，以及 status，即你所站的位置。

normal.en: stabilis = stare 'stand' + -bilis 'able': stable is literally 'able to stand'. Stability is that ability as a noun.
normal.cn: stabilis = stare“站”+ -bilis“能”：stable 字面上就是“站得住”。stability 就是这种能力的名词形式。

normal.en: stabulum 'standing place' is the horse stable: a building where animals stand and are fed.
normal.cn: stabulum“站立之处”就是马厩：动物站立、进食的建筑。

normal.en: status is also from stare, but it means the position where you stand; statistic came to English through German Statistik from status.
normal.cn: status 也来自 stare，但意为“你所站的位置”；statistic 则经德语 Statistik 上溯 status 进入英语。

normal.en: A stable isotope is an atom that stands instead of decaying — the same 'able to stand' in physics.
normal.cn: 稳定同位素就是一个“站住”而不衰变的原子——物理学里同一个“站得住”。

normal.en: A stable of writers treats a group of talent like horses in one barn: kept, trained and sent out.
normal.cn: a stable of writers 把一群人才当作一个马房里的马：养着、训练、派出去。

abstract.en: A cone standing on its base: as long as its centre of gravity stays over the base, it stands. Stable is that condition, not the cone.
abstract.cn: 一个用底面站立的圆锥：只要重心留在底面之上，它就站着。stable 是那个条件，不是圆锥本身。

abstract.en: A gyroscope keeps its axis while spinning. Stable does not mean motionless; it means able to return to the same position after a push.
abstract.cn: 陀螺旋转时保持自己的轴。stable 不是“不动”，而是被推一下之后能回到同一位置。

abstract.en: A ball at the bottom of a bowl rolls back when pushed. The stability belongs to the shape of the bowl, not to the ball.
abstract.cn: 碗底的小球被推一下会滚回来。稳定性属于碗的形状，而不是小球。

examples.en: Check that the scaffolding is stable before anyone climbs it.
examples.cn: 任何人爬上去之前，先确认脚手架稳固。

examples.en: The economy stayed stable despite the political crisis.
examples.cn: 尽管发生政治危机，经济仍保持稳定。

examples.en: She has worked in the same stable since she was sixteen.
examples.cn: 她十六岁起就在同一个马厩工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: “斯泰波”——斯泰波四条腿扎进土里，怎么推都不倒 → stable 稳定的、稳固的

root: 拉丁语 stabilis“稳固的”= stare“站立”+ -bilis“能…的”；名词“马厩”来自 stabulum“站立之处”，同出 stare。核心是“站得稳、站得住”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of stable, all one act of standing: a firm structure, an unchanging level, a steady character, a non-decaying atom, a holding medical condition, a horse house, a yard of horses, a pool of talent, and the boundary with steady.
sensesIntro.cn: stable 的九个义项都是同一个“站住”的动作：稳固结构、不变水平、稳重性格、不衰变的原子、维持住的病情、马厩、一群赛马、一班子人才，以及与 steady 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body stands on its base, its weight centred, and a push does not knock it over.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个物体立在底座上，重量居中，推一下也倒不了。

branches.en: BALANCE: a structure that stands, and a level that holds in time.
branches.cn: 平衡：站得住的结构，以及随时间维持住的水平。

branches.en: CHARACTER: the same balance turns inward and becomes emotional steadiness.
branches.cn: 性格：同一种平衡转向内部，成为情绪上的稳重。

branches.en: TECHNICAL: an atom or a patient that holds its structure instead of falling apart.
branches.cn: 专业：保持结构而不散架的原子或病人。

branches.en: THE NOUN: stabulum is literally a standing place, then the horses that stand in it.
branches.cn: 名词：stabulum 字面就是站立之处，再指站在其中的马。

branches.en: EXTENSION AND EDGE: talent kept like horses, and steady (a rate) versus stable (a state).
branches.cn: 延伸与边界：人才像马一样被养着；steady 讲速率，stable 讲状态。

intro.en: Stable has no live English prefix; its Latin parts are frozen inside stabilis. English adds -ity, -ize and the negative un- to the finished adjective.
intro.cn: stable 没有活的英语前缀；它的拉丁成分凝固在 stabilis 里。英语在成品形容词上加 -ity、-ize 与否定前缀 un-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on stare 'to stand': stabilis 'able to stand', stabulum 'standing place', status 'position stood in', and stabilire 'to make firm'.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族围绕 stare“站立”：stabilis“站得住的”、stabulum“站立之处”、status“所站的位置”、stabilire“使稳固”。

items.meaning: the quality or state of being stable
items.meaningCN: 稳定；稳固性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: Political stability encouraged foreign investment.
items.exampleCN: 政治稳定促进了外国投资。

items.meaning: to make something stable or keep it from changing
items.meaningCN: 使稳定；使稳固（-ize 表示“使…化”）
items.example: Doctors used drugs to stabilize her heart rate.
items.exampleCN: 医生用药稳定她的心率。

items.meaning: likely to move, change, or collapse
items.meaningCN: 不稳定的；不稳固的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: The cliff is unstable after the heavy rain.
items.exampleCN: 大雨之后，那处悬崖很不稳固。

items.meaningCN: 稳定地；稳固地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The platform sits stably on four concrete feet.
items.exampleCN: 这个平台稳稳地立在四个混凝土支脚上。

items.example: The verb is the standing image behind stable.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 stable 背后“站立”的意象。

items.example: The adjective came through Old French into English as stable.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词进入英语成为 stable。

items.example: Latin stabulum already meant a place where animals stand.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 stabulum 本已指牲畜站立之处。

items.example: It forms stabilize, to make something steady.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 stabilize，即使某物稳定。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 稳固的；坚定的；站得住的

latinEntries.meaning: to stand, remain standing
latinEntries.meaningCN: 站立；保持站立
