definition_zh: 统计量；统计数据；统计数字
definition_en: a single numerical fact obtained by collecting and analysing data; in the plural, the science of collecting and interpreting such data
core_image: 从一大片散乱的数字里，量出一个能代表整体的数
scene: 人口研究办公室里，研究员把十万份问卷汇成一张表。The average of 2.3 people per household was the one statistic that summed up the whole city.
sceneCN: 这里 statistic 是「统计量」（第 1 个义项：由大量数据算出的单个数值）；句意：平均每户 2.3 人这一个统计量，就概括了整座城市。图中可辨识物件：问卷堆、汇总表、屏幕上的数字、办公室。

pos.zh: 统计量；统计数据；统计数字

senses.title: One figure drawn from data
senses.titleCN: 从数据中算出的单个数值
senses.definition: a single number that summarizes a set of data, such as a rate, average, or total
senses.definitionCN: 概括一组数据的单个数值，如比率、平均值或总数
senses.example: The average income is the statistic most often quoted.
senses.exampleCN: 平均收入是最常被引用的统计量。
senses.why: Statistic is a back-formation from statistics: the mass noun was cut down to name one item inside it. The first sense is therefore a single measured figure, not the discipline.
senses.whyCN: statistic 是由 statistics 逆构而来：把表示整体的名词切下一块，用来命名其中的一项。因此第一个义项是单个测得的数值，而不是学科。

senses.title: A reported data point
senses.definition: one item of numerical information in a report, table, or news story
senses.definitionCN: 报告、表格或新闻报道中的一项数字信息
senses.example: Unemployment is the statistic that decides the election.
senses.exampleCN: 失业率是决定选举的那项数据。
senses.why: Once a figure is quoted, it becomes a unit of public argument. The word moves from calculation to citation: a statistic is something a report can point at.
senses.whyCN: 数字一旦被引用，就成了公共论证的单位。词义从“计算”转向“引用”：statistic 是报告可以指着说的那一项。

senses.title: Statistics: the science
senses.definition: in the plural statistics, the science of collecting, analysing, and interpreting numerical data
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式 statistics，指收集、分析并解释数值数据的学科
senses.example: She studied statistics before turning to journalism.
senses.exampleCN: 她先学统计学，之后转做新闻。
senses.why: The discipline name came from German Statistik, the 'science of the state'. English kept the plural form but treats it as one subject, so statistics takes a singular verb here.
senses.whyCN: 学科名来自德语 Statistik，即“关于国家状况的学问”。英语保留复数形式，却把它当作一门学科，因此这里的 statistics 接单数动词。

senses.title: Statistics: the collected data
senses.titleCN: 统计数据：收集起来的一堆数字
senses.definition: in the plural statistics, the numerical data themselves, taken as a body
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式 statistics，指作为整体的一批数值数据本身
senses.example: The latest statistics show a fall in road deaths.
senses.exampleCN: 最新统计数据显示道路死亡人数下降。
senses.why: The same plural word can name the output rather than the method. Here statistics is a mass of figures, and the verb is plural because the figures are many.
senses.whyCN: 同一个复数词可以指学科的产出，而不是方法。这里的 statistics 是一大堆数字，动词用复数，因为数字是多个。

senses.title: A comparative measure
senses.definition: a calculated value used to compare groups or to test whether a difference is real
senses.definitionCN: 用来比较群体、或检验差异是否真实存在的计算值
senses.example: The test statistic fell just below the threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 检验统计量略低于临界值。
senses.why: In research, the figure is built precisely to carry a comparison. This is the technical core of the word: a number whose job is to decide a question.
senses.whyCN: 在研究里，这个数值是专门为承载比较而构造的。这是该词的技术核心：一个以“判定问题”为职责的数字。

senses.title: A performance number in sport
senses.definition: in sport, a recorded count of a player's actions, such as goals, assists, or possession
senses.definitionCN: 体育中指球员某项动作的记录数字，如进球、助攻或控球率
senses.example: His scoring statistics improved every season.
senses.exampleCN: 他的得分数据每个赛季都在提高。
senses.why: Sport turns every action into a countable event, so the same word covers performance records. The figure is still a summary; only the subject has changed from a population to a player.
senses.whyCN: 体育把每个动作都变成可计数的事件，于是同一个词也覆盖表现记录。数值仍是概括，只是对象从人群变成了球员。

senses.title: A person reduced to a number
senses.definition: in informal usage, a person regarded as a mere count, especially a casualty or a case
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指只被当成一个数字的人，尤指伤亡者或案例
senses.example: He refused to be just another statistic in the accident report.
senses.exampleCN: 他拒绝只成为事故报告里的又一个数字。
senses.why: This is the dehumanising branch: when a life is entered as one row in a table, the word records the loss of individuality. The coldness is the point.
senses.whyCN: 这是去人性化的分支：当一条生命被记成表格里的一行，这个词记录了个体性的丧失。冷漠正是它的用意。

senses.title: Usage boundary: statistic vs statistics
senses.definition: statistic is one item; statistics is either the science (singular verb) or the body of data (plural verb); the adjective is statistical
senses.definitionCN: statistic 是一项数据；statistics 或指学科（接单数动词），或指一批数据（接复数动词）；形容词是 statistical
senses.example: One statistic is not enough; statistics as a science tells you how to read many.
senses.exampleCN: 一项 statistic 不够；作为学科的 statistics 教你怎么读许多项。
senses.why: The singular/plural split is the whole grammar of the word. Counting decides the meaning: one figure, one discipline, or many figures.
senses.whyCN: 单复数的分工就是这个词的全部语法。数一数就决定了意思：一个数值、一门学科，还是一堆数值。

intro.en: Statistic is a back-formation from statistics, and statistics began as a German name for the study of the state. The chain runs from Latin status 'condition' through New Latin statisticus 'of state affairs' to German Statistik, then into English. The singular statistic is a 19th-century cut-down of the plural.
intro.cn: statistic 是由 statistics 逆构而来，而 statistics 最初是德语里“研究国家”的学问名称。链条从拉丁语 status“状况”，经新拉丁语 statisticus“国家事务的”，到德语 Statistik，再进入英语。单数 statistic 是 19 世纪从复数形式切下来的。

items.en: English adopts statistics in the late 18c. (often dated to the 1770s-1780s) as 'the science of the state', a loan from German Statistik. The exact first date is uncertain, since several authors used the word almost at once.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪晚期（常被定为 1770—1780 年代）借入 statistics，意为“关于国家的学问”，来自德语 Statistik。确切的首见年代存疑，因为好几位作者几乎同时使用了这个词。

items.en: German Statistik was established as a university subject in the 18th c., notably by Gottfried Achenwall (1749). It meant the systematic description of a state's population, resources, and institutions.
items.cn: 德语 Statistik 在 18 世纪成为大学学科，尤其由戈特弗里德·阿亨瓦尔（1749）确立。它指对一个国家的人口、资源与制度作系统描述。

items.en: Statistik goes back to New Latin statisticus 'of state affairs or politics', from Latin status 'condition, position, state'.
items.cn: Statistik 上溯到新拉丁语 statisticus“国家事务或政治的”，后者来自拉丁语 status“状况、位置、状态”。

items.en: Latin status is a noun from stare 'to stand'. The PIE base *sta- 'to stand' is generally accepted, not proven. The same family gives state, static, station, constant, and stable.
items.cn: 拉丁语 status 是来自 stare“站立”的名词。原始印欧语 *sta-“站立”属于一般认为，而非确证。同一个词族还给出 state、static、station、constant、stable。

items.en: The singular statistic appears in the 19th c. (roughly the 1850s-1870s; exact first use uncertain) as a back-formation meaning one item of statistical data. Speakers needed a word for a single figure inside the new mass noun.
items.cn: 单数 statistic 出现在 19 世纪（大致 1850—1870 年代；确切首用存疑），是逆构词，指一项统计数据。使用者需要一个词来指称这个新集合名词里的单个数值。

items.en: Statistic and status are cousins, not synonyms. Both descend from stare: status is the standing condition itself, while statistic is one figure derived from data about the state. Statistics remains the name of the discipline.
items.cn: statistic 与 status 是同族词，不是同义词。两者都出自 stare：status 是“所站的状态”本身，statistic 则是从关于国家的数据里得出的一个数值。statistics 仍是学科名称。

note.en: The first group is form-and-root neighbours: the plural, the adjective, and the Latin cousin status. The second group separates a single measured number from raw data, a quoted figure, an indicator, and a limit.
note.cn: 第一组是词形与词根上的邻居：复数形式、形容词，以及拉丁同族词 status。第二组把“单个测得的数”与原始数据、被引用的数字、指标和界限区分开。

entries.definition: the science of data, or the body of data itself. It is not a synonym when you mean one figure.
entries.definitionCN: 统计学，或数据本身。当你想说“一个数值”时，它不是同义词。

entries.definition: relating to statistics. The adjective never names a single number.
entries.definitionCN: 与统计有关的。这个形容词从不指单个数字。

entries.definition: rank or condition. It shares the status/stare family but means standing, not a data item.
entries.definitionCN: 地位或状态。它同属 status/stare 词族，但指“所站的位置”，不是一项数据。

entries.definition: a single raw fact, before any analysis. A statistic is usually calculated from many data.
entries.definitionCN: 未经分析的单个原始事实。statistic 通常由许多 data 计算得出。

entries.definition: a number quoted in writing or speech. It may or may not be statistical.
entries.definitionCN: 书面或口头引用的数字。它可能是统计数字，也可能不是。

entries.definition: a measure chosen to track performance. It is built for judgement, while a statistic can be purely descriptive.
entries.definitionCN: 为追踪表现而选定的度量。它为评判而生，而 statistic 可以只是描述性的。

entries.definition: a limit or fixed characteristic of a system; in statistics it means a true population value, not a sample figure.
entries.definitionCN: 系统的界限或固定特征；在统计学中指总体的真实值，而不是样本数值。

normalIntro.en: Real parts: statistics minus its plural -s gives statistic, and the whole family rests on Latin status 'condition', from stare 'to stand'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：statistics 去掉复数 -s 就是 statistic，整个词族建立在拉丁语 status“状况”上，后者来自 stare“站立”。

normal.en: statistics has -s, statistic does not. The singular is literally a piece cut out of the plural.
normal.cn: statistics 有 -s，statistic 没有。单数就是从复数里切下来的一块。

normal.en: The German subject Statistik described the state; statistic is one item from that state's data.
normal.cn: 德语的 Statistik 这门学问描述国家；statistic 就是从这个国家的数据里取出的一项。

normal.en: status and statistic share stare 'to stand': status is where something stands, statistic is a number taken from data about that standing.
normal.cn: status 与 statistic 共享 stare“站立”：status 是东西站在哪儿，statistic 是从关于这种状态的数据里取出的一个数。

normal.en: One statistic, two statistics; statistics with a singular verb is the science.
normal.cn: 一个 statistic，两个 statistics；statistics 接单数动词时就是这门学科。

normal.en: Statistical and statistician are the adjective and the person; the noun statistic stays countable.
normal.cn: statistical 是形容词，statistician 是从业者；名词 statistic 始终可数。

abstract.en: Imagine a beach of countless grains. A statistic is the one measured heap you scoop out and call 'average grain size'.
abstract.cn: 想象一片由无数沙粒组成的海滩。statistic 就是你舀起来、并称为“平均粒径”的那一撮测量结果。

abstract.en: A wall of numbers covers the screen; one cell is circled in red. The circled cell is the statistic.
abstract.cn: 整屏都是数字，其中一格被红笔圈出。被圈出的那一格就是 statistic。

abstract.en: A life entered as a single row in a table: that is the moment a person becomes a statistic.
abstract.cn: 一条生命被记进表格里的一行：那一刻，一个人就成了 statistic。

examples.en: The report's most striking statistic is the doubling of rents.
examples.cn: 报告中最触目的统计数字是租金翻倍。

examples.en: Statistics is the tool she uses to test the claim.
examples.cn: 统计学是她检验这一说法的工具。

examples.en: Victims of the fire were soon reduced to statistics in the news.
examples.cn: 火灾受害者在新闻里很快被化成了数字。

dict_mnemonic.text: “死盯数据”——死盯一堆数据，最后盯出一个统计量 → statistic 统计量、统计数据

root: 拉丁语 status“状态、状况”（来自 stare“站立”）→ 新拉丁语 statisticus“国家事务的”→ 德语 Statistik“国家状况之学”→ 英语 statistics → 逆构 statistic；核心是“从国家状态的数据里取出的一项”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of statistic: one calculated figure, one quoted data point, the science, the body of data, a comparative measure, a sports record, a person turned into a number, and the grammar that keeps them apart.
sensesIntro.cn: statistic 的八个义项：一个算出的数值、一项被引用的数据、一门学科、一批数据、一个比较指标、一项体育记录、一个被化成数字的人，以及把它们区分开的语法边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one measured number is lifted out of a mass of data to stand for the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一个庞大的数据堆里，取出一个测得的数字来代表整体。

branches.en: MEASURE: a calculated value makes a mass of data comparable.
branches.cn: 度量：一个计算值让一堆数据变得可比较。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE: statistics names the science that produces such figures.
branches.cn: 学科：statistics 命名生产这些数值的学问。

branches.en: DATA: the plural also names the collected numbers themselves.
branches.cn: 数据：复数形式也指收集起来的数字本身。

branches.en: REPORT: a figure is quoted in news, research, or sport.
branches.cn: 报告：数字被引用于新闻、研究或体育。

branches.en: REDUCTION AND BOUNDARY: a person can become a statistic, and singular versus plural marks the difference.
branches.cn: 化约与边界：人可以变成一个 statistic，而单数与复数标记出差别。

intro.en: English builds the whole family from statistics: -ics names the discipline, -al makes the adjective, -ly the adverb, and -ian the person. The Latin stem status stays inside but is not a live English prefix.
intro.cn: 英语整族词都从 statistics 长出：-ics 命名学科，-al 构成形容词，-ly 构成副词，-ian 指从业者。拉丁词干 status 藏在里面，但不是活的英语前缀。

latinIntro.en: The classical family is the stare 'to stand' group: status, state, station, constant, and stable all describe standing or being fixed.
latinIntro.cn: 这一古典词族是 stare“站立”组：status、state、station、constant、stable 都描述站立或固定。

items.meaning: the science of collecting and interpreting data
items.meaningCN: 统计学（-ics 构成学科名）
items.example: Statistics has its own department now.
items.exampleCN: 统计学现在有自己的系了。

items.meaningCN: 统计的；统计学的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: They reported a statistical rise in cases.
items.exampleCN: 他们报告病例在统计上有所上升。

items.meaning: according to statistics; in statistical terms
items.meaningCN: 从统计上看（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Statistically, the two groups are alike.
items.exampleCN: 从统计上看，这两个群体是相似的。

items.structure: statistic + -ian (person who works in a field)
items.meaning: a person who studies or applies statistics
items.meaningCN: 统计学家；统计员（-ian 指从业者）
items.example: The statistician checked the sampling method.
items.exampleCN: 统计员核查了抽样方法。

items.meaning: a standing, a position, a state
items.example: The noun ties the word to the standing family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把该词系到“站立”词族。

items.structure: stem of Latin stare and status
items.example: The stem appears in status, statue and statistic.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 status、statue 与 statistic。

items.meaning: the discipline ending; statistics came first, statistic was cut back from it
items.meaningCN: 学科词尾；先有 statistics 这门学科，statistic 是它的逆构截短
items.example: The ending names the discipline, and the singular was cut back from it.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾命名学科，单数形式是从学科名逆构截短而来。

items.example: It forms statistical, relating to statistics.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 statistical，即与统计有关的。

items.meaning: one who works in a field
items.example: It forms statistician, a person trained in statistics.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 statistician，即统计学家。

latinEntries.meaning: rank or condition
latinEntries.meaningCN: 地位；状态

latinEntries.structure: Old French estat, from Latin status
latinEntries.meaning: condition; a political unit
latinEntries.meaningCN: 状态；国家；州

latinEntries.structure: Latin statio 'a standing place', from stare
latinEntries.meaning: a stopping place; a post
latinEntries.meaningCN: 车站；岗位（站立之地）

latinEntries.meaning: standing firm; unchanging
latinEntries.meaningCN: 恒定的；持续的（站得住不变）

definition_zh: 地位；身份；状态；状况；（正式的）情形
definition_en: the position or rank of someone or something in relation to others, or the current condition of a situation or process
core_image: 一个人站在社会阶梯的哪一级，以及他此刻站成的样子
scene: 机场值机柜台前，工作人员刷新航班信息。The screen showed that the flight's status had changed to delayed, and the passenger was allowed to change her ticket.
sceneCN: 这里 status 是「状态」（第 3 个义项：某事物在某一刻的状况）；句意：屏幕显示航班状态已变成“延误”，旅客因此获准改签。图中可辨识物件：值机柜台、航班信息屏、登机牌、排队旅客。

pos.zh: 地位；身份；状态；状况

senses.title: Social rank: where one stands among others
senses.titleCN: 社会地位：在他人之间所站的位置
senses.definition: the rank or position of a person or group in relation to other people, especially in a society
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体相对于他人所处的等级或位置，尤指在社会中的
senses.example: Her family's status rose sharply after the marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 婚后她家的社会地位骤然上升。
senses.why: Latin status is a noun of standing, from stare 'to stand'. The first sense is spatial before it is social: where you stand in a ranked order is your status.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 status 是“站立”的名词，来自 stare“站”。第一个义项在成为社会概念之前先是空间概念：你在一个有等级的顺序里站在哪里，就是你的 status。

senses.title: Official or legal standing
senses.definition: the official category that a person or thing is placed in by an authority, such as marital, refugee, or employment status
senses.definitionCN: 权威机构把个人或事物归入的正式类别，如婚姻、难民或就业身份
senses.example: Applicants must prove their legal status in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 申请人必须证明自己在该国的合法身份。
senses.why: An authority assigns the position rather than measuring it. Status becomes a label entered in a register, so the word now means a formal category.
senses.whyCN: 这里的位置由权威机构指派，而不是测量得出。status 变成登记册里的一个标签，因此词义转为正式类别。

senses.title: Current condition of a thing or process
senses.titleCN: 事物或过程当前的状态
senses.definition: the condition of a process, device, or situation at a particular moment
senses.definitionCN: 过程、设备或情形在某一特定时刻的状况
senses.example: The flight status changed from delayed to boarding.
senses.exampleCN: 航班状态从“延误”变成了“登机”。
senses.why: The 'way of standing' can describe a thing rather than a person: a flight, a patient, or a machine stands in some condition right now. This is the condition branch.
senses.whyCN: “站立的方式”也可以描述物而非人：航班、病人或机器此刻“站”在某种状况里。这就是“状况”分支。

senses.title: Prestige: status as a valued thing
senses.definition: high rank or prestige, especially when it is displayed or desired
senses.definitionCN: 较高的等级或威望，尤指被展示或被追求时
senses.example: The watch is bought mainly for status.
senses.exampleCN: 买这块表主要是为了身份感。
senses.why: Rank is neutral, but rank can be desired. When the position itself becomes a possession, status means prestige, and objects can carry it.
senses.whyCN: 等级本身是中性的，但等级会被人渴求。当位置本身变成一种所有物，status 就指威望，物品也能承载它。

senses.title: Status quo: the existing state
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase status quo, the existing state of affairs, especially when seen as something to preserve
senses.definitionCN: 固定短语 status quo 中指事物的现有状态，尤指被视为应当维持的状态
senses.example: Both sides agreed to keep the status quo for another year.
senses.exampleCN: 双方同意再维持一年现状。
senses.why: The Latin phrase means 'the state in which'. English keeps the whole phrase, and quo fixes the reference to what currently stands.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁短语意为“处于其中的状态”。英语保留整条短语，quo 把所指锁定为当下站立着的样子。

senses.title: Technical standing in a system of classification
senses.titleCN: 分类体系中的技术性地位
senses.definition: in biology or law, the recognized standing of a name, species, or case within an official system
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学或法律中，名称、物种或案件在官方体系里被承认的地位
senses.example: The species now has the status of a protected animal.
senses.exampleCN: 该物种现在具有受保护动物的地位。
senses.why: Every classification assigns places. Status here is not prestige but a slot in a system, and the slot carries legal or scientific consequences.
senses.whyCN: 每一种分类都在分配位置。这里的 status 不是威望，而是体系中的一个槽位，而这个槽位带有法律或科学后果。

senses.title: Machine-readable state: computing
senses.titleCN: 机器可读的状态：计算机用法
senses.definition: in computing, the condition of a process, account, or request, often reported as a code
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中指进程、账户或请求的状况，常以代码形式报告
senses.example: The server returned a status code of 404.
senses.exampleCN: 服务器返回了 404 状态码。
senses.why: A system reports where a request 'stands' at a given moment. The old standing image survives in a purely technical register.
senses.whyCN: 系统会报告一个请求在某一刻“站在”哪一步。古老的“站立”意象在纯技术语域里存活下来。

senses.title: Usage boundary: status vs state
senses.definition: status usually means relative standing or an official category; state means the general condition of someone or something, and also a political unit
senses.definitionCN: status 通常指相对地位或正式类别；state 指人或事物的一般状况，同时也可指政治单位（国家、州）
senses.example: His status as a citizen is secure, but his health state is poor.
senses.exampleCN: 他的公民身份稳固，但健康状况很差。
senses.why: Both descend from stare, but English split the work: status keeps the ranked or official position, while state covers condition and polity. Stable, from the same root, adds 'standing firm'.
senses.whyCN: 两者都出自 stare，但英语做了分工：status 保留“有等级或正式的位置”，state 覆盖“状况”与“政体”。同根的 stable 则添上“站得稳”。

intro.en: Status is a Latin noun of standing, not a French loan. Latin status 'manner of standing, position, condition' comes from stare 'to stand'. English borrowed it around 1700 and later gave it the social sense. It is a cousin of stable and state, but not their synonym.
intro.cn: status 是拉丁语中表示“站立”的名词，不是法语借词。拉丁语 status“站立方式、位置、状况”来自 stare“站立”。英语约在 1700 年借入，后来发展出社会地位义。它与 stable、state 同源，但不是同义词。

items.en: Latin status is a verbal noun from stare 'to stand, stand firm'. Its oldest sense is 'manner of standing', then 'position, place', then 'condition, state'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 status 是来自 stare“站立、站稳”的动名词。最古老的义项是“站立方式”，再是“位置、地方”，再是“状况、状态”。

items.en: stare also gives stabilis 'firm', statio 'a standing place', and constare 'to stand together'. English stable, station, and constant descend from these; stable means 'standing firm', status means 'standing somewhere'.
items.cn: stare 还给出 stabilis“牢固的”、statio“站立之地”、constare“站在一起”。英语 stable、station、constant 由此而来；stable 是“站得稳”，status 是“站在某处”。

items.en: Status enters English around 1700, first as a learned term for position or standing. The social and official senses develop in the 18th and 19th c.; the exact first date of each sense is uncertain.
items.cn: status 约在 1700 年进入英语，最初是表示“位置、地位”的书面学术词。社会义与官方义在 18、19 世纪发展出来；各义项的确切首见年代存疑。

items.en: Sociology and law turn status into a technical concept: status versus contract (Maine), and later ascribed versus achieved status. The word now names a position inside a system, not just a place in space.
items.cn: 社会学与法学把 status 变成技术概念：status 与 contract 相对（梅因），后来又有所属地位与获致地位之分。这个词从此指体系内的位置，而不只是空间中的地点。

items.en: The base *sta- 'to stand' is generally accepted for this family, though the exact pre-Latin forms are reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: 这一词族的底层 *sta-“站立”属于一般认为，不过拉丁语之前的具体形式是重构的，并无实证。

items.en: Status is not statistic: status is the standing itself, statistic is one figure taken from data about the state. Nor is it state: status is ranked or official position, state is general condition or a polity.
items.cn: status 不是 statistic：status 是所站的状态本身，statistic 是从关于国家的数据中取出的一个数值。它也不是 state：status 是有等级或正式的位置，state 是一般状况或政体。

note.en: The first group is root-and-form neighbours from stare. The second group separates position, condition, rank, and the esteem that rank can attract.
note.cn: 第一组是出自 stare 的词根与词形邻居。第二组把位置、状况、等级，以及等级带来的敬重分开。

entries.definition: a condition, or a political unit. It covers condition and polity, while status covers rank and official standing.
entries.definitionCN: 状况，或政治单位。它覆盖状况与政体，而 status 覆盖等级与正式身份。

entries.definition: a carved or cast figure of a person or animal. Latin statua is 'something set up', from stare.
entries.definitionCN: 人或动物的雕像。拉丁语 statua 是“被立起来的东西”，出自 stare。

entries.definition: the science or body of data. It comes from the same status family but means figures, not standing.
entries.definitionCN: 统计学或一批数据。它同出 status 词族，但指数字，不指地位。

entries.definition: the physical state of a person or thing, especially regarding health or repair. It overlaps status only in the 'current state' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 人或物的物理状态，尤指健康或完好程度。它只在“当前状况”这一义项上与 status 重叠。

entries.definition: a position in a graded order, especially in the army or an organization. It is narrower and more countable than status.
entries.definitionCN: 分级顺序中的位置，尤指军队或组织中的级别。它比 status 更窄、更可数。

entries.definition: a person's reputation or position in a group, often earned. It stresses how others judge you, while status can be assigned.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人在群体中的声誉或位置，常是挣得的。它强调他人的评价，而 status 可以被指派。

entries.definition: the respect and admiration attached to success or high rank. It is the esteem side of status, not the position itself.
entries.definitionCN: 成功或高等级带来的尊敬与仰慕。它是 status 的“敬重”一面，而不是位置本身。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: status is a bare Latin noun from stare 'to stand', with state, station, stable, and constant as true relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：status 是来自 stare“站立”的纯拉丁名词，state、station、stable、constant 都是真正的同族词。

normal.en: stare 'to stand' → status 'standing'. Your status is where you stand in the order.
normal.cn: stare“站” → status“站立状态”。你的 status 就是你在顺序里站的位置。

normal.en: stable and status are siblings: stable is 'standing firm', status is 'standing somewhere'.
normal.cn: stable 与 status 是兄弟：stable 是“站得稳”，status 是“站在某处”。

normal.en: state and status split the work: state = condition or polity, status = rank or official category.
normal.cn: state 与 status 分工：state = 状况或政体，status = 等级或正式类别。

normal.en: status quo is the whole Latin phrase 'the state in which'; quo locks the reference to what stands now.
normal.cn: status quo 是完整的拉丁短语“处于其中的状态”；quo 把所指锁定为当下站立的样子。

normal.en: social status, marital status, flight status are three branches: rank, official label, current condition.
normal.cn: social status、marital status、flight status 是三条分支：等级、官方标签、当前状况。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase. Status is not the step you are on but the fact that others can see which step it is.
abstract.cn: 想象一级级台阶。status 不是你所站的那一级本身，而是“别人看得见你站在哪一级”这件事。

abstract.en: A label stuck to a file: 'approved'. The file has not changed, but its official status has.
abstract.cn: 一张贴在档案上的标签，写着“已批准”。档案本身没变，变的只是它的官方 status。

abstract.en: A water-level mark on a wall: status is a reading taken at one moment, not the river itself.
abstract.cn: 墙上的一道水位线：status 是某一刻读取的数值，而不是河流本身。

examples.en: The scholarship is open to all students, regardless of status.
examples.cn: 这项奖学金对所有学生开放，不论身份地位。

examples.en: Please check the status of your application online.
examples.cn: 请在线查询你的申请状态。

examples.en: The reforms changed the legal status of migrant workers.
examples.cn: 这些改革改变了外来务工者的法律身份。

dict_mnemonic.text: “使塔特”——把人“使”到塔顶（塔特），站得最高 → status 地位、身份

root: 拉丁语 status“站立方式、位置、状况”，来自 stare“站立”；核心是“站在哪里、以什么姿态站着”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of status, all one standing image: social rank, official label, current condition, prestige, the status quo, a place in a classification, a machine state, and the boundary with state.
sensesIntro.cn: status 的八个义项都是同一幅“站立”图：社会等级、官方标签、当前状况、威望、现状、分类体系中的位置、机器状态，以及与 state 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something stands at a particular place, and that place is visible to others.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物站在某个特定位置，而这个位置是别人看得见的。

branches.en: RANK: the vertical place one occupies among others.
branches.cn: 等级：在他人之间所占的纵向位置。

branches.en: OFFICIAL STANDING: an authority assigns a slot, and the slot has consequences.
branches.cn: 官方身份：权威机构指派一个槽位，槽位带有后果。

branches.en: CONDITION: a person, flight, or process stands in some state at this moment.
branches.cn: 状况：人、航班或进程此刻站在某种状态里。

branches.en: ESTEEM AND PRESERVATION: rank becomes prestige, and the status quo is what still stands.
branches.cn: 敬重与维持：等级变成威望，而 status quo 是仍然站立着的现状。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: status keeps rank and official labels; state keeps condition and polity.
branches.cn: 边界：status 保留等级与官方标签；state 保留状况与政体。

intro.en: Status takes no living English suffix; its family grows by compounds and fixed phrases. The Latin noun is borrowed whole, so the morphology below is phrase-building rather than derivation.
intro.cn: status 不接活的英语后缀；它的家族靠复合词和固定短语扩展。这个拉丁名词是整体借入的，因此下面的构词是“造短语”而不是派生。

latinIntro.en: The classical family is the stare 'to stand' group: status, state, station, stable, constant, and exist all describe some kind of standing.
latinIntro.cn: 这一古典词族是 stare“站立”组：status、state、station、stable、constant、exist 都描述某种“站立”。

items.meaning: more than one status; the regular English plural
items.meaningCN: 多个地位或状态（-es 构成英语常规复数）
items.example: The database stores several statuses for each order.
items.exampleCN: 数据库为每个订单保存多个状态。

items.meaningCN: 现状（拉丁语 quo“在其中”固定搭配）
items.example: They chose the status quo over another reform.
items.exampleCN: 他们选择维持现状，而不是再来一次改革。

items.meaning: an object that shows the owner's high rank
items.example: In that neighbourhood, a large garden is a status symbol.
items.exampleCN: 在那个街区，大花园是身份的象征。

items.meaning: a short report on the current state of something
items.example: The project manager posts a weekly status update.
items.exampleCN: 项目经理每周发布一次状态更新。

items.example: The verb supplies the standing behind status.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 status 背后的“站立”。

items.example: The stem appears in state, station and status.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 state、station 与 status。

items.example: The ending keeps status looking Latin in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾让 status 在英语里仍像拉丁词。

items.structure: Old French estat, from Latin status
items.example: The family estate passed to the elder son.
items.exampleCN: 家族地产传给了长子。

items.example: The statutory limit is two weeks.
items.exampleCN: 法定上限是两周。

latinEntries.structure: Old French estat, from Latin status
latinEntries.meaning: condition; a political unit
latinEntries.meaningCN: 状态；国家；州

latinEntries.meaning: a stopping place; a post
latinEntries.meaningCN: 车站；岗位（站立之地）

latinEntries.meaning: steady; not likely to change
latinEntries.meaningCN: 稳定的；稳固的（站得稳）

latinEntries.meaning: standing firm; unchanging
latinEntries.meaningCN: 恒定的；持续的（站住不变）

definition_zh: 战略；策略；计谋；统筹全局的谋划
definition_en: a plan designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim, or the art of planning and directing such moves
core_image: 将军在地图上调动整支军队的那只手
scene: 围棋进入中盘，选手长考后改变整体策略。He gave up the small corners and surrounded the centre instead, and that change of strategy decided the game.
sceneCN: 这里 strategy 是「战略、整体策略」（第 2 个义项：为达成总体目标的长期谋划）；句意：他放弃边角小利，改为围住中央，这次策略的改变决定了整盘棋。图中可辨识物件：棋盘、棋子、计时器、选手的手。

pos.zh: 战略；策略；计谋

senses.title: Generalship: the art of commanding a whole force
senses.titleCN: 统帅术：指挥整支力量的技艺
senses.definition: the art of planning and directing the overall movements of an army or other large force
senses.definitionCN: 筹划并指挥军队或其他庞大力量的总体行动的技艺
senses.example: The campaign is remembered for its bold strategy.
senses.exampleCN: 这场战役因大胆的统帅之术而被记住。
senses.why: Greek stratēgia meant the office of a general, from stratēgos 'general'. The word starts as a role, not a document: it is the general's whole art of command.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 stratēgia 指将军的职位，来自 stratēgos“将军”。这个词最初是一个角色，而不是一份文件：它是将军统率全局的整套技艺。

senses.title: A long-term plan for an overall aim
senses.titleCN: 为总体目标制定的长期计划
senses.definition: a plan that coordinates many actions over time in order to reach a major aim
senses.definitionCN: 为达成重大目标而在一段时间内协调许多行动的计划
senses.example: The company adopted a five-year strategy for growth.
senses.exampleCN: 公司采取了一项五年增长战略。
senses.why: The general's art becomes a written plan. The military image survives in the scale: many moves, one aim, a long horizon.
senses.whyCN: 将军的技艺变成一份书面计划。军事意象留在“规模”里：许多动作、一个目标、很长的时间跨度。

senses.title: A clever scheme or trick
senses.definition: a clever method or scheme used to get an advantage, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 为取得优势而用的巧妙方法或计谋，常用复数
senses.example: He tried every strategy to avoid the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他想尽各种办法来躲开这场会议。
senses.why: When the horizon shrinks, strategy can mean a personal trick. The word keeps its cunning edge from Greek warfare, but the battlefield is now an office or a family.
senses.whyCN: 当时间跨度缩短，strategy 可以指个人的小计谋。这个词从希腊战场带来的“机巧”锋芒仍在，只是战场换成了办公室或家庭。

senses.title: Overall plan in a game, as opposed to tactics
senses.titleCN: 棋局或比赛中的全局谋划（相对于战术）
senses.definition: in games and sport, the overall plan for winning, while tactics are the specific moves used to carry it out
senses.definitionCN: 在棋类与体育中，为取胜而定的总体方案；战术则是执行它的具体着法
senses.example: His strategy was to trade pieces early; his tactics won the endgame.
senses.exampleCN: 他的策略是早早兑子；他的战术赢下了残局。
senses.why: Greek warfare already opposed the general's overall plan to the officer's local manoeuvre. Strategy keeps the map; tactics keeps the next move.
senses.whyCN: 希腊战争早已把将军的总体谋划与军官的局部机动相对。strategy 看地图，tactics 看下一步。

senses.title: Game theory: a complete plan of choices
senses.titleCN: 博弈论：一套完整的选择方案
senses.definition: in game theory, a complete plan that specifies what a player will do in every possible situation
senses.definitionCN: 博弈论中，规定参与者在每一种可能情形下如何行动的完整方案
senses.example: A mixed strategy can be better than always choosing the same move.
senses.exampleCN: 混合策略可能优于总是选择同一步。
senses.why: The technical sense formalises the general's plan: not one decision, but a rule covering all contingencies. It is the most precise use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 技术义把将军的计划形式化：不是一个决定，而是一条覆盖所有可能情况的规则。这是该词最精确的用法。

senses.title: A method for learning or solving a problem
senses.titleCN: 学习或解决问题的策略
senses.definition: in education and psychology, a method deliberately used to understand, remember, or solve something
senses.definitionCN: 在教育与心理学中，为理解、记忆或解决某事而有意采用的方法
senses.example: Guessing from context is a useful reading strategy.
senses.exampleCN: 根据上下文猜测是一种有用的阅读策略。
senses.why: The scale drops again: the 'campaign' is now a learner's path through a text. The word still means a coordinated plan, only the terrain is cognitive.
senses.whyCN: 规模再次缩小：“战役”现在是一个学习者穿过文本的路径。词仍指协调过的计划，只是地形变成了认知层面。

senses.title: The field or doctrine of strategy
senses.definition: the academic or professional field that studies how overall aims should be pursued, especially in war, business, or politics
senses.definitionCN: 研究应如何追求总体目标的学术或专业领域，尤指战争、商业或政治中
senses.example: She teaches strategy at a business school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一所商学院教战略。
senses.why: Once a body of knowledge forms, the art becomes a subject. Uncountable strategy names the discipline, just as uncountable statistics names its science.
senses.whyCN: 一旦形成知识体系，技艺就变成学科。不可数的 strategy 命名这门学问，就像不可数的 statistics 命名它的学科。

senses.title: Usage boundary: strategy vs tactic vs plan
senses.definition: strategy is the overall long-term direction; tactics are the short-term moves that execute it; plan is the neutral word for any arranged series of steps
senses.definitionCN: strategy 是长期的总体方向；tactics 是执行它的短期动作；plan 是对任何安排好的步骤序列的中性说法
senses.example: The strategy was sound; the tactics failed; the plan was rewritten.
senses.exampleCN: 战略是稳妥的，战术失败了，计划被重写。
senses.why: Three words mark three altitudes: the map, the move, and the schedule. Strategy is the highest and the most purpose-driven of the three.
senses.whyCN: 三个词标记三个高度：地图、动作、日程。strategy 是三者中最高、也最受目标驱动的一层。

intro.en: Strategy is a Greek military word that climbed from the general's tent to the boardroom. Greek stratēgos 'general' joins stratos 'army' and agein 'to lead'; stratēgia is the general's office. English took the word through French in the early 19th c.
intro.cn: strategy 是一个从将军帐篷走进会议室的希腊军事词。希腊语 stratēgos“将军”由 stratos“军队”与 agein“引导”构成；stratēgia 指将军的职位。英语在 19 世纪初经法语借入。

items.en: Greek stratēgia means 'office or command of a general', and also 'generalship, the art of a commander'. It is an abstract noun built on stratēgos.
items.cn: 希腊语 stratēgia 意为“将军之职或统帅权”，也指“将道、统帅的技艺”。它是建立在 stratēgos 之上的抽象名词。

items.en: stratēgos 'general' = stratos 'army, host' + agein 'to lead, drive'. The general is literally the one who leads the host.
items.cn: stratēgos“将军”= stratos“军队、队伍”+ agein“引导、驱赶”。将军字面上就是“带领队伍的人”。

items.en: English strategy is recorded from around 1810, borrowed from French stratégie, which had taken the Greek word. The exact first date is uncertain; early uses are mostly military.
items.cn: 英语 strategy 约见于 1810 年，借自法语 stratégie，后者又从希腊语借入。确切首见年代存疑；早期用法多为军事。

items.en: The word extends from war to business, politics, and games in the 19th and 20th c. Game theory then gives it a formal sense: a complete plan of choices.
items.cn: 19、20 世纪，这个词从战争扩展到商业、政治与游戏。随后博弈论给出正式义：一套完整的选择方案。

items.en: stratos is often linked to a 'spread out' root and agein to *ag- 'to drive', but these deeper connections are generally accepted but partly uncertain, not established fact.
items.cn: stratos 常被联系到一个“铺开”的词根，agein 则联系到 *ag-“驱赶”，但这些更深层的联系属于一般认为且部分存疑，并非既定事实。

items.en: Strategy is not tactic: strategy is the overall direction, tactics are the moves. Nor is it a plan: a plan can be tactical and short, while strategy implies a long horizon and a major aim.
items.cn: strategy 不是 tactic：strategy 是总体方向，tactics 是具体动作。它也不等于 plan：plan 可以是短期战术性的，而 strategy 隐含长时段与重大目标。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek command family or looks close to it. The second group separates overall direction, immediate moves, a neutral plan, a policy line, and a cunning scheme.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊语“统帅”词族，或词形接近。第二组区分总体方向、即时动作、中性计划、政策路线与机巧计谋。

entries.definition: relating to strategy, or important for reaching an overall aim. It describes the quality, not the plan itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与战略有关的，或对达成总体目标至关重要的。它描述性质，而不是计划本身。

entries.definition: a person skilled in making strategies. The -ist suffix names the planner, not the plan.
entries.definitionCN: 善于制定战略的人。-ist 指谋划者，而不是谋划本身。

entries.definition: a trick or cunning plan to gain an advantage. Greek stratēgēma is a general's device, a much narrower word than strategy.
entries.definitionCN: 为取得优势而用的计谋。希腊语 stratēgēma 是将军的计策，比 strategy 窄得多。

entries.definition: a specific action used to carry out a plan. Tactics are the moves; strategy is the direction they serve.
entries.definitionCN: 为执行计划而采取的具体行动。tactics 是动作，strategy 是这些动作服务的总方向。

entries.definition: any arranged set of steps for doing something. It is neutral in scale; strategy implies a major, long-term aim.
entries.definitionCN: 为做某事而安排好的任何步骤集合。它对规模是中性的；strategy 隐含重大而长期的目标。

entries.definition: a settled line of action adopted by an organization or government. It is a rule to follow, while strategy is a direction to win.
entries.definitionCN: 组织或政府采取的既定行动路线。它是遵守的规则，而 strategy 是求胜的方向。

entries.definition: a systematic plan, often with a tone of cunning. British English uses it neutrally, but it colours strategy's trick branch.
entries.definitionCN: 系统性的计划，常带机巧意味。英式英语中性使用，但它渲染 strategy 的“计谋”分支。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: Greek stratos 'army' + agein 'to lead' = stratēgos 'general' → stratēgia 'generalship' → strategy. The -ic, -ist, -ize suffixes are English additions.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：希腊语 stratos“军队”+ agein“引导”= stratēgos“将军”→ stratēgia“将道”→ strategy。后缀 -ic、-ist、-ize 是英语添加的。

normal.en: stratos 'army' + agein 'to lead' = the one who leads the army. Strategy began as the general's job.
normal.cn: stratos“军队”+ agein“引导”= 带领军队的人。strategy 最初就是将军的活儿。

normal.en: strategy and stratagem are relatives: one is the whole art, the other is one general's trick.
normal.cn: strategy 与 stratagem 是同族：前者是整门技艺，后者是某位将军的一条计。

normal.en: strategic, strategist, strategize are the adjective, the person, and the verb; the noun strategy stays the plan or the art.
normal.cn: strategic、strategist、strategize 分别是形容词、人物名词和动词；名词 strategy 仍是计划或技艺。

normal.en: Strategy is the map; tactics are the next move. If it fits on one square, it is not strategy.
normal.cn: strategy 是地图；tactics 是下一步。如果它只装得下一个格子，那就不是 strategy。

normal.en: The word crossed from war to business: a marketing strategy is a campaign plan with a long horizon.
normal.cn: 这个词从战争跨到商业：a marketing strategy 就是一份长时段的战役计划。

abstract.en: Picture lines drawn across a whole map, not a single arrow. Strategy is the shape those lines make together.
abstract.cn: 想象画在整张地图上的许多条线，而不是一支箭头。strategy 是这些线共同构成的形状。

abstract.en: A path seen through fog: you cannot see the end, but the direction is chosen before the first step.
abstract.cn: 雾中的一条路：你看不到尽头，但在迈出第一步之前，方向已经选好。

abstract.en: The general's eye rises above the battlefield until the soldiers become pieces and the noise becomes a pattern.
abstract.cn: 将军的目光升到战场之上，直到士兵变成棋子，喧嚣变成图案。

examples.en: Their strategy is to enter the market through smaller cities first.
examples.cn: 他们的策略是先通过较小的城市进入市场。

examples.en: The coach changed tactics, but the overall strategy stayed the same.
examples.cn: 教练换了战术，但总体战略没变。

examples.en: Saving the strongest argument for the end was a good strategy.
examples.cn: 把最有力的论据留到最后，是个好策略。

dict_mnemonic.text: “死抓特基”——死抓关键（特基），先定大方向 → strategy 战略、策略

root: 希腊语 stratos“军队、队伍”+ agein“引导”= stratēgos“将军”，再派生 stratēgia“将军之职、统帅术”；核心是“统率全局的谋划”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of strategy, one rising viewpoint: the general's art, a long-term plan, a personal trick, the overall plan in a game, a formal plan in game theory, a learning method, the academic field, and the boundary with tactics.
sensesIntro.cn: strategy 的八个义项共享一个不断升高的视角：将军的技艺、长期计划、个人计谋、棋局的全局方案、博弈论的正式方案、学习方法、学术领域，以及与 tactics 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a commander looks down on the whole field and moves many parts toward one aim.
core.cn: 核心意象：统帅俯瞰整个战场，把许多部分调向同一个目标。

branches.en: COMMAND: the art and later the academic field of directing a whole force.
branches.cn: 统帅：指挥整支力量的技艺，后来成为学术领域。

branches.en: LONG-TERM PLAN: many coordinated actions aimed at one major goal.
branches.cn: 长期计划：许多协调动作指向一个重大目标。

branches.en: TRICK: the cunning edge of the military word applied to small personal gains.
branches.cn: 计谋：军事词的机巧锋芒被用在个人的小算盘上。

branches.en: GAME: the overall plan in a contest, formalised in game theory as a rule for every case.
branches.cn: 博弈：竞赛中的全局方案，在博弈论里形式化为覆盖所有情形的规则。

branches.en: METHOD AND BOUNDARY: a learning strategy is a plan for the mind, and tactics remain the short moves.
branches.cn: 方法与边界：学习策略是给头脑的计划，而 tactics 始终是短期动作。

intro.en: Strategy takes English suffixes freely: -ic makes the adjective, -ist the person, -ize the verb, -ally the adverb. The Greek stem stratēg- is the fixed core.
intro.cn: strategy 可以自由接英语后缀：-ic 构成形容词，-ist 指人，-ize 构成动词，-ally 构成副词。希腊词干 stratēg- 是固定的核心。

latinIntro.en: This family is Greek rather than Latin in origin, though the entries below are the classical elements that Latin and French passed on: stratos 'army', agein 'to lead', stratēgos 'general', stratēgia 'generalship'.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族在起源上是希腊语而非拉丁语；下面列出的，是经拉丁语和法语传下来的古典成分：stratos“军队”、agein“引导”、stratēgos“将军”、stratēgia“将道”。

items.meaning: relating to strategy; important for the overall aim
items.meaningCN: 战略的；对总体目标关键的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: The port is of great strategic value.
items.exampleCN: 这个港口具有重大的战略价值。

items.meaning: a person skilled in planning strategy
items.meaningCN: 战略家；善于谋划者（-ist 指从业或擅长的人）
items.example: The campaign was run by a seasoned strategist.
items.exampleCN: 这场竞选由一位老练的战略家操盘。

items.meaningCN: 制定战略；谋划（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The team met to strategize before the launch.
items.exampleCN: 团队在发布前开会谋划。

items.meaning: in a way that serves an overall aim
items.meaningCN: 在战略上；有策略地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The shop is strategically placed near the station.
items.exampleCN: 这家店在车站附近，位置很有策略。

items.example: The noun supplies the army half of strategy.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供 strategy 的“军队”一半。

items.example: The verb supplies the leading half of strategy.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 strategy 的“率领”一半。

items.example: The general is the person the word first named.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最早命名的就是将军。

items.example: It forms strategic, relating to overall planning.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 strategic，即与总体谋划有关的。

items.example: It forms strategist, one who makes strategy.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 strategist，即制定战略的人。

latinEntries.meaning: an army, a body of soldiers
latinEntries.meaningCN: 军队；队伍

latinEntries.meaning: to lead or drive
latinEntries.meaningCN: 引导；驱赶

latinEntries.meaning: a general, the leader of an army
latinEntries.meaningCN: 将军；军队的统领

latinEntries.meaning: the office or art of a general
latinEntries.meaningCN: 将军之职；统帅术

definition_zh: 压力；紧张；重音；强调；应力；强调；使紧张
definition_en: mental or physical pressure, special emphasis, the loudest part of a spoken word, force acting on a material, or to emphasize something
core_image: 一股从外面压过来的力，把东西挤紧
scene: 地震救援现场，队员已连续工作三十六小时。The commander could see the stress on every face and sent the teams out in shifts.
sceneCN: 这里 stress 是「心理压力」（第 2 个义项：情绪上的紧张与压迫感）；句意：指挥员看得出每张脸上的心理压力，于是安排队伍分批轮换。图中可辨识物件：救援头盔、担架、照明灯、疲惫的队员。

pos.zh: 压力；紧张；重音；强调；应力
强调；重读；使紧张

senses.title: Physical pressure on an object
senses.titleCN: 施加在物体上的物理压力
senses.definition: a force that presses, pulls, or compresses a physical object
senses.definitionCN: 压、拉或挤压一个物体的力
senses.example: The bridge collapsed under the stress of the floodwater.
senses.exampleCN: 桥梁在洪水的压力下坍塌了。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin strictus 'tight, compressed'. The oldest image is something squeezed: a beam, a rope, a structure bearing a load.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 strictus“紧的、压紧的”。最古老的画面是某物被挤紧：一根梁、一条绳、一座承重的结构。

senses.title: Mental or emotional pressure
senses.definition: a feeling of strain and worry caused by difficult demands or threats
senses.definitionCN: 由困难要求或威胁引起的紧张与担忧感
senses.example: Long hours and tight deadlines caused serious stress.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间工作和紧迫的截止日期造成了严重的压力。
senses.why: The 20th-century sense transfers the squeeze inward: pressure is no longer on a beam but on a person's mind. This is a later branch, not the original meaning.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的义项把“挤紧”转向内部：压力不再加在梁上，而加在人的心上。这是后起分支，不是本义。

senses.title: Special emphasis on an idea
senses.titleCN: 对某一观念的特别强调
senses.definition: special importance or attention given to an idea, fact, or word
senses.definitionCN: 给予某个观念、事实或词语的特殊重要性或注意
senses.example: The report lays stress on prevention rather than cure.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告强调预防而非治疗。
senses.why: To put stress on something is to put weight on it. Emphasis is pressure applied in speech or argument, so the physical image becomes rhetorical.
senses.whyCN: 把 stress 放在某物上，就是给它加重量。强调是施加在言语或论证上的压力，物理意象由此变成修辞意象。

senses.title: Linguistic stress: the strong beat of a word
senses.titleCN: 语言学重音：词里的强拍
senses.definition: the greater force used on one syllable of a word or one word in a phrase
senses.definitionCN: 在词的一个音节或短语的一个词上使用的更强力度
senses.example: In 'record', the stress falls on the first syllable as a noun.
senses.exampleCN: record 作名词时，重音落在第一个音节。
senses.why: Air is pressed out harder on one syllable. The word names the loudest beat, which is literally a local increase of pressure.
senses.whyCN: 在某个音节上，气流被更用力地压出。这个词命名最响的那一拍，字面上就是局部压力的增加。

senses.title: To emphasize something
senses.definition: to say or show that something is especially important
senses.definitionCN: 说明或显示某事特别重要
senses.example: She stressed that the deadline could not move.
senses.exampleCN: 她强调截止日期不能改。
senses.why: The verb converts the noun's 'weight' into an act: you place the weight yourself. Emphasis is something a speaker does, not something a word has.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的“重量”转化为动作：重量由你亲手放上去。强调是说话者做的事，而不是词自带的东西。

senses.title: To make someone anxious
senses.definition: in informal usage, to make someone feel worried or anxious
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，使某人感到担忧或焦虑
senses.example: Don't stress me about the tickets; I'll handle it.
senses.exampleCN: 别拿票的事让我紧张，我会处理。
senses.why: The verb turns the mental-pressure sense outward: one person becomes the source of the squeeze. The subject now applies the stress to someone else.
senses.whyCN: 动词把“心理压力”义转向外部：一个人成了挤压的来源。主语现在把压力施加到别人身上。

senses.title: Engineering stress: force per unit area
senses.titleCN: 工程应力：单位面积上的力
senses.definition: in mechanics, the internal force per unit area inside a material, distinct from strain, which is the resulting deformation
senses.definitionCN: 力学中指材料内部单位面积上的内力，与表示形变的 strain 不同
senses.example: The steel is designed to withstand a stress of 400 megapascals.
senses.exampleCN: 这种钢被设计成能承受 400 兆帕的应力。
senses.why: Engineering makes the word precise: stress is the force, strain is the shape change it causes. The everyday 'pressure' becomes a measurable quantity.
senses.whyCN: 工程学让这个词精确化：stress 是力，strain 是它造成的形状改变。日常的“压力”变成可测量的量。

senses.title: Usage boundary: stress, strain, pressure, anxiety
senses.definition: stress is the load or the internal response to it; strain is the deformation or the effort of enduring; pressure is an external force or urgent demand; anxiety is the emotional worry itself
senses.definitionCN: stress 是负荷或对负荷的内部反应；strain 是形变或承受的努力；pressure 是外部力量或紧迫要求；anxiety 是情绪上的担忧本身
senses.example: The pressure from the client produced strain in the team, and the stress showed as anxiety.
senses.exampleCN: 客户的压力让团队产生消耗，而这种压力表现为焦虑。
senses.why: All four come from squeezing, but each keeps a different part of the image: the load, the deformation, the push from outside, and the worry inside.
senses.whyCN: 四个词都来自“挤压”，但各自保留意象的不同部分：负荷、形变、外部推力、内部担忧。

intro.en: Stress began as a word for hardship and tight pressure, not for psychology. Middle English stresse came from Old French estrece 'narrowness, oppression', from Vulgar Latin *strictia, from Latin strictus 'tight', the past participle of stringere 'to tighten, graze'. The mental sense is a 20th-century extension.
intro.cn: stress 最初指困苦与紧紧的压迫，而不是心理状态。中古英语 stresse 来自古法语 estrece“狭窄、压迫”，再上溯通俗拉丁语 *strictia，源自拉丁语 strictus“紧的”，即 stringere“勒紧、擦过”的过去分词。心理义是 20 世纪的延伸。

items.en: stresse is recorded meaning 'hardship, distress, oppression, force'. It also covers the sense of a tight or narrow passage. The modern spelling stress settles later.
items.cn: stresse 有记录的意思是“困苦、悲痛、压迫、力量”，也涵盖“狭窄通道”之义。现代拼写 stress 后来才固定。

items.en: From Old French estrece 'narrowness, oppression', related to estroit 'narrow, tight' (Modern French étroit).
items.cn: 来自古法语 estrece“狭窄、压迫”，与 estroit“狭窄的、紧的”相关（现代法语 étroit）。

items.en: Vulgar Latin *strictia 'tightness' is built on Latin strictus 'tight, compressed', the past participle of stringere 'to tighten, bind, graze'.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语 *strictia“紧”建立在拉丁语 strictus“紧的、压紧的”之上，后者是 stringere“勒紧、捆绑、擦过”的过去分词。

items.en: stringere also gives strict, stringent, strain, distress, and restrict. All carry the image of drawing tight or pressing hard.
items.cn: stringere 还给出 strict、stringent、strain、distress、restrict。它们都带着“拉紧或压紧”的意象。

items.en: Engineering adopts stress for internal force per area in the 19th c. The psychological sense develops in the early 20th c. and spreads widely after the 1930s; this is the latest branch, not the oldest.
items.cn: 工程学在 19 世纪用 stress 表示单位面积的内力。心理学义在 20 世纪初发展，1930 年代后广泛传播；这是最晚的分支，不是最古老的含义。

items.en: The deeper root *streig- 'to press, stroke' is generally accepted for this family, but the reconstruction is not certain in every detail. Stress is not related to strategy or structure.
items.cn: 这一词族更深层的词根 *streig-“压、擦”属于一般认为，但重构并非每个细节都确定。stress 与 strategy、structure 没有词源关系。

note.en: The first group shares the stringere 'tighten' root or looks close to it. The second group separates the load, the deformation, the outside push, the spoken beat, and the emotional worry.
note.cn: 第一组共享 stringere“拉紧”词根，或词形接近。第二组区分负荷、形变、外部推力、口语重音与情绪担忧。

entries.definition: extreme sadness, pain, or difficulty. The prefix dis- adds 'apart', so the tightness becomes a tearing apart.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的悲伤、痛苦或困境。前缀 dis- 添上“分开”，紧的状态变成被撕开。

entries.definition: a severe demand on strength or resources, or the deformation caused by stress. It is the effort or the shape change, not the load itself.
entries.definitionCN: 对体力或资源的严苛要求，或应力造成的形变。它是承受的努力或形状改变，而不是负荷本身。

entries.definition: demanding obedience; exact. It comes from strictus 'tight', the same participle behind stress.
entries.definitionCN: 要求服从的；严格的。它来自 strictus“紧的”，与 stress 同出这一个过去分词。

entries.definition: a force pressing on something, or an urgent demand from outside. Pressure is often the cause; stress is the load or the response.
entries.definitionCN: 压在某物上的力，或来自外部的紧迫要求。pressure 常是因，stress 是负荷或反应。

entries.definition: a stretched or strained state, physical or social. It is the pulling image, while stress is the pressing image.
entries.definitionCN: 被拉紧或紧张的状态，物理上或人际上。它是“拉”的意象，而 stress 是“压”的意象。

entries.definition: special importance given to a word or idea. It overlaps stress only in the emphasis and pronunciation senses.
entries.definitionCN: 给予词或观念的特殊重要性。它只在“强调”和“发音”义项上与 stress 重叠。

entries.definition: a feeling of worry or unease. It names the emotion itself, while stress can name the cause, the state, or the response.
entries.definitionCN: 担忧或不安的感受。它命名情绪本身，而 stress 可以指原因、状态或反应。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: Latin strictus 'tight' → *strictia → Old French estrece → Middle English stresse. The English suffixes -ful, -ed, -or, and the compound -free build the modern family.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：拉丁语 strictus“紧的”→ *strictia → 古法语 estrece → 中古英语 stresse。英语后缀 -ful、-ed、-or 与复合成分 -free 构成现代词族。

normal.en: strictus means 'tight'. Stress is the state of being squeezed tight, first a rope, then a mind.
normal.cn: strictus 意为“紧的”。stress 就是被挤紧的状态，先是一根绳，后来是一颗心。

normal.en: strict, stringent, strain, distress, restrict all share the tighten root; only the prefix or ending changes the direction.
normal.cn: strict、stringent、strain、distress、restrict 都共享“拉紧”词根，只是前缀或词尾改变了方向。

normal.en: Stress as a beat in a word is a local squeeze of air: the loud syllable gets more pressure.
normal.cn: stress 作为词里的强拍，是空气的局部挤压：响亮的音节承受更多压力。

normal.en: Two verb branches: stress a point = put weight on it; stress a person = put weight on them.
normal.cn: 两个动词分支：stress a point = 给观点加重量；stress a person = 给人加重量。

normal.en: The psychological sense is recent. In older texts, stress means hardship or force, not burnout.
normal.cn: 心理义是晚近的。在较早的文本里，stress 指困苦或力量，而不是现代意义上的“累垮”。

abstract.en: A beam bends under a load. The stress inside it is invisible, yet it is what holds or breaks the whole building.
abstract.cn: 一根梁在负荷下弯曲。它内部的应力看不见，却决定整栋楼是撑住还是断裂。

abstract.en: A foot lands on one syllable of a sentence, and the ground gives slightly. That landing is stress.
abstract.cn: 一只脚落在句子的某个音节上，地面微微下沉。那次落地就是 stress。

abstract.en: A rubber band pulled almost to its limit: still whole, but every fibre is tightened. That is the quiet picture behind the word.
abstract.cn: 一根被拉到极限的橡皮筋：还没断，但每根纤维都绷紧了。这就是这个词背后的安静画面。

examples.en: Exercise is one of the best ways to reduce stress.
examples.cn: 运动是减轻压力的最佳方式之一。

examples.en: The teacher stressed the difference between fact and opinion.
examples.cn: 老师强调了事实与观点的区别。

examples.en: The material failed because the stress exceeded its limit.
examples.cn: 材料失效是因为应力超过了极限。

dict_mnemonic.text: “死拽死”——死拽死拉，越拉越紧 → stress 压力、紧张

root: 拉丁语 strictus“紧的、压紧的”（stringere“勒紧、擦过”的过去分词）→ 通俗拉丁语 *strictia → 古法语 estrece → 中古英语 stresse；核心是“被压紧的状态”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of stress, one squeeze: force on a beam, strain on a mind, weight on an idea, a beat in a word, the act of emphasizing, the act of worrying someone, force per area in engineering, and the boundary with strain and pressure.
sensesIntro.cn: stress 的八个义项都是同一种“挤压”：加在梁上的力、加在心上的紧绷、加在观念上的重量、词里的强拍、强调的动作、让别人紧张的动作、工程上的单位面积力，以及与 strain、pressure 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an outside force squeezes something tight, and the tightness shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股外力把某物挤紧，而紧绷显现出来。

branches.en: PHYSICAL LOAD: force on a beam or a material, measured per unit area in engineering.
branches.cn: 物理负荷：加在梁或材料上的力，工程上按单位面积计量。

branches.en: MENTAL LOAD: the squeeze moves inward, and one person can also apply it to another.
branches.cn: 心理负荷：挤压转向内部，一个人也能把它施加到别人身上。

branches.en: EMPHASIS: weight placed on an idea, as noun or as verb.
branches.cn: 强调：加在观念上的重量，名词与动词皆可。

branches.en: SPEECH: a local squeeze of air makes one syllable the strong beat.
branches.cn: 语音：空气的局部挤压让某个音节成为强拍。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: stress is the load, strain the deformation, pressure the outside push, anxiety the worry.
branches.cn: 边界：stress 是负荷，strain 是形变，pressure 是外部推力，anxiety 是担忧。

intro.en: English builds stress into adjectives and nouns with -ful, -ed, -or, and the combining form -free. The Latin stem strict- stays inside but is not productive in English.
intro.cn: 英语用 -ful、-ed、-or 以及组合成分 -free 把 stress 构成形容词和名词。拉丁词干 strict- 藏在内部，但在英语中不能产。

latinIntro.en: The classical family is the stringere 'to tighten' group: strict, stringent, strain, distress, and restrict all describe drawing tight or pressing hard.
latinIntro.cn: 这一古典词族是 stringere“拉紧”组：strict、stringent、strain、distress、restrict 都描述拉紧或压紧。

items.meaningCN: 压力大的；令人紧张的（-ful 表示“充满”）
items.example: It was a stressful week at the hospital.
items.exampleCN: 那是医院里压力很大的一周。

items.meaningCN: 焦虑的；承受压力的（-ed 分词作形容词）
items.example: She looked tired and stressed.
items.exampleCN: 她看上去疲惫而焦虑。

items.meaningCN: 压力源；应激因素（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: Noise is a common stressor in open offices.
items.exampleCN: 噪音是开放式办公室里常见的压力源。

items.meaningCN: 无压力的；轻松的（-free 表示“没有”）
items.example: They planned a stress-free weekend by the sea.
items.exampleCN: 他们安排了一个海边无压力周末。

items.example: The verb is the tightening behind stress and strict.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 stress 与 strict 背后的“拉紧”。

items.example: The stem appears in strict, restrict and constrict.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 strict、restrict 与 constrict。

items.example: Engineering strain measures the same kind of pull.
items.exampleCN: 工程里的应变量的也是同一类拉力。

items.example: It forms stressful, full of stress.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 stressful，即充满压力的。

items.example: The storm caused widespread distress.
items.exampleCN: 风暴造成了大范围的困苦。

latinEntries.meaning: demanding obedience; exact
latinEntries.meaningCN: 严格的；精确的（被勒紧、不留余地）

latinEntries.structure: Latin stringent-, present participle of stringere
latinEntries.meaning: strict and severe; tight
latinEntries.meaningCN: 严厉的；紧缩的（勒得很紧）

latinEntries.structure: Old French estreindre, from Latin stringere
latinEntries.meaning: to stretch tight; severe effort
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉紧；竭力（被拉到极限）

latinEntries.meaning: extreme pain or difficulty
latinEntries.meaningCN: 极度痛苦；困境（被拉开、撕裂）

definition_zh: 结构；构造；建筑物；体系；组织；构建
definition_en: the way parts are arranged and joined to form a whole, a built thing, an organized system, or to arrange parts into a whole
core_image: 一块一块材料按次序叠起来、拼成一个立得住的整体
scene: 桥梁合龙前夜，工程师逐一核对钢梁。He checked how each diagonal brace was joined and how the load was shared, because the structure had to hold for a hundred years.
sceneCN: 这里 structure 是「结构」（第 1 个义项：各部分如何排列连接成一个整体）；句意：他核对每根斜撑如何连接、荷载怎样分担，因为这个结构要撑一百年。图中可辨识物件：钢梁、斜撑、连接节点、工程图纸。

pos.zh: 结构；构造；建筑物；体系
组织；安排；构建

senses.title: The arrangement of parts in a whole
senses.titleCN: 各部分在整体中的排列方式
senses.definition: the way the parts of something are arranged and connected to each other
senses.definitionCN: 某物各部分相互排列与连接的方式
senses.example: The structure of the molecule explains its unusual colour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个分子的结构解释了它不寻常的颜色。
senses.why: Latin structura is 'a fitting together', from struere 'to pile, build'. The core sense is not the thing but the arrangement: which part sits where, and what holds it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 structura 意为“拼合”，来自 struere“堆叠、建造”。核心义不是东西本身，而是排列：哪一部分在哪儿，靠什么连住。

senses.title: A built object: building or framework
senses.definition: a thing that has been built, such as a building, bridge, or tower
senses.definitionCN: 已经建成的东西，如建筑物、桥梁或塔
senses.example: The old structure was replaced by a glass tower.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧建筑被一座玻璃高塔取代。
senses.why: When the arrangement is made of stone or steel, the word shifts from pattern to object. A structure is a whole that was deliberately put together.
senses.whyCN: 当排列由石头或钢铁做成，词义就从“图案”转向“物体”。structure 就是被有意拼合起来的整体。

senses.title: An organized system in society or an institution
senses.titleCN: 社会或机构中的组织体系
senses.definition: the organized pattern of relationships or parts in a society, organization, or system
senses.definitionCN: 社会、组织或体系中关系与部分的组织化模式
senses.example: The reform changed the structure of local government.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革改变了地方政府的结构。
senses.why: The building image is abstracted: roles are the parts, rules are the joints. Social structure is a building you cannot see.
senses.whyCN: 建筑意象被抽象化：角色是部件，规则是接缝。社会结构是一座看不见的建筑。

senses.title: The organization of a text or argument
senses.titleCN: 文章或论证的组织方式
senses.definition: the order and arrangement of sections, points, or ideas in a piece of writing or speech
senses.definitionCN: 文章或讲话中各部分、要点或观点的顺序与安排
senses.example: A clear structure makes a long essay easier to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 清晰的结构让长文更容易读。
senses.why: Parts become paragraphs and joints become transitions. The same question applies: what holds this together and in what order?
senses.whyCN: 部件变成段落，接缝变成过渡。同一个问题仍然适用：是什么把这些连住，按什么次序？

senses.title: Technical arrangement in biology or chemistry
senses.titleCN: 生物或化学中的技术性构造
senses.definition: the internal arrangement of cells, organs, atoms, or molecules in a natural object
senses.definitionCN: 自然物体内部细胞、器官、原子或分子的排列构造
senses.example: The structure of the cell wall was mapped in detail.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞壁的结构被详细绘制出来。
senses.why: Science asks how nature builds. The word keeps its 'put together' meaning but loses the human builder: the arrangement is given, not designed.
senses.whyCN: 科学追问自然如何“建造”。这个词保留“拼合”义，却去掉了人类建造者：排列是给定的，而不是设计出来的。

senses.title: To arrange or organize something deliberately
senses.titleCN: 有意地组织或安排某事
senses.definition: to plan and arrange the parts of something so that it works as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 计划并安排某物的各部分，使其作为整体运作
senses.example: She structured the course around weekly projects.
senses.exampleCN: 她围绕每周项目来组织这门课。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: the arrangement is no longer found, it is made. The builder now appears in the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：排列不再是被发现的，而是被制造的。建造者此时出现在句子里。

senses.title: Computing: an organized way to store data
senses.titleCN: 计算机：组织数据的方式
senses.definition: in computing, a defined way of storing and linking data so that it can be used efficiently
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中为高效使用而定义的数据存储与连接方式
senses.example: A hash table is a common data structure.
senses.exampleCN: 哈希表是一种常见的数据结构。
senses.why: Data also has parts and joints. The technical sense keeps the pure arrangement meaning, with no physical building at all.
senses.whyCN: 数据同样有部件与接缝。技术义保留纯粹的“排列”含义，完全不涉及实体建筑。

senses.title: Usage boundary: structure, construction, framework, infrastructure
senses.definition: structure is the arrangement or a built thing; construction is the act or industry of building; framework is a supporting skeleton; infrastructure is the basic public systems a society runs on
senses.definitionCN: structure 是排列方式或建成之物；construction 是建造行为或建筑业；framework 是支撑性的骨架；infrastructure 是社会运转所依赖的基础公共系统
senses.example: The construction of the bridge took years; its structure is sound, but the transport infrastructure still lags.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥建了很多年；它的结构是稳固的，但交通基础设施仍然落后。
senses.why: Four words separate what is built, the act of building, the supporting frame, and the public base. Structure is the most general: it can be a pattern, an object, or a system.
senses.whyCN: 四个词分别指向“建成之物”“建造行为”“支撑骨架”“公共底座”。structure 最泛：它可以是图案、物体或体系。

intro.en: Structure comes from Latin structura 'a fitting together, building', from struere 'to pile up, build, arrange'. It belongs to the struere family (construct, instruct, destroy), not to the stare 'stand' family that gives status and stable. Latin structura passed through Old French into English in the late 14th c.
intro.cn: structure 来自拉丁语 structura“拼合、建造、建筑”，源自 struere“堆叠、建造、安排”。它属于 struere 词族（construct、instruct、destroy），而不属于产出 status、stable 的 stare“站立”词族。拉丁语 structura 经古法语于 14 世纪晚期进入英语。

items.en: Latin structura means 'a fitting together, building, construction', and also the arrangement itself. It is a noun of result built on the past participle structus.
items.cn: 拉丁语 structura 意为“拼合、建造、施工”，也指排列本身。它是建立在过去分词 structus 之上的结果名词。

items.en: struere 'to pile up, build, arrange, devise' has the past participle structus. Its compounds include construere 'heap together' and instruere 'build in, equip'.
items.cn: struere“堆叠、建造、安排、设计”的过去分词是 structus。它的复合词包括 construere“堆在一起”和 instruere“在内搭建、装备”。

items.en: struere is traced to PIE *streu- 'to spread out, strew, heap up', which is generally accepted. Relatives may include strew, straw, and stratum, though the exact links are reconstructed.
items.cn: struere 被追溯到原始印欧语 *streu-“铺开、撒、堆积”，这属于一般认为。同族可能包括 strew、straw、stratum，不过具体联系是重构的。

items.en: English structure is recorded from the late 14th c. meaning 'the act of building' and 'a building'. It came through Old French, which had borrowed Latin structura.
items.cn: 英语 structure 最早记录于 14 世纪晚期，意为“建造行为”和“建筑物”。它经由古法语借入，古法语又从拉丁语借来 structura。

items.en: The word extends to anatomy, language, and society: the structure of a body, a sentence, or a state. The verb 'to structure' is a later, mostly 19th-20th c. development.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到解剖、语言与社会：身体的结构、句子的结构、国家的结构。动词“to structure”是较晚的发展，主要在 19、20 世纪。

items.en: Structure is not a derivative of stare. status and stable come from stare 'to stand'; structure comes from struere 'to pile'. The resemblance in spelling is accidental, and the two families mean different things: standing versus building.
items.cn: structure 不是 stare 的派生词。status 与 stable 来自 stare“站立”；structure 来自 struere“堆叠”。拼写相似是偶然的，两个词族的意思也不同：站立 versus 建造。

note.en: The first group shares the struere 'build' root or looks close to it. The second group separates an arrangement, the act of building, a supporting frame, a composition, and an organized system.
note.cn: 第一组共享 struere“建造”词根，或词形接近。第二组区分排列方式、建造行为、支撑骨架、构成成分与组织体系。

entries.definition: to build or put together. It is the verb of building, while structure is the arrangement or the built result.
entries.definitionCN: 建造；拼合。它是“建造”的动词，而 structure 是排列方式或建成结果。

entries.definition: to teach or give orders. Latin instruere meant 'build in, equip', so instruction builds knowledge into a mind.
entries.definitionCN: 教导；指示。拉丁语 instruere 意为“在内搭建、装备”，所以 instruction 是把知识搭进头脑。

entries.definition: relating to structure or to the basic parts of a system. It describes the arrangement, not a particular building.
entries.definitionCN: 与结构或系统基本部分有关的。它描述排列，而不是某一座建筑。

entries.definition: a supporting frame or a set of basic ideas. It is the skeleton that other parts hang on, while structure is the whole arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑框架或一套基本观念。它是其他部分赖以悬挂的骨架，而 structure 是整体排列。

entries.definition: the process or business of building. Structure is the result or the pattern; construction is the activity that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 建造的过程或行业。structure 是结果或模式；construction 是产生它的活动。

entries.definition: the parts or ingredients that make up a whole. It stresses materials and proportions more than their connections.
entries.definitionCN: 构成整体的部分或成分。它更强调材料与配比，而不是它们之间的连接。

entries.definition: the way parts are arranged for a purpose, or a body so arranged. It overlaps structure in the social and institutional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的而排列各部分的方式，或如此组织起来的机构。它在社会与机构义项上与 structure 重叠。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: Latin struere 'to pile, build' → structus → structura → structure. English adds -al, -ally, -ed, and re- + -ing.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：拉丁语 struere“堆叠、建造”→ structus → structura → structure。英语添加 -al、-ally、-ed，以及 re- + -ing。

normal.en: struere means 'to pile up'. A structure is what you get when parts are piled and joined in a order.
normal.cn: struere 意为“堆叠”。structure 就是各部分被按次序堆起、连接之后得到的东西。

normal.en: construct, instruct, destroy, obstruct all contain struere; each prefix changes what is piled or un-piled.
normal.cn: construct、instruct、destroy、obstruct 都含有 struere；每个前缀改变“堆起”还是“拆开”。

normal.en: structure is not from stare. status and stable stand; structure piles. Similar spelling, different family.
normal.cn: structure 不出自 stare。status 与 stable 是“站”，structure 是“堆”。拼写相似，词族不同。

normal.en: The noun is the pattern or the building; the verb is the act of arranging. Same letters, builder included or not.
normal.cn: 名词是模式或建筑物；动词是安排的动作。同样的字母，有时含建造者，有时不含。

normal.en: -ure makes a result noun, -al makes the adjective, -ed makes 'having a structure', and restructuring means building again.
normal.cn: -ure 构成结果名词，-al 构成形容词，-ed 表示“具有结构的”，restructuring 则是“重新搭建”。

abstract.en: A tower of blocks: each block is ordinary, but their positions decide whether the tower stands. Structure is the positions, not the blocks.
abstract.cn: 一座积木塔：每块积木都很普通，但它们的位置决定塔是否站得住。structure 是位置，不是积木。

abstract.en: A cross-section drawing outlives the building it describes: the lines are the arrangement that stone only happens to fill.
abstract.cn: 一张剖面图比它描述的建筑物活得更久：线条才是排列本身，石头只是恰好填充了它。

abstract.en: A skeleton under skin: invisible from outside, yet it decides the shape of everything you can see.
abstract.cn: 皮肤下的一副骨架：从外面看不见，却决定了你能看到的一切形状。

examples.en: The structure of the family has changed over two generations.
examples.cn: 家庭结构在两代人之间发生了变化。

examples.en: He structured his answer around three clear points.
examples.cn: 他围绕三个清晰的要点来组织回答。

examples.en: The engineer found a crack in the structure of the roof.
examples.cn: 工程师在屋顶的结构中发现了裂缝。

dict_mnemonic.text: “死抓车架”——死抓车架不放，因为车架就是整车的结构 → structure 结构、构造

root: 拉丁语 structura“拼合、建造、建筑”，来自 struere“堆叠、建造、安排”（过去分词 structus）；核心是“把分散的部分堆叠拼合成一个整体”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of structure, one act of putting together: an arrangement of parts, a built object, a social system, a text's order, a natural construction, the act of organizing, a data arrangement, and the boundary with construction and framework.
sensesIntro.cn: structure 的八个义项都是同一种“拼合”：各部分的排列、建成之物、社会体系、文章次序、自然构造、组织动作、数据安排，以及与 construction、framework 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate parts are piled and joined in an order that can stand as one whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：分散的部分被按某种次序堆起、连接，作为一个整体立住。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENT: the order of parts, whether in a molecule, a sentence, or an essay.
branches.cn: 排列：各部分的次序，无论在分子、句子还是文章里。

branches.en: BUILT THING: when the arrangement is made of stone or steel, it becomes an object.
branches.cn: 建成之物：当排列由石头或钢铁做成，它就变成一个物体。

branches.en: SYSTEM: roles and rules, or data and links, form an invisible structure.
branches.cn: 体系：角色与规则，或数据与连接，构成看不见的结构。

branches.en: NATURE: biology and chemistry describe arrangements that were not designed by a builder.
branches.cn: 自然：生物与化学描述并非由建造者设计的排列。

branches.en: ACTION AND BOUNDARY: the verb makes the arrangement, and construction names the act of building it.
branches.cn: 动作与边界：动词制造排列，而 construction 命名建造它的行为。

intro.en: Structure takes -al for the adjective, -ally for the adverb, -ed for 'having a structure', and re- + -ing for building again. The Latin stem struct- stays fixed underneath.
intro.cn: structure 接 -al 构成形容词，-ally 构成副词，-ed 表示“具有结构的”，re- + -ing 表示“重新搭建”。拉丁词干 struct- 固定在底层。

latinIntro.en: The classical family is the struere 'to pile, build' group: construct, instruct, destroy, and obstruct all describe putting together or taking apart.
latinIntro.cn: 这一古典词族是 struere“堆叠、建造”组：construct、instruct、destroy、obstruct 都描述拼合或拆开。

items.meaning: relating to structure or to basic parts
items.meaningCN: 结构的；结构性的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The building has a structural weakness.
items.exampleCN: 这座建筑有结构性缺陷。

items.meaningCN: 在结构上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two designs are structurally similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两种设计在结构上相似。

items.meaning: having a clear or deliberate structure
items.meaningCN: 有结构的；结构化安排的（-ed 分词作形容词）
items.example: The interview followed a structured format.
items.exampleCN: 面试按结构化的流程进行。

items.meaning: the act of organizing something in a new way
items.meaningCN: 重组；结构调整（re- 表“重新”，-ing 构成动作名词）
items.example: The company announced a major restructuring.
items.exampleCN: 公司宣布了一项重大重组。

items.example: The verb is the building behind structure and construct.

senses.title: A pointed pen for wax tablets
senses.definition: a pointed instrument used for writing or scratching on wax or clay
senses.definitionCN: 用于在蜡板或泥板上书写、刻划的尖头工具
senses.example: The Roman student wrote with a stilus on a wax tablet.
senses.exampleCN: 那名罗马学生用尖笔在蜡板上写字。
senses.why: The Latin stilus was first a physical pointed stake. Writing was scratching marks with that stake, so the tool existed before the manner it produced.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 stilus 最初指一根有尖头的桩。书写就是用这根桩刻出痕迹，因此先有工具，才有工具留下的“方式”。

senses.title: The look of written words
senses.definition: a particular manner of writing, including word choice and sentence structure
senses.definitionCN: 写作或书写的特定方式，包括用词与句式
senses.example: Her letters have a formal, measured style.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书信有一种正式而克制的文风。
senses.why: Once the pen makes marks, those marks have a recognisable shape. The trace of the tool becomes the writer's manner, which is why style first meant writing before it meant anything else.
senses.whyCN: 笔一旦留下痕迹，这些痕迹就有可辨认的形状。工具的痕迹变成了写作者的方式，所以 style 最早的引申义是“写法、文风”。

senses.title: A way of doing things
senses.definition: a distinctive way of behaving, working, or dealing with people
senses.definitionCN: 为人处事、工作或与人打交道的特有方式
senses.example: His style of management is to listen first and decide later.
senses.exampleCN: 他的管理风格是先听意见、后作决定。
senses.why: The 'trace' is no longer on paper: repeated actions leave a recognisable pattern just as repeated strokes leave a recognisable hand.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“痕迹”已不在纸上：反复的行动会留下可辨认的模式，正如反复的笔画会留下可辨认的笔迹。

senses.title: Fashion and elegance
senses.definition: a fashionable or elegant manner of dress, speech, or living
senses.definitionCN: 穿着、言谈或生活方式中时髦、优雅的方式
senses.example: The hotel is short on style but strong on comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店不太讲究格调，但舒适度很高。
senses.why: In the 17th and 18th centuries style spread from writing to dress and social life. Whatever is done in a marked, admired way can be called a style.
senses.whyCN: 17、18 世纪，style 从书写扩展到衣着与社交生活。任何以明显而受人赞赏的方式做出来的事，都可以叫一种 style。

senses.title: Cut and design: clothes and hair
senses.definition: a particular cut, shape, or design given to clothes, hair, or objects
senses.definitionCN: 赋予衣服、头发或器物的特定剪裁、形状或设计
senses.example: She asked the hairdresser for a shorter style.
senses.exampleCN: 她请理发师给她剪一个更短的款式。
senses.why: A design is a shape deliberately impressed on material, exactly as a pen impresses a shape on wax. The old gesture of the stilus survives in the noun.
senses.whyCN: 设计就是有意把某种形状压进材料里，正如笔在蜡上压出形状。尖笔的古老动作在这个名词义里留存下来。

senses.title: To design or shape something
senses.definition: to design, shape, or arrange something in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 按特定方式设计、塑形或布置某物
senses.example: The chef styled the salad with edible flowers.
senses.exampleCN: 主厨用可食用花装饰这道沙拉。
senses.why: The noun's 'impressed shape' turns into the act of impressing it. The verb keeps the original gesture: a hand gives material a visible form.
senses.whyCN: 名词里“被压出的形状”转为“压出形状”的动作。动词保留了最初的手势：手给材料一个看得见的形式。

senses.title: The stalk of a pistil
senses.definition: the narrow part of a pistil between the ovary and the stigma
senses.definitionCN: 雌蕊中连接子房与柱头的细长部分
senses.example: Pollen grains land on the stigma and grow down the style.
senses.exampleCN: 花粉落在柱头上，再沿花柱向下生长。
senses.why: Latin stilus also meant 'stake, stalk'. Botanists reused the old 'pointed post' image for the flower's upright column.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 stilus 也指“桩、茎”。植物学家借用了这个古老的“尖柱”意象，来命名花中直立的柱状结构。

senses.title: To be styled: named or titled
senses.definition: to give someone or something a title or name, often in the phrase be styled
senses.definitionCN: 给某人或某物一个称号或名称，常用于 be styled 结构
senses.example: The building is styled 'the eighth wonder of the world'.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑被称为“世界第八大奇迹”。
senses.why: A title is a mark publicly attached to a person, like a written label. The 'inscription' branch of stilus survives in this formal usage.
senses.whyCN: 称号是公开贴在一个人身上的标记，就像写上去的标签。stilus 的“书写、铭刻”分支在这个正式用法里保留下来。

senses.title: The shared look of a period or group
senses.definition: the body of shared visual conventions that identify a period, school, or artist
senses.definitionCN: 标识某一时代、流派或艺术家的一组共同视觉惯例
senses.example: The exhibition traces the Gothic style across three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这场展览梳理了哥特风格三个世纪的演变。
senses.why: When many hands repeat the same trace, the manner becomes a collective mark. Art history turned that collective trace into a category.
senses.whyCN: 当许多只手重复同一种痕迹，这种方式就成了集体的标记。艺术史把这种集体痕迹提升为一个分类概念。

intro.en: Style comes from Latin stilus, a pointed writing stick, and also 'manner of writing'. The Greek stylos 'pillar' is a different word: it influenced the 16th-century spelling, not the origin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: style 来自拉丁语 stilus，指书写用的尖笔，也指“书写方式”。希腊语 stylos“柱子”是另一个词：它影响的是 16 世纪的拼写，而不是词源。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Stilus meant a pointed instrument for writing on wax, a stake or goad, and by extension the manner of writing. The spelling stylus is a later variant.
items.cn: stilus 指在蜡板上书写用的尖器、尖桩或刺棒，并引申指书写方式。拼写 stylus 是后来的变体。

items.en: Old French estile, stile passed into Middle English in the 14th century. English first used it for the writing tool, then for 'manner of writing'.
items.cn: 古法语 estile、stile 在 14 世纪进入中古英语。英语先用它指书写工具，再指“写法、文风”。

items.en: The spelling was changed to style under the influence of Greek stylos 'pillar'. This is an orthographic fashion, not a change of source: the word remains stilus.
items.cn: 拼写在希腊语 stylos“柱子”的影响下改成 style。这是拼写风气，不是词源改变：这个词仍然出自 stilus。

items.en: Style extended from writing to dress, speech and social life, taking the sense 'fashionable or elegant manner'. 'In style' belongs to this period.
items.cn: style 从书写扩展到衣着、言谈和社交生活，取得“时髦、优雅的方式”这一义。短语 in style 属于这一时期。

items.en: Design and craft senses grew: the cut of clothes, the shape of hair, a period style in art history. The verb 'to style' became common in fashion and advertising.
items.cn: 设计与工艺义发展起来：衣服的剪裁、发型的样式、艺术史中的时代风格。动词 style 在时尚与广告业变得常用。

items.en: Style now covers personal manner, design, art-historical categories and computing style sheets. The through-line is still 'a recognisable way of leaving a mark'.
items.cn: 现代 style 覆盖个人作风、设计、艺术史分类以及计算机的样式表。贯穿始终的仍是“留下可辨认痕迹的方式”。
