note.cn: 下面两组把“拼写相近”与“意思接近”分开。先看词形与读音，再看词义。

entries.definition: a set of steps used to climb over a fence. It comes from Old English stigel, not from Latin stilus.
entries.definitionCN: 翻越篱笆用的阶梯。它来自古英语 stigel，与拉丁 stilus 无关。

entries.definition: a pointed writing tool, especially for tablets or digital screens. It is the same Latin stilus, respelled.
entries.definitionCN: 尖头书写工具，尤指用于手写板或电子屏的触控笔。它正是同一个拉丁词 stilus 的改拼形式。

entries.definition: a painful swelling on the eyelid. It is unrelated to style and only looks similar in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 眼睑上的疼痛性肿胀（麦粒肿）。它与 style 没有词源关系，只是书写形近。

entries.definition: the prevailing custom in dress or behaviour. It stresses what is currently accepted, while style stresses a distinctive manner.
entries.definitionCN: 衣着或行为中当下流行的风尚。它强调当下被接受的东西，而 style 强调有辨识度的方式。

entries.definition: a way of doing or behaving. It is broader and less evaluative than style.
entries.definitionCN: 做事或行为的方式。它比 style 更宽泛，也更少评价色彩。

entries.definition: a particular way or method, often technical, as in mode of transport. It is less about personal expression than style.
entries.definitionCN: 特定的方式或方法，常用于技术语境，如交通方式。它比 style 更少涉及个人表达。

entries.definition: a category of art or writing with shared conventions. Style is the individual treatment within or across genres.
entries.definitionCN: 具有共同惯例的艺术或写作类别。style 则是类型内部或跨类型的个人处理方式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实短语和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Stilus was a pointed stick. The word began as the pen, not as the manner, so the tool comes first and the trace comes second.
normal.cn: stilus 是一根尖桩。这个词最初指笔，而不是指方式：先有工具，后有痕迹。

normal.en: A style is what a pen leaves behind: the same tool, different traces. That is why writing was the first extended sense.
normal.cn: style 是笔留下的东西：同样的工具，不同的痕迹。正因如此，“书写”才是它最早的引申义。

normal.en: Style and stylus are the same word twice: English style, and the revived Latin stylus for digital pens.
normal.cn: style 与 stylus 是同一个词的两次出现：英语 style，以及为电子笔复活的拉丁语 stylus。

normal.en: In art history, Gothic style and Baroque style name a shared set of traces left by many hands.
normal.cn: 在艺术史里，哥特风格、巴洛克风格指的是许多只手留下的共同痕迹。

normal.en: Stylish does not mean 'full of style' literally; it means 'having the admired manner'.
normal.cn: stylish 并不是字面上的“充满风格”，而是“具有受人赞赏的方式”。

abstract.en: Picture a single stroke of ink: the stroke is the manner, not the matter. Style is the shape of the doing.
abstract.cn: 想象一道墨迹：这道墨迹是方式，而不是内容。风格就是“做”的形状。

abstract.en: Style is a shadow cast by repeated action: you see the pattern, not the hand that made it.
abstract.cn: 风格是反复行动投下的影子：你看见的是模式，而不是做出它的那只手。

abstract.en: Write the same sentence in three hands: the words match, the traces differ. Style is the difference.
abstract.cn: 用三种笔迹写同一句话：字相同，痕迹不同。风格就是那个差别。

examples.en: The two sisters have completely different styles of answering questions.
examples.cn: 两姐妹回答问题的风格完全不同。

examples.en: This building is a fine example of Victorian style.
examples.cn: 这座建筑是维多利亚风格的优秀范例。

examples.en: She styled her hair in a loose wave for the interview.
examples.cn: 为面试她把头发做成松散的波浪造型。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“斯泰尔”——斯泰尔先生每次出场都换一种造型 → style 风格、款式

root: 源自拉丁 stilus“书写用的尖笔、尖桩”，也指“书写方式”；英语 14 世纪先指书写工具，后指写法、文风，再泛化为风格。16 世纪拼写受希腊 stylos“柱子”影响改为 style，词源仍是 stilus。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of style, all built on one image: a pointed tool leaves a recognisable trace. The trace moves from wax to writing, to behaviour, to dress, to design, to shared period looks.
sensesIntro.cn: style 的九个义项都建立在一个意象上：尖头工具留下可辨认的痕迹。痕迹从蜡板移到文字，再移到行为、衣着、设计，最后成为时代共同的外观。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pointed pen leaves a recognisable trace on wax; the trace, not the tool, becomes the style.
core.cn: 核心意象：尖笔在蜡上留下可辨认的痕迹；成为“风格”的是痕迹，而不是工具。

branches.en: TOOL AND STALK: the physical pointed thing, whether a pen or a flower's upright column.
branches.cn: 工具与柱茎：那个有尖头的实体，既可以是一支笔，也可以是花中直立的柱状结构。

branches.en: TRACE AND COLLECTIVE TRACE: one writer's mark, then a period's shared mark.
branches.cn: 痕迹与集体痕迹：先是一个写作者的标记，后来是一个时代共同的标记。

branches.en: ACTION AND MANNER: repeated doing becomes a pattern, and the verb impresses that pattern on material.
branches.cn: 行动与方式：反复的做成为模式，而动词则是把这种模式压进材料里。

branches.en: SOCIAL SURFACE: dress, hair and objects carry the admired manner.
branches.cn: 社会表面：衣着、发型与器物承载着受人赞赏的方式。

branches.en: LABEL: a title is a mark publicly attached to a name.
branches.cn: 标签：称号是公开贴在名字上的标记。

intro.en: Style is a borrowed noun and verb. English adds -ish, -ist, -ize and -istic; the Latin base stilus is frozen and is not a living English prefix.
intro.cn: style 是借入的名词兼动词。英语在其后加 -ish、-ist、-ize、-istic；拉丁词基 stilus 已经凝固，不是活的英语前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around stilus is small: stilus 'stake, pen', the respelled variant stylus, and Italian stiletto. Greek stylos 'pillar' is a different word and affected only the spelling.
latinIntro.cn: 围绕 stilus 的拉丁词族很小：stilus“桩、笔”、改拼变体 stylus，以及意大利语 stiletto。希腊语 stylos“柱子”是另一个词，只影响了拼写。

items.meaning: fashionable and elegant; having the admired manner
items.meaningCN: 时髦的；有格调的（-ish 表示“具有……性质的”）
items.example: He wore a stylish black coat to the opening.
items.exampleCN: 他穿了一件时髦的黑色外套去参加开幕式。

items.meaning: a person who arranges hair or clothes; also a writer admired for style
items.meaningCN: 造型师；文体家（-ist 表示从事该活动的人）
items.example: The stylist chose a simple dress for the ceremony.
items.exampleCN: 造型师为典礼选了一条简洁的裙子。

items.structure: style + -ize (make or treat in a way)
items.meaning: to represent something in a simplified or exaggerated style
items.meaningCN: 使风格化；按某种风格简化或夸张地表现（-ize 表示“使……化”）
items.example: The film stylizes the city into blocks of pure colour.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影把城市风格化成一块块纯色。

items.meaning: relating to style, especially in writing or art
items.meaningCN: 文体的；风格上的（-istic 表示“与……有关的”）
items.example: The editor made only stylistic changes.
items.exampleCN: 编辑只做了风格上的改动。

items.example: The noun is the direct source of style.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 style 的直接来源。

items.structure: Latin variant spelling and English noun
items.meaning: a pointed writing tool; a needle
items.example: The stylus marks the wax surface.
items.exampleCN: 尖笔在蜡面上留下痕迹。

items.example: It forms stylish, having style.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 stylish，即有格调的。

items.example: It forms stylist, one who shapes style.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 stylist，即设计或讲究风格的人。

items.example: It forms stylize, to treat in a chosen style.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 stylize，即按某种风格处理。

latinEntries.meaning: the original pointed writing tool and the source of English style
latinEntries.meaningCN: 最初的尖头书写工具，也是英语 style 的来源

latinEntries.meaning: a pointed pen, now especially a digital pen for a screen
latinEntries.meaningCN: 尖笔，现多指用于屏幕的触控笔

latinEntries.meaning: a small dagger; also a thin high heel
latinEntries.meaningCN: 短剑；也指细高跟

latinEntries.structure: stilus → Old French stile → English style
latinEntries.meaning: the English descendant, first the pen, then the manner
latinEntries.meaningCN: 英语中的后代词，先指笔，再指方式

definition_zh: 提交；呈递；屈服；服从；提出（证据、论点）；接受（检查、治疗）
definition_en: to hand in something for official consideration, or to yield to a power, rule, or process
core_image: 一双手把文件或自己放到对方面前、低于对方的位置——递上去，也低下去
scene: 投稿截止前，研究生把修改后的论文上传到期刊系统。She pressed the button to submit the paper at ten that night, and the screen answered that it had been received.
sceneCN: 这里 submit 是「提交、呈递」（第 2 个义项：把文件交给机构审理）；句意：她在当晚十点按下按钮提交论文，屏幕随即回示已接收。图中可辨识物件：论文稿件、期刊投稿系统、截止日期、接收回执。

pos.zh: 提交；呈递；提出（证据、论点）
屈服；服从；接受（检查、治疗）（submit to）

senses.title: To yield to power
senses.definition: to accept the authority or power of someone stronger, often after resistance
senses.definitionCN: 接受更强者的权威或权力，常指经过抵抗之后
senses.example: The rebels finally submitted to the king.
senses.exampleCN: 叛军最终向国王屈服。
senses.why: Latin submittere meant 'to send under, lower'. The self is placed below the other, so yielding is the original physical gesture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 submittere 意为“送到下面、降低”。自我被放到他者之下，因此“屈服”是最初的身体动作。

senses.title: To hand in for consideration
senses.definition: to give a document, proposal, or application to an authority for review
senses.definitionCN: 把文件、方案或申请交给权威机构审阅
senses.example: Please submit your application by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 请在周五前提交申请。
senses.why: The object is sent under the authority's eyes. It travels upward in status while the hand that offers it moves down.
senses.whyCN: 物件被送到权威的眼下。它在地位上向上走，而递出它的那只手却向下低。

senses.title: To offer a plan or proposal
senses.definition: to present a plan, report, or proposal formally so that others may decide
senses.definitionCN: 正式提出计划、报告或方案，交由他人决定
senses.example: The committee submitted a revised budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会提交了一份修订后的预算。
senses.why: The same hand-over, now with a proposal whose fate lies with the receiver. The emphasis shifts from obeying to offering.
senses.whyCN: 还是同一次递交，只是所交之物变成方案，其命运掌握在接收者手里。重点从“服从”转到“呈上”。

senses.title: To undergo a test or treatment
senses.definition: to agree to be examined, tested, or treated, often something unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 同意接受检查、检验或治疗，常指不愉快的过程
senses.example: All applicants must submit to a medical examination.
senses.exampleCN: 所有申请人都必须接受体检。
senses.why: Here the self, not a document, is placed under a procedure. Submission is to a process rather than to a person.
senses.whyCN: 这里被放到程序之下的不是文件，而是自己。服从的对象从一个人变成了一道程序。

senses.title: To put forward evidence or an argument
senses.definition: in law or formal debate, to present evidence, a claim, or an argument for the record
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或正式辩论中，提交证据、主张或论点以供记录在案
senses.example: The defence submitted that the evidence was unreliable.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方提出该证据不可靠。
senses.why: The court is the authority; what is handed over is a statement to be weighed. The verb marks the formal register of the exchange.
senses.whyCN: 法庭是权威，交出的是供权衡的陈述。这个动词标明了这场交流的正式语域。

senses.title: To argue a point in formal speech
senses.definition: in the phrase I submit that, used in debates and courts to state an opinion politely
senses.definitionCN: 用于 I submit that，在辩论和法庭上礼貌地陈述观点
senses.example: I submit that the plan is too costly to defend.
senses.exampleCN: 我谨认为，这项计划成本过高，难以辩护。
senses.why: The speaker lowers himself before the assembly while still advancing a claim. Politeness and assertion share one verb.
senses.whyCN: 说话者在议会面前放低自己，同时仍在提出主张。礼貌与断言共用同一个动词。

senses.title: To give in to a feeling or temptation
senses.definition: to allow a desire or feeling to overcome one's resistance
senses.definitionCN: 任由欲望或情绪压倒自己的抵抗
senses.example: He submitted to despair after the third rejection.
senses.exampleCN: 第三次被拒后，他屈服于绝望。
senses.why: The self's resistance is what is placed below, and the winner is an inner force. The old 'yield' sense turns inward.
senses.whyCN: 被放到下方的是自我的抵抗，胜出者则是一股内在力量。古老的“屈服”义转向了内心。

senses.title: To subject something to a process
senses.definition: to cause something to be treated, measured, or tested by a process
senses.definitionCN: 使某物经受某种处理、测量或检验
senses.example: The alloy was submitted to extreme heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这种合金经受了极高温的处理。
senses.why: The object is sent under a procedure. This is the passive-technical edge of the same 'send under' image.
senses.whyCN: 物件被送到一道程序之下。这是同一个“送到下面”意象的被动、技术化边缘。

intro.en: Submit is a Latin verb borrowed whole: sub- 'under' + mittere 'send, let go'. The PIE root *mit- 'to send' is generally accepted, but its deeper origin is not settled.
intro.cn: submit 是整体借入的拉丁动词：sub-“在下”＋mittere“送、放”。原始印欧语词根 *mit-“送”属一般认为，但其更深来源尚无定论。

items.en: Submittere meant 'to lower, let down; to yield; to hand over'. The prefix sub- 'under' is spatial before it is social.
items.cn: submittere 意为“降低、放下；屈服；交出”。前缀 sub-“在下”先是空间意义，然后才是社会意义。

items.en: English first uses submit for 'to lower oneself, yield, be obedient', in religious and feudal contexts.
items.cn: 英语最早用 submit 表示“放低自己、屈服、服从”，见于宗教与封建语境。

items.en: The legal and diplomatic sense appears: to refer a case to a judge, to present something for a decision.
items.cn: 法律与外交义出现：把案件交由法官裁决，把某事呈交决定。

items.en: Everyday 'hand in a document or petition' develops. The modern bureaucratic sense takes shape alongside the older sense of yielding.
items.cn: 日常的“递交文件或请愿书”义发展起来。现代行政义与古老的“屈服”义并行成形。

items.en: Extended to applications, manuscripts and examinations, and to 'submit to treatment'. Computing adds 'submit a form'.
items.cn: 扩展到申请、稿件、考试，以及“接受治疗”。计算机领域又添“提交表单”。

items.en: PIE *mit- 'to send' is the usual reconstruction behind admit, permit, commit and transmit. The deeper root is uncertain, so only the 'send' layer is safe to state.
items.cn: 原始印欧语 *mit-“送”是 admit、permit、commit、transmit 背后通行的重构。更深层的词根不确定，因此只能稳妥地说到“送”这一层。

note.en: The groups below separate spelling neighbours from words with a close meaning. Form is checked first, then the kind of yielding or handing over involved.
note.cn: 下面两组把“拼写相近”与“意思接近”分开。先看词形，再看所涉及的屈服或递交方式。

entries.definition: the top of a mountain, or a high-level meeting. It comes from Latin summus 'highest', the opposite direction from sub-.
entries.definitionCN: 山峰之顶，或高层会议。它来自拉丁 summus“最高的”，与 sub- 方向相反。

entries.definition: a topic, or a person under a ruler. It shares sub- but takes jacere 'throw', not mittere 'send'.
entries.definitionCN: 主题，或统治者属下的人。它同样带 sub-，但词根是 jacere“投、掷”，不是 mittere“送”。

entries.definition: to include something under a larger category. It is sub- + sumere 'take', a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物归入更大的类别。它是 sub-＋sumere“取”，动词不同。

entries.definition: to give way under pressure. It is broader and often physical, while submit stresses accepting an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 在压力下让步。它更宽泛，常偏物理意义，而 submit 强调接受某种权威。

entries.definition: to hand over power or arms after defeat. It is more concrete and military than submit.
entries.definitionCN: 战败后交出权力或武器。它比 submit 更具体，军事色彩更浓。

entries.definition: to offer or hand in formally. It is neutral about power, whereas submit implies an authority above you.
entries.definitionCN: 正式提供或递交。它对权力关系保持中立，而 submit 暗示上方存在权威。

entries.definition: to offer formally a resignation, bid, or apology. It is very formal and often legal or commercial.
entries.definitionCN: 正式提出辞呈、投标或道歉。它非常正式，常用于法律或商业语境。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实短语和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Sub- means under and mittere means send: to submit is to send something under someone's authority.
normal.cn: sub- 意为“在下”，mittere 意为“送”：submit 就是把某物送到某人的权威之下。

normal.en: The same mittere family: admit lets in, permit lets through, transmit sends across, commit sends fully.
normal.cn: 同一个 mittere 词族：admit 放进来，permit 放通过，transmit 送过去，commit 完全交出去。

normal.en: Submit an application and submit to authority keep the two directions: the object goes up, the self goes down.
normal.cn: submit an application 与 submit to authority 保留两个方向：物件向上走，自我向下低。

normal.en: I submit that... is not a surrender but a polite lowering of the speaker before the assembly.
normal.cn: I submit that... 不是投降，而是说话者在议会面前礼貌地放低自己。

normal.en: In computing you submit a form: the button sends data to a server, a modern version of 'send under'.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，submit a form 是点按钮把数据送到服务器，这是“送到下面”的现代版本。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lowering a sheet onto a desk that is higher than the hand: the paper goes up in status and the hand goes down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把纸放到一张比手更高的桌上：纸的地位上升，手的位置下降。

abstract.en: Submission is a vector: the object travels toward authority while the self moves below it.
abstract.cn: 提交是一个向量：物件朝权威运动，同时自我移到它下方。

abstract.en: Reverse the arrow and you get 'undergo': instead of the self being lowered, the thing is sent into a process.
abstract.cn: 把箭头反过来就得到“经受”：不是自我被放低，而是物件被送进一道程序。

examples.en: You must submit the signed form to the office in person.
examples.cn: 你必须亲自把签好的表格交到办公室。

examples.en: The journal rejected the paper, so he submitted it elsewhere.
examples.cn: 那家期刊拒了论文，于是他把稿子投到了别处。

examples.en: The villagers refused to submit to the new tax.
examples.cn: 村民们拒绝服从这项新税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“萨布密特”——萨布把密件（mit）双手递到上司桌前 → submit 提交、呈递

root: 源自拉丁 submittere“降低、送交、使服从”＝sub-“在下”＋mittere“放、送”，核心是“把自己或物件送到下方／对方面前”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of submit, all one vector: something is sent under an authority or a process. What travels may be the self, a document, a proposal, evidence, a statement, or a material.
sensesIntro.cn: submit 的八个义项共用同一个向量：某物被送到权威或程序之下。被送去的可以是自我、文件、方案、证据、陈述或材料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand sends something downward, under the eyes of a higher authority.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把某物向下送，送到更高权威的眼下。

branches.en: SELF BELOW POWER: the self is lowered and the stronger party is accepted.
branches.cn: 自我低于权力：自我被放低，较强者被接受。

branches.en: INNER FORCE: the same lowering happens inside, where a feeling defeats resistance.
branches.cn: 内在力量：同样的“放低”发生在内心，情绪击败了抵抗。

branches.en: DOCUMENTS AND PROPOSALS: papers and plans are sent under review, their fate held by the receiver.
branches.cn: 文件与方案：纸张和计划被送到审阅之下，命运由接收者掌握。

branches.en: PROCEDURE: the self or a material is sent into a test or treatment rather than to a person.
branches.cn: 程序：自我或材料被送进检查、处理，而不是送给某个人。

branches.en: FORMAL RECORD: evidence and formal statements are handed to a court or assembly to be weighed.
branches.cn: 正式记录：证据与正式陈述被交给法庭或议会，供其权衡。

intro.en: Submit keeps its Latin prefix sub- and root mittere. English adds -sion, -ive, -al and -er; the double t in submitted is a spelling rule, not a new morpheme.
intro.cn: submit 保留拉丁前缀 sub- 与词根 mittere。英语加 -sion、-ive、-al、-er；submitted 的双写 t 是拼写规则，不是新语素。

latinIntro.en: Mittere 'to send, let go' is one of Latin's most productive verbs: admit, permit, commit, transmit, emit, mission and emissary all send something somewhere.
latinIntro.cn: mittere“送、放”是拉丁语最能产的动词之一：admit、permit、commit、transmit、emit、mission、emissary 都把某物送到某处。

items.structure: submit + -sion (noun of action, on the Latin stem submiss-)
items.meaning: the act of submitting; something submitted; the state of yielding
items.meaningCN: 提交；提交物；屈服（-sion 构成行为名词，基于拉丁词干 submiss-）
items.example: The deadline for submissions is 1 May.
items.exampleCN: 提交截止日期是 5 月 1 日。

items.meaningCN: 顺从的；过于听命的（-ive 表示倾向，源自拉丁 submissus）
items.example: The dog gave a submissive whimper.
items.exampleCN: 那只狗发出顺从的呜咽声。

items.meaning: the act of sending in documents, especially in business or construction
items.meaningCN: （文件等的）提交，多用于商务或工程语境（-al 构成行为名词）
items.example: The contractor sent the submittal to the architect.
items.exampleCN: 承包商把提交文件发给了建筑师。

items.meaningCN: 提交者（-er 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: Each submitter receives a confirmation email.
items.exampleCN: 每位提交者都会收到一封确认邮件。

items.example: The verb is the sending behind submit and permit.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 submit 与 permit 背后的“送出”。

items.example: The stem appears in mission and in the participle behind submission.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 mission、submission 与 permit。

items.example: The prefix lowers the self into submission.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把自身放到“服从”的位置。

items.example: It forms submission, the act of yielding or sending in.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 submission，即屈服或提交的行为。

items.example: It forms submissive, tending to yield.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 submissive，即倾向顺从的。

latinEntries.meaning: to send something across or pass it on
latinEntries.meaningCN: 传送；传播（送到另一边）

latinEntries.meaning: to let someone in or allow something to be true
latinEntries.meaningCN: 准许进入；承认（送到里面）

latinEntries.meaning: to allow something to pass or happen
latinEntries.meaningCN: 允许；许可（让之通过）

latinEntries.meaning: to carry out an act, or to entrust oneself fully
latinEntries.meaningCN: 犯（罪）；承诺；托付（完全送出）

definition_zh: 随后的；后来的；接着发生的；后文的；（法律）后续的
definition_en: coming after something else in time, order, or sequence
core_image: 队伍中紧跟在第一个身影之后的第二个身影——位置由前一个人定义
scene: 第一场暴雨冲毁了路基。More rain came in the subsequent weeks, and the repair crew had to fill the same trench again and again.
sceneCN: 这里 subsequent 是「随后的」（第 1 个义项：时间上跟着发生）；句意：随后的几周里又下了几场雨，抢修队只能一遍遍回填同一条沟。图中可辨识物件：被冲毁的路基、雨云、抢修队、填土铲。

pos.zh: 随后的；后来的；后文的

derivatives.zh: 子序列；后续（多用于数学、技术语境）

senses.title: Following in time
senses.definition: happening or existing after a particular event or time
senses.definitionCN: 在某一事件或时间之后发生或存在
senses.example: Subsequent repairs closed the bridge for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 随后的维修让这座桥封闭了数周。
senses.why: Subsequi is 'to follow'. The adjective is the present participle, so it names whatever is still walking behind an event.
senses.whyCN: subsequi 意为“跟随”。这个形容词是现在分词，因此它命名的是仍走在某个事件后面的东西。

senses.title: Following in order or sequence
senses.definition: coming next in a series, list, or process
senses.definitionCN: 在一系列、清单或流程中紧接着出现
senses.example: Each subsequent chapter assumes the one before.
senses.exampleCN: 后面每一章都以先前一章为前提。
senses.why: Following is spatial as well as temporal: items in a series stand in a line, and the later one is behind.
senses.whyCN: “跟随”既是时间性的，也是空间性的：系列中的项目排成一线，较后的那个就在后面。

senses.title: Later in a text or argument
senses.definition: appearing later in a book, argument, or discussion
senses.definitionCN: 出现在书、论证或讨论的较后部分
senses.example: Subsequent sections examine the evidence in detail.
senses.exampleCN: 后面几节将详细考察证据。
senses.why: A text unfolds in time for the reader; the later page is literally the page that follows.
senses.whyCN: 文本对读者而言是按时间展开的；后一页就是字面意义上“跟在后面”的那一页。

senses.title: In the phrase subsequent to
senses.definition: in the phrase subsequent to, meaning after a particular event
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 subsequent to，意为在某事件之后
senses.example: Subsequent to the hearing, new evidence emerged.
senses.exampleCN: 听证会之后，出现了新证据。
senses.why: The participle plus to turns 'following' into a preposition-like phrase. The formal register marks it as written, legal or official.
senses.whyCN: 分词加 to 把“跟随”变成一个类似介词的短语。正式语域使它带书面、法律或官方色彩。

senses.title: Later holder or purchaser in law
senses.definition: in law, a person who acquires a right or property after an earlier holder
senses.definitionCN: 法律上，在较早持有人之后取得权利或财产的人
senses.example: A subsequent purchaser takes the land subject to the existing lease.
senses.exampleCN: 后续购买人取得土地时须受既有租约约束。
senses.why: Property records form a sequence; the later buyer stands behind the earlier one in the chain of title.
senses.whyCN: 产权记录构成一个序列；较晚的买家在权利链上排在较早者之后。

senses.title: A later layer or period
senses.definition: in geology or history, belonging to a period that comes after an earlier one
senses.definitionCN: 在地质学或历史学中，属于较早期之后的阶段
senses.example: Subsequent erosion cut channels through the lava.
senses.exampleCN: 后期的侵蚀在熔岩中切出了沟道。
senses.why: Strata pile up in order, and what lies above was laid down later. The same 'behind in sequence' image is read as 'later in time'.
senses.whyCN: 地层按顺序堆叠，上面的地层是后来沉积的。同一个“在序列后面”的意象被读成“在时间上较晚”。

senses.title: Resulting or consequent
senses.definition: following as a result or consequence of something
senses.definitionCN: 作为某事的结果或后果而随之发生
senses.example: The subsequent decline in sales worried investors.
senses.exampleCN: 随之而来的销售下滑让投资者担忧。
senses.why: What follows an event is often caused by it. The temporal 'after' slides into the logical 'as a result'.
senses.whyCN: 跟着事件发生的东西往往由它造成。时间上的“之后”滑向了逻辑上的“因此”。

senses.title: Later generations or descendants
senses.definition: belonging to later generations, often in the phrase subsequent generations
senses.definitionCN: 属于后来的世代，常用于短语 subsequent generations
senses.example: Subsequent generations inherited both the house and its debts.
senses.exampleCN: 后代既继承了房子，也继承了债务。
senses.why: Generations form a line in time; each later one follows the one before, so the word can mark descent.
senses.whyCN: 世代在时间中排成一线；每个较晚的世代都跟在先前世代之后，因此这个词也能标记血脉传承。

intro.en: Subsequent is the Latin present participle of subsequi 'to follow after', borrowed through French. The PIE root *sekw- 'to follow' is generally accepted; the deeper layer is not reconstructed with certainty.
intro.cn: subsequent 是拉丁语 subsequi“跟随在后”的现在分词，经由法语借入。原始印欧语词根 *sekw-“跟随”属一般认为；更深层未能确定重构。

items.en: Subsequi 'to follow after' = sub- 'under, close behind' + sequi 'to follow'. Its present participle is subsequentem, 'following'.
items.cn: subsequi“跟随在后”＝sub-“在下、紧随”＋sequi“跟随”。其现在分词是 subsequentem，意为“跟随的”。

items.en: Middle French subséquent carried the Latin participle into French usage, from which English took it.
items.cn: 中古法语 subséquent 把这个拉丁分词带入法语，英语又从法语借入。

items.en: English records subsequent as an adjective meaning 'following in time, coming after'.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪早期记录 subsequent 作形容词，意为“时间上随后的、接着来的”。

items.en: Legal and chronological writing adopts the word widely. The compound preposition subsequent to develops in formal prose.
items.cn: 法律与编年写作广泛采用这个词。复合介词 subsequent to 在正式散文里发展起来。

items.en: Subsequent becomes standard in academic, legal and historical prose. The adverb subsequently becomes far more frequent than the adjective in speech.
items.cn: subsequent 成为学术、法律与历史散文的标准用词。副词 subsequently 在口语中的使用频率远高于形容词。

items.en: PIE *sekw- 'to follow' is the usual reconstruction behind Latin sequi, sequence, sequel and second. The reconstruction is standard but remains a reconstruction, not a recorded form.
items.cn: 原始印欧语 *sekw-“跟随”是拉丁 sequi、sequence、sequel、second 背后通行的重构。这是标准重构，但仍是重构，而非有记录的形式。

note.en: The groups below separate spelling neighbours from words with a close meaning. Form is checked first, then whether the word marks time, order, or consequence.
note.cn: 下面两组把“拼写相近”与“意思接近”分开。先看词形，再看这个词标记的是时间、次序还是结果。

entries.definition: following as a result. It shares sequi but builds a logical, not merely temporal, link.
entries.definitionCN: 作为结果而随后的。它与 sequi 同根，但建立的是逻辑联系，而不只是时间联系。

entries.definition: a sequence within a sequence, especially in mathematics. It is a technical noun, not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 序列中的子序列，尤用于数学。它是技术名词，不是这个形容词。

entries.definition: following in order; rare and technical. It is the bare Latin participle without sub-.
entries.definitionCN: 按次序跟随的；罕用且偏技术。它是去掉 sub- 的纯拉丁分词。

entries.definition: coming next. It is neutral about cause and usable in everyday speech, unlike the formal subsequent.
entries.definitionCN: 接着的、下一个的。它对原因保持中立，可用于日常口语，不像 subsequent 那样正式。

entries.definition: at a later time. It is purely temporal and often comparative.
entries.definitionCN: 在较晚的时间。它是纯时间性的，且常作比较级。

entries.definition: happening after and usually as a result. It is formal and common in news and legal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 随后发生且通常是作为结果发生。它偏正式，常见于新闻与法律写作。

entries.definition: following one after another in a series. It stresses repetition, not a single later item.
entries.definitionCN: 在一系列中一个接一个的。它强调重复，而不是单个较后的事项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实短语和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Sub- 'after, under' + sequi 'follow': subsequent is the thing that follows behind.
normal.cn: sub-“在后、在下”＋sequi“跟随”：subsequent 就是跟在后面的那个东西。

normal.en: Sequence, sequel, second and consecutive all come from sequi 'follow'.
normal.cn: sequence、sequel、second、consecutive 都来自 sequi“跟随”。

normal.en: Subsequent is usually attributive: subsequent events, the subsequent chapter, not usually 'the events are subsequent'.
normal.cn: subsequent 通常作定语：subsequent events、the subsequent chapter，一般不说 the events are subsequent。

normal.en: Subsequent to is the formal preposition: after. In everyday speech, 'after' is simpler.
normal.cn: subsequent to 是正式介词短语，意为“在……之后”。日常口语里，after 更简单。

normal.en: Subsequently is the everyday adverb; the adjective is mostly written.
normal.cn: subsequently 是日常副词；形容词形式主要用于书面语。

abstract.en: Picture two dots on a timeline: the second is not later by itself, it is later because the first exists.
abstract.cn: 想象时间线上的两个点：第二个点本身并不“较晚”，它较晚是因为第一个点存在。

abstract.en: Subsequent is a shadow cast by a previous event onto the next one.
abstract.cn: subsequent 是前一个事件投到下一个事件上的影子。

abstract.en: The word is a queue, not a clock: order matters more than minutes.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一支队列，而不是一座钟：次序比分钟更重要。

examples.en: The first storm damaged the roof; subsequent storms made the repairs impossible.
examples.cn: 第一场风暴损坏了屋顶；随后的风暴让维修无法进行。

examples.en: Subsequent to the interview, the company asked for two references.
examples.cn: 面试之后，公司要求提供两份推荐信。

examples.en: Later chapters return to this question; the subsequent discussion is technical.
examples.cn: 后面的章节会回到这个问题；随后的讨论偏技术性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“萨布西昆特”——检票员西昆特总是跟在队伍后面 → subsequent 随后的

root: 源自拉丁 subsequi“跟随在后”的现在分词 subsequentem＝sub-“在下、紧随”＋sequi“跟随”，核心是“跟在后面”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of subsequent, all one position: behind something that has already happened or been listed. Time, order, text, law, geology and result are different readings of that position.
sensesIntro.cn: subsequent 的八个义项共用一个位置：在已经发生或已被列出的事物后面。时间、次序、文本、法律、地质与结果，都是对这个位置的不同读法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second figure walking directly behind the first.
core.cn: 核心意象：第二个身影紧紧走在第一个身影后面。

branches.en: TIME AND CAUSE: later in time, and often later because of what came first.
branches.cn: 时间与原因：在时间上较晚，且常常因为先前之事而较晚。

branches.en: SEQUENCE AND LINEAGE: order in a series or in generations.
branches.cn: 序列与血脉：在系列中的次序，或在世代中的次序。

branches.en: TEXT: the later page follows the earlier one for the reader.
branches.cn: 文本：对读者而言，后一页跟在前面那一页之后。

branches.en: PREPOSITIONAL USE: subsequent to packages the following relation as a formal phrase.
branches.cn: 介词用法：subsequent to 把“跟随”关系包装成正式短语。

branches.en: PROFESSIONAL ORDER: title chains and geological layers are both sequences read as time.
branches.cn: 专业次序：产权链与地质层都是被读作时间的序列。

intro.en: Subsequent is a Latin present participle borrowed as an adjective. English adds -ly and -ness; sub- and sequi belong to the Latin verb, not to living English rules.
intro.cn: subsequent 是作为形容词借入的拉丁现在分词。英语加 -ly、-ness；sub- 与 sequi 属于拉丁动词，不是活的英语规则。

latinIntro.en: Sequi 'to follow' is the source of sequence, sequel, second, consecutive and obsequious, all images of one thing behind another.
latinIntro.cn: sequi“跟随”是 sequence、sequel、second、consecutive、obsequious 的来源，都是“一物在另一物后面”的意象。

items.meaning: afterwards; later in time or order
items.meaningCN: 随后；后来（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The building was subsequently sold to a trust.
items.exampleCN: 这座建筑随后被卖给了一家信托机构。

items.meaning: a sequence contained within another sequence, especially in mathematics
items.meaningCN: 子序列；序列中的序列，尤用于数学
items.example: Every infinite sequence has infinitely many subsequences.
items.exampleCN: 每个无限序列都有无限多个子序列。

items.meaning: following as a consequence; a rare adjective
items.meaningCN: 随之而来的；结果性的（较少用形容词）
items.example: The subsequential effects were hard to measure.
items.exampleCN: 随之而来的影响很难衡量。

items.meaning: the quality of being subsequent; a rare noun
items.meaningCN: 随后性；处于后续状态（罕用名词）
items.example: The subsequence of events, not their subsequentness, concerned the court.
items.exampleCN: 法庭关心的是事件的先后顺序，而不是它们的“随后性”。

items.example: The verb is the following behind subsequent.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 subsequent 背后的“跟随”。

items.example: The stem appears in consecutive and in the participle behind prosecution.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 consecutive 与 sequence。

items.example: The prefix places the following right behind.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把“跟随”放在紧后面。

items.example: It forms subsequent, being in the following position.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 subsequent，即处于随后位置的。

items.example: It forms subsequently, meaning afterward.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 subsequently，意为随后。

latinEntries.meaning: a set of things that follow one another in order
latinEntries.meaningCN: 序列；按顺序相接的一组事物

latinEntries.meaning: a work or event that follows an earlier one
latinEntries.meaningCN: 续集；后续事件（跟在原作之后的东西）

latinEntries.meaning: following continuously one after another
latinEntries.meaningCN: 连续的；一个接一个跟随的

latinEntries.meaning: too eager to follow or obey; servile
latinEntries.meaningCN: 谄媚的；过分顺从的（急于跟随）

definition_zh: 大量的；可观的；实质的；坚固的；重大的；财力雄厚的
definition_en: large in amount or degree, solid in build, or belonging to the real substance of something
core_image: 脚下实心的一整块地基：看不见，却撑住了上面的一切
scene: 审计报告指出，这家工厂每年消耗的水电都很惊人。The plant uses a substantial amount of water and power each year, and the bill is as thick as a book.
sceneCN: 这里 substantial 是「大量的」（第 3 个义项：数量或程度大）；句意：这家工厂每年消耗大量水和电，账单厚得像一本书。图中可辨识物件：审计报告、水电账单、工厂管道、计算器。

pos.zh: 大量的；可观的；实质的；坚固的；重大的

derivatives.zh: 在很大程度上；大体上；实质上

senses.title: Standing under: having real substance
senses.definition: existing as a real thing with substance, not merely as a name or an appearance
senses.definitionCN: 以有实体的真实事物存在，而不只是名称或表象
senses.example: The argument needs a substantial basis, not rhetoric.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证需要实质性的依据，而不是空话。
senses.why: Substantia is what stands under appearances. The first sense is the metaphysical one: real being rather than mere look.
senses.whyCN: substantia 是站在表象下面的东西。第一个义项是形而上的：真实存在，而非仅仅是外观。

senses.title: Essential rather than accidental
senses.definition: belonging to the essence of a thing rather than to its incidental features
senses.definitionCN: 属于事物的本质，而不是偶然、附带的特征
senses.example: The substantial issue is who owns the land.
senses.exampleCN: 实质问题是这块土地归谁所有。
senses.why: What stands under a thing is also what makes it what it is. 'Substantial' becomes 'essential'.
senses.whyCN: 站在一个东西下面的，也是使它成为它的东西。于是 substantial 变成“本质的”。

senses.title: Large in amount
senses.definition: large in size, amount, or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在规模、数量或程度上很大
senses.example: The project required a substantial investment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目需要大量投资。
senses.why: A large mass has more 'stuff' standing under it. Quantity grew out of the image of solid bulk in the 16th century.
senses.whyCN: 大的物体下面有更多“东西”撑着。数量义正是从 16 世纪“实心块体”的意象中生长出来的。

senses.title: Important or significant
senses.definition: important enough to matter or to change a situation
senses.definitionCN: 重要到足以产生影响或改变局势
senses.example: There was a substantial disagreement over the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 在预算问题上存在重大分歧。
senses.why: What has weight also has consequence. Importance is mass transferred to an argument.
senses.whyCN: 有重量的东西也有后果。重要性就是被转移到论证上的“质量”。

senses.title: Solidly built
senses.definition: strongly built, thick, and not easily damaged
senses.definitionCN: 建造得结实、厚实，不易损坏
senses.example: The house has substantial stone walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这座房子有坚固的石墙。
senses.why: The literal 'standing under' returns: a substantial wall is one that can bear weight.
senses.whyCN: 字面的“站在下面”回来了：substantial 的墙就是能承重的墙。

senses.title: Financially strong
senses.definition: having considerable wealth or resources
senses.definitionCN: 拥有相当多的财富或资源
senses.example: A substantial donor paid for the new wing.
senses.exampleCN: 一位财力雄厚的捐赠者出资建了新侧楼。
senses.why: Money is treated as mass. A person with much of it has substantial means, a 19th-century commercial extension.
senses.whyCN: 金钱被当作质量来对待。拥有很多钱的人就有 substantial means，这是 19 世纪商业语境的引申。

senses.title: Legal: real and not merely formal
senses.definition: in law, real, important, and not merely technical, as in substantial compliance or substantial evidence
senses.definitionCN: 法律上真实、重要，而不只是技术性的，如实质遵守或实质性证据
senses.example: The court found substantial evidence for the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定该主张有实质性证据支持。
senses.why: Law separates the substance of a matter from its form. Substantial marks what goes to the essence.
senses.whyCN: 法律把事情的实质与形式分开。substantial 标记的是触及本质的部分。

senses.title: Philosophical: pertaining to substance
senses.definition: in philosophy, relating to substance as the underlying reality of a thing
senses.definitionCN: 哲学上，指与作为事物底层实在的“实体”相关
senses.example: Aristotle's substantial form gives a thing its identity.
senses.exampleCN: 亚里士多德的实体形式赋予事物同一性。
senses.why: The Scholastic term substantialis kept the technical sense alive. It names what inheres in the substance itself.
senses.whyCN: 经院哲学的 substantialis 让技术义活了下来。它命名的是依附于实体本身的东西。

senses.title: Hearty or filling
senses.definition: of a meal, large enough to satisfy hunger; a usage boundary rather than a separate root sense
senses.definitionCN: 指一餐分量足够、能吃饱；这是用法边界，而非独立词源义
senses.example: We had a substantial breakfast before the climb.
senses.exampleCN: 爬山前我们吃了一顿丰盛的早餐。
senses.why: Food is measured by bulk and staying power. The 'large amount' sense narrows to a plate that visibly satisfies.
senses.whyCN: 食物按体积和耐饿程度衡量。“大量”义收窄到一盘看得见能吃饱的饭。

intro.en: Substantial comes from Latin substantia 'that which stands under; essence', built on substare 'to stand under'. It shares the stare family with substitute, but the branches differ. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: substantial 来自拉丁 substantia“站在下面的东西；本质”，由 substare“在下面站立”构成。它与 substitute 同出 stare 词族，但分支不同。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Substare 'to stand under, be present' = sub- 'under' + stare 'to stand'. The derived noun substantia names what underlies appearances.
items.cn: substare“站在下面、存在于下面”＝sub-“在下”＋stare“站立”。派生名词 substantia 命名的是表象之下的东西。

items.en: Philosophical Latin uses substantia for 'essence, substance', partly to render Greek ousia. The term is technical before it is everyday.
items.cn: 哲学拉丁语用 substantia 表示“本质、实体”，部分是为了对译希腊语 ousia。这个词先有技术义，后有日常义。

items.en: Substantialis 'of substance, essential' appears in late Latin Christian and philosophical writing, especially from the 4th century onward.
items.cn: substantialis“实体的、本质的”出现在晚期拉丁基督教与哲学写作中，尤其自 4 世纪起。

items.en: English borrows the adjective through Old French substantiel, first in the sense 'real, essential, having actual existence'.
items.cn: 英语经由古法语 substantiel 借入这个形容词，最初义为“真实的、本质的、实际存在的”。

items.en: The sense 'large, considerable, ample' develops. A substantial amount is literally a mass with substance under it.
items.cn: “大量的、可观的、充足的”义发展出来。a substantial amount 字面上就是下面有实体支撑的一大块。

items.en: The word branches into 'solidly built', 'financially strong', and legal phrases such as substantial evidence and substantial compliance. The 20th century adds the 'hearty meal' usage.
items.cn: 这个词分叉出“坚固建造”“财力雄厚”以及 substantial evidence、substantial compliance 等法律短语。20 世纪又添“丰盛一餐”的用法。

note.en: The groups below separate spelling neighbours from words with a close meaning. Form is checked first, then whether the word means essence, bulk, or importance.
note.cn: 下面两组把“拼写相近”与“意思接近”分开。先看词形，再看这个词指的是本质、体积还是重要性。

entries.definition: having a firm basis, or dealing with substance. In grammar it means a noun. It is closer to 'essential' than to 'large'.
entries.definitionCN: 有坚实依据的，或涉及实质的。在语法中指名词。它更接近“本质的”，而不是“大量的”。

entries.definition: to prove or give substance to a claim. It is the verb built on the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 证实或为某一主张提供实质依据。它是同一词干构成的动词。

entries.definition: the material or essential nature of something. It is the noun underlying the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的材料或本质。它是这个形容词底下的名词。

entries.definition: large in amount or extent. It often modifies abstract nouns and carries no image of solidity.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或范围很大。它常修饰抽象名词，不带“坚固”的意象。

entries.definition: large or important enough to matter. It stresses consequence rather than bulk.
entries.definitionCN: 大到或重要到足以产生影响。它强调后果，而不是体积。

entries.definition: firm and reliable in quality or build. It is physical or figurative, but not a quantity word.
entries.definitionCN: 质量或结构上坚固可靠。它可实可虚，但不是数量词。

entries.definition: fairly large in size or number. It is more informal and less evaluative than substantial.
entries.definitionCN: 尺寸或数量相当大。它比 substantial 更口语化，评价色彩更少。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实短语和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Sub- 'under' + stare 'stand': substance is what stands under a thing.
normal.cn: sub-“在下”＋stare“站立”：substance 就是站在一个东西下面的东西。

normal.en: Substantial and substitute share stare, but one branch stands under (substance) and the other sets something in place (statuere).
normal.cn: substantial 与 substitute 同出 stare，但一支是“站在下面”（substance），另一支是“把某物安置到位”（statuere）。

normal.en: The 16th-century jump from 'essential' to 'large' is the key: a substantial amount is a mass with weight.
normal.cn: 16 世纪从“本质的”跳到“大量的”是关键：a substantial amount 就是有重量的一大块。

normal.en: Substantial evidence and substantial compliance are legal phrases where substantial means 'going to the essence', not 'huge'.
normal.cn: substantial evidence 与 substantial compliance 是法律短语，这里的 substantial 意为“触及本质”，不是“巨大”。

normal.en: Stable, statue, constant and institute all stand in the same Latin family.
normal.cn: stable、statue、constant、institute 都站在同一个拉丁词族里。

abstract.en: Picture a foundation stone under a building: you see the building, not the stone, but the stone is what holds it.
abstract.cn: 想象建筑下面的一块基石：你看见的是建筑，不是石头，但石头才是撑住它的东西。

abstract.en: Substantial is weight made visible: a claim, a meal and a wall all have 'how much is under them'.
abstract.cn: substantial 是变得可见的重量：主张、饭菜、墙壁都有“下面垫了多少”的问题。

abstract.en: Move the foundation upward and it becomes a statue (statuere); leave it under and it is substance.
abstract.cn: 把地基往上移，它就变成雕像（statuere）；留在下面，它就是实体（substance）。

examples.en: The company made a substantial contribution to the research fund.
examples.cn: 这家公司向研究基金捐了一大笔钱。

examples.en: There is substantial evidence that the climate is changing.
examples.cn: 有大量证据表明气候正在变化。

examples.en: The old bridge is substantial enough to carry heavy trucks.
examples.cn: 这座老桥足够坚固，能承载重型卡车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“萨布斯坦肖”——萨布能一手拎起一大块实心石头 → substantial 大量的、实质的

root: 源自拉丁 substantia“实体、本质”，由 substare“在下面站立”构成（sub-＋stare）；16 世纪由“本质的”发展出“大量、可观”义。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of substantial, all one image: something massive stands under a visible surface. From that image come real being, essence, bulk, importance, solid build and the legal 'goes to the essence'.
sensesIntro.cn: substantial 的九个义项共用一个意象：某个厚实的东西站在可见表面的下面。真实存在、本质、体积、重要性、坚固建造，以及法律上的“触及本质”，都从这个意象而来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a massive foundation standing under a visible surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整块厚实的地基站在可见表面的下方。

branches.en: METAPHYSICS: what stands under appearances is real being and substance.
branches.cn: 形而上学：站在表象下面的，是真实存在与实体。

branches.en: ESSENCE VS FORM: law and philosophy separate substance from accident or mere form.
branches.cn: 本质与形式：法律和哲学把实体与偶然属性或纯形式分开。

branches.en: MASS: solid bulk becomes large amount, down to a filling meal.
branches.cn: 质量：实心体积变成大量，一直落到能吃饱的一餐。

branches.en: BEARING WEIGHT: walls and fortunes are judged by what they can support.
branches.cn: 承重：墙壁与家产都按“能撑住多少”来评判。

branches.en: CONSEQUENCE: importance is weight transferred to an argument.
branches.cn: 后果：重要性就是转移到论证上的重量。

intro.en: Substantial is Latin substantia + -alis, borrowed through French. English adds -ly, -ity and -ness; sub- and stare are frozen inside the Latin noun.
intro.cn: substantial 是拉丁 substantia＋-alis，经法语借入。英语加 -ly、-ity、-ness；sub- 与 stare 凝固在拉丁名词里。

latinIntro.en: Stare 'to stand' gives stable, statue, constant and rest. Statuere 'set up' is its causative branch, which also produced substitute. Substantial belongs to the 'stand under' side.
latinIntro.cn: stare“站立”给出 stable、statue、constant、rest。statuere“安置”是它的使役分支，也产生了 substitute。substantial 属于“站在下面”这一支。

items.meaning: to a great extent; also in essence
items.meaningCN: 在很大程度上；实质上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Costs have risen substantially since last year.
items.exampleCN: 自去年以来成本大幅上升。

items.meaning: the quality of being substantial or real
items.meaningCN: 实质性；实体性（-ity 表示性质或状态）
items.example: The court questioned the substantiality of the claim.
items.exampleCN: 法院质疑该主张的实质性。

items.meaning: the state of being substantial; a rare synonym of substantiality
items.meaningCN: 实质性；坚固性（罕用，与 substantiality 近义）
items.example: The substantialness of the walls impressed the inspector.
items.exampleCN: 墙壁的坚固程度给检查员留下了深刻印象。

items.meaning: real and important; in grammar, a noun
items.meaningCN: 实质性的、重要的；语法中作名词（-ive 源自拉丁 substantivus）
items.example: The report makes several substantive recommendations.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告提出了几项实质性建议。

items.example: The verb is the standing-under behind substance.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 substance 背后“站在下面”。

items.example: The prefix puts the standing under the surface.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把“站立”放到表面之下。

items.example: The stem appears in substance and constant.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 substance 与 constant。

items.example: It forms substantial, having substance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 substantial，即有实体的。

items.meaning: the material or essential nature of something
items.example: The substance of the argument is sound.
items.exampleCN: 论证的实质是站得住的。

latinEntries.meaning: steady and not likely to move or change
latinEntries.meaningCN: 稳定的；不易移动或改变的

latinEntries.meaning: a carved or cast figure set up in a place
latinEntries.meaningCN: 雕像（被立起来的形象）

latinEntries.meaning: to establish an organization or system
latinEntries.meaningCN: 设立；建立（在原地立起来）

latinEntries.meaning: remaining the same; standing firm
latinEntries.meaningCN: 恒定的；坚定不移的（一起站住）

definition_zh: 代替品；替代者；替补队员；代课教师；用……代替；取代（化学）；代入（数学）
definition_en: a person or thing that takes the place of another, or to put a person or thing in another's place
core_image: 空出的位置马上被另一个身影占住——位置不变，人换了
scene: 中场受伤的前锋被换下。The substitute ran onto the same grass and stood in the same position, and the game went on without a pause.
sceneCN: 这里 substitute 是「替补队员」（第 3 个义项：运动中替换上场的球员）；句意：替补球员跑进同一块草皮、站进同一个位置，比赛没有停。图中可辨识物件：球场、受伤前锋、替补背心、换人牌。

senses.title: A person who acts for another
senses.titleCN: 替代者：替别人站进位置
senses.definition: a person who takes another person's place or performs their duties
senses.definitionCN: 占据他人位置或履行其职责的人
senses.example: The manager sent a substitute to represent him at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 经理派了一名代表替他出席会议。
senses.why: Substituere is 'to place in turn, put in place of'. A person is placed where another stood, so the role passes to the stand-in.
senses.whyCN: substituere 意为“依次放置、放到原位”。一个人被放到另一个人站过的地方，于是角色转到替身身上。

senses.title: A thing used instead of another
senses.definition: a thing used in place of another, often because the first is unavailable
senses.definitionCN: 用来代替另一物的东西，常因原物不可得
senses.example: There is no substitute for clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 干净的水无可替代。
senses.why: The same slot can be filled by an object. The word does not require a person, only a position left open.
senses.whyCN: 同一个位置也可以由物件填上。这个词并不要求是人，只需要一个空出来的位置。

senses.title: Sports: a player who comes on
senses.definition: a player who replaces another during a game
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中替换另一名球员上场的队员
senses.example: The coach brought on a substitute after the break.
senses.exampleCN: 中场休息后教练换上了一名替补。
senses.why: Sport formalises the slot: a fixed bench, a fixed position, and a visible swap.
senses.whyCN: 体育运动把这个位置制度化了：固定的替补席、固定的位置，以及一次看得见的交换。

senses.title: A substitute teacher
senses.definition: a teacher who fills in for another, often for a short period
senses.definitionCN: 临时替另一位教师上课的人，常为短期
senses.example: A substitute covered the class for two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 一位代课教师给这个班上了两周课。
senses.why: Institutions create temporary slots. The substitute occupies the same room and role without owning the post.
senses.whyCN: 机构会制造临时位置。代课者占据同一间教室和同一个角色，却不拥有这个职位。

senses.title: Verb: to use in place of
senses.definition: to use one thing or person instead of another
senses.definitionCN: 用一物或一人来代替另一物或另一人
senses.example: You can substitute honey for sugar in this recipe.
senses.exampleCN: 这道菜谱里你可以用蜂蜜代替糖。
senses.why: The verb turns the placement into an action: put this in that position. Note the pattern substitute A for B.
senses.whyCN: 动词把“放置”变成动作：把这个放到那个位置。注意搭配是 substitute A for B。

senses.title: Chemistry: replace an atom or group
senses.definition: to replace one atom or group in a molecule with another
senses.definitionCN: 用另一种原子或基团替换分子中的某一原子或基团
senses.example: A chlorine atom can substitute for hydrogen in the ring.
senses.exampleCN: 氯原子可以取代环上的氢原子。
senses.why: Chemistry gives the 'slot' a precise address: a bonded site. Substitution becomes a structural operation.
senses.whyCN: 化学给了这个“位置”一个精确地址：成键位点。取代于是成为一种结构操作。

senses.title: Mathematics: put a value in place
senses.definition: to replace a symbol or expression with a value or another expression
senses.definitionCN: 用数值或另一表达式替换符号或表达式
senses.example: Substitute x = 3 into the equation.
senses.exampleCN: 把 x＝3 代入方程。
senses.why: A variable is an empty slot. Substitution fills it while keeping the form of the expression.
senses.whyCN: 变量就是一个空位。代入把它填上，同时保持表达式的形式。

senses.title: Food: an alternative ingredient
senses.definition: an ingredient used in place of one that is unavailable or unsuitable
senses.definitionCN: 因原料不可得或不适宜而用来替代的食材
senses.example: This recipe lists substitutes for butter and eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 这份食谱列出了黄油和鸡蛋的代用品。
senses.why: The kitchen is a small system of slots. When one ingredient is missing, another must occupy its function.
senses.whyCN: 厨房是一个小小的位置系统。某种食材缺席时，另一种必须占住它的功能。

senses.title: Fixed phrase: no substitute for
senses.definition: in the phrase no substitute for, meaning nothing can perform the same function as well
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 no substitute for，意为没有什么能同样好地发挥该功能
senses.example: Nothing is a substitute for experience.
senses.exampleCN: 没有什么能替代经验。
senses.why: The negative phrase marks a slot that cannot be filled. The word's logic is clearest when no stand-in qualifies.
senses.whyCN: 否定短语标记的是一个填不上的位置。当没有任何替身合格时，这个词的逻辑最清楚。

intro.en: Substitute comes from Latin substitutus, the past participle of substituere 'put in place of'. It is built on statuere, the causative of stare 'stand'. This is the same stare family as substantial, but a different branch: substantial is what stands under, substitute is what is set in place.
intro.cn: substitute 来自拉丁 substitutus，是 substituere“把……放到原位”的过去分词。它建立在 statuere 上，而 statuere 是 stare“站立”的使役形式。这与 substantial 同出 stare 词族，但分支不同：substantial 是站在下面的东西，substitute 是被安置到位的替身。

items.en: Substituere 'to put in place of another, set in turn' = sub- 'in place of, under' + statuere 'set up, place'. Its past participle substitutus supplies the English word.
items.cn: substituere“把……放到另一物之位、依次安置”＝sub-“代替、在下”＋statuere“安置、使站立”。其过去分词 substitutus 提供了英语这个词。

items.en: In legal Latin a substitutus is a person appointed to act in another's place, especially an heir or a delegate.
items.cn: 在法律拉丁语中，substitutus 指被指定代他人行事的人，尤指继承人或代表。

items.en: English takes the noun first, meaning 'a person deputed to act for another'.
items.cn: 英语先借入名词，意为“受指派代他人行事的人”。

items.en: The verb 'to put one person or thing in another's place' becomes current, in legal, military and everyday contexts.
items.cn: 动词义“把一人或一物放到另一者的位置上”流行起来，见于法律、军事与日常语境。

items.en: Chemistry and mathematics adopt substitution as technical terms. Sport develops the fixed 'substitute player'.
items.cn: 化学与数学把 substitution 采纳为技术术语。体育发展出固定的“替补球员”义。

items.en: Substitute teacher, food substitutes and 'no substitute for' spread the word to any functional slot. The PIE root *stā- 'stand' behind stare is generally accepted.
items.cn: substitute teacher、food substitutes 与 no substitute for 把这个词扩散到任何功能性的位置。stare 背后的原始印欧语词根 *stā-“站立”属一般认为。

note.en: The groups below separate spelling neighbours from words with a close meaning. Form is checked first, then whether the word is a person, an option, or a formal replacement.
note.cn: 下面两组把“拼写相近”与“意思接近”分开。先看词形，再看这个词指人、指选项，还是指正式替换。

entries.definition: the act or result of replacing. It is the noun derived from substitute, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 替换的行为或结果。它是 substitute 派生的名词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: acting as a replacement. It is the adjective derived from the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 起替代作用的。它是同一动词派生的形容词。

entries.definition: the material or surface beneath something. It is sub- + stratum 'layer', a common false friend of substitute.
entries.definitionCN: 某物下面的材料或表面。它是 sub-＋stratum“层”，常被误认为与 substitute 同源。

entries.definition: to put something new in a position. It often implies the old one is gone for good.
entries.definitionCN: 把新东西放进某个位置。它常暗示旧的已经永久不在。

entries.definition: a person or thing acting in another's role, often with emotional or medical weight, as in surrogate mother.
entries.definitionCN: 代他人承担角色的人或物，常带情感或医学分量，如代孕母亲。

entries.definition: another option available alongside the first. It need not occupy the same slot.
entries.definitionCN: 与第一个选项并存的另一个选择。它不必占据同一个位置。

entries.definition: a person officially authorized to act for another. It is administrative and hierarchical.
entries.definitionCN: 获正式授权代他人行事的人。它带有行政与层级色彩。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实短语和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Sub- 'in place of' + statuere 'set up': a substitute is what is set up in another's place.
normal.cn: sub-“代替”＋statuere“安置”：substitute 就是被安置到他人位置上的东西。

normal.en: The pattern is substitute A for B: the new item goes into B's position, not the other way round.
normal.cn: 搭配是 substitute A for B：新东西进入 B 的位置，而不是反过来。

normal.en: Sports, schools and kitchens all have visible slots. Substitute fills a slot rather than replacing a substance.
normal.cn: 球场、学校、厨房都有看得见的位置。substitute 填的是位置，而不是替换某种实体。

normal.en: Statue, statute, institute and constitute are all 'set up' words from statuere. Substitute is the 'set up in place of' one.
normal.cn: statue、statute、institute、constitute 都来自 statuere“安置”。substitute 是其中“安置到替代位置”的那一个。

normal.en: Substantial and substitute share stare, but substantial stands under, while substitute stands in place.
normal.cn: substantial 与 substitute 同出 stare，但 substantial 站在下面，substitute 站在替代的位置上。

abstract.en: Picture a chessboard: remove one piece and put another on the same square. The square, not the piece, defines substitute.
abstract.cn: 想象一张棋盘：拿走一个棋子，把另一个放到同一个格子上。定义 substitute 的是格子，不是棋子。

abstract.en: A substitute is a function without an identity: the role travels, the person or thing does not.
abstract.cn: substitute 是没有身份的功能：角色在移动，而人或物本身没有移动。

abstract.en: The word is a slot-filler: player, teacher, atom, value and ingredient are all empty positions waiting to be filled.
abstract.cn: 这个词是“填空者”：球员、教师、原子、数值、食材，都是等待被填上的空位。

examples.en: Margarine was used as a substitute for butter during the war.
examples.cn: 战争期间人造黄油被用作黄油的替代品。

examples.en: No amount of theory is a substitute for hands-on practice.
examples.cn: 再多的理论也替代不了实际动手练习。

examples.en: The injured striker was substituted in the second half.
examples.cn: 受伤的前锋在下半场被换下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“萨布斯特丢特”——球员被换下，替补丢特跑上场 → substitute 替补、代替

root: 源自拉丁 substituere“把……放到原位”，过去分词 substitutus＝sub-“代替、在下”＋statuere“安置、使站立”（stare 的使役支），核心是“在空位上放一个替身”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of substitute, all one image: an empty slot is filled by a stand-in. The slot can be a role, a bench, a classroom, a bond site, a variable, or a kitchen function.
sensesIntro.cn: substitute 的九个义项共用一个意象：空位被替身填上。这个位置可以是角色、替补席、教室、成键位点、变量或厨房里的功能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty square is filled by a stand-in while the original is away.
core.cn: 核心意象：原主缺席时，一个空格被替身填上。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND PLAYERS: a person occupies another's role, permanently or for a match.
branches.cn: 人与球员：一个人占据另一个人的角色，长期或只限一场比赛。

branches.en: OBJECTS AND INGREDIENTS: a thing performs another thing's function.
branches.cn: 物件与食材：一个东西履行另一个东西的功能。

branches.en: ACTION: the verb puts the stand-in into the slot.
branches.cn: 动作：动词把替身放进那个位置。

branches.en: TECHNICAL SLOTS: atoms and variables are positions that can be filled.
branches.cn: 技术位置：原子与变量都是可以被填上的位置。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS AND LIMITS: temporary posts can be filled; some slots admit no substitute.
branches.cn: 制度与边界：临时职位可以填上；有些位置则不容任何替身。

intro.en: Substitute is a Latin participle used as noun and verb. English adds -ion, -able, -ive and -al; sub- and statuere are frozen inside the Latin verb.
intro.cn: substitute 是兼作名词与动词的拉丁分词。英语加 -ion、-able、-ive、-al；sub- 与 statuere 凝固在拉丁动词里。

latinIntro.en: Statuere 'set up' is the causative of stare 'stand'. Its family includes statute, constitute, institute and restitution. Substantial belongs to stare itself; substitute belongs to the causative branch.
latinIntro.cn: statuere“安置”是 stare“站立”的使役形式。它的词族包括 statute、constitute、institute、restitution。substantial 属于 stare 本身；substitute 属于使役分支。

items.meaning: the act or result of replacing one thing with another
items.meaningCN: 替换；代替；代入（-ion 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The substitution of steel for wood made the bridge stronger.
items.exampleCN: 用钢替代木材让这座桥更坚固。

items.meaning: able to be replaced by something else
items.meaningCN: 可代替的；可替换的（-able 表示“能够被……”）
items.example: The two parts are functionally substitutable.
items.exampleCN: 这两个部件在功能上可以互换。

items.meaningCN: 替代的；起代替作用的（-ive 表示倾向或功能）
items.example: The drug has a substitutive role in therapy.
items.exampleCN: 这种药在治疗中起替代作用。

items.meaning: relating to substitution, especially in grammar or chemistry
items.meaningCN: 替代的；替换性质的（-al 表示“与……有关的”）
items.example: The substitutional relation links the two symbols.
items.exampleCN: 这种替换关系把两个符号联系起来。

items.meaning: to cause to stand, to set up
items.example: The verb is the placing behind substitute and statute.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 substitute 与 statute 背后的“安置”。

items.example: The prefix puts one thing in another's place.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把一物放到另一物的位置。

items.example: English took this participle as the base of the word.
items.exampleCN: 英语以这个分词为这个词的词基。

items.example: It forms substitution, the act of putting one in another's place.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 substitution，即替换行为。

items.example: It forms substitutable, able to be replaced.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 substitutable，即可被替代的。

latinEntries.structure: statuere 'set up' → statutum 'a thing set up, a decree'
latinEntries.meaning: a written law formally set up by a legislature
latinEntries.meaningCN: 由立法机构正式设立成文的法令

latinEntries.meaning: to form or establish something
latinEntries.meaningCN: 构成；设立（一起立起来）

latinEntries.meaning: to establish an organization, rule, or practice
latinEntries.meaningCN: 设立；建立（在原地立起来）

latinEntries.meaning: the act of restoring something to its owner or former place
latinEntries.meaningCN: 归还；恢复原状（重新放回原位）
